vec2 g=sobel(uv);float m=length(g)/4.;float a=atan(g.y,g.x);float q=mod(floor((a+PI/8.)/(PI/4.)),4.);vec2 d=q<.5?vec2(1.,0.):q<1.5?vec2(1.,1.):q<2.5?vec2(0.,1.):vec2(-1.,1.);d*=u_px;float m1=length(sobel(uv+d))/4.,m2=length(sobel(uv-d))/4.;float e=(m>=m1&&m>=m2)?(m>u_p2?1.:(m>u_p1?.5:0.)):0.;return vec4(vec3(e),1.);
float e=T(uv).r;if(e<.25||e>.75)return vec4(vec3(e),1.);for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){if(T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_px).r>.75)return vec4(vec3(1.),1.);}return vec4(vec3(.5),1.);
float e=T(uv).r;if(e<.25||e>.75)return vec4(vec3(e),1.);for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){if(T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_px).r>.75)return vec4(vec3(1.),1.);}return vec4(vec3(.5),1.);
float e=T(uv).r;if(e<.25||e>.75)return vec4(vec3(e),1.);for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){if(T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_px).r>.75)return vec4(vec3(1.),1.);}return vec4(vec3(.5),1.);
float e=T(uv).r;if(e<.25||e>.75)return vec4(vec3(e),1.);for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){if(T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_px).r>.75)return vec4(vec3(1.),1.);}return vec4(vec3(.5),1.);
float e=T(uv).r;if(e<.25||e>.75)return vec4(vec3(e),1.);for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){if(T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_px).r>.75)return vec4(vec3(1.),1.);}return vec4(vec3(.5),1.);
float e=T(uv).r;if(e<.25||e>.75)return vec4(vec3(e),1.);for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){if(T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_px).r>.75)return vec4(vec3(1.),1.);}return vec4(vec3(.5),1.);
float e=T(uv).r;if(e<.25||e>.75)return vec4(vec3(e),1.);for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){if(T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_px).r>.75)return vec4(vec3(1.),1.);}return vec4(vec3(.5),1.);
float e=T(uv).r;if(e<.25||e>.75)return vec4(vec3(e),1.);for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){if(T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_px).r>.75)return vec4(vec3(1.),1.);}return vec4(vec3(.5),1.);
float e=step(.75,T(uv).r);return vec4(vec3(u_p3>.5?1.-e:e),1.);

filters.name: Skeletonize (Zhang-Suen)
filters.note: 12 thinning iterations
passes: float l=luma(c.rgb);return vec4(vec3((l<u_p0)!=(u_p1>.5)?1.:0.),1.);

float s=T(uv).r;if(u_p3>.5){for(int j=-8;j<=8;j++)for(int i=-8;i<=8;i++){vec2 o=vec2(float(i),float(j));if(length(o)>u_p3*.5+.3)continue;s=max(s,T(uv+o*u_px).r);}}int m=int(u_p2+.5);if(m==2)return vec4(mix(O(uv).rgb*.5,vec3(1.,.2,.1),s),1.);return vec4(vec3(m==0?1.-s:s),1.);

filters.name: Line Endpoints & Junctions
filters.note: run after Skeletonize; red = ends, cyan = junctions
passes:
float th=u_p0;bool inv=u_p1>.5;float on=float((L(uv)<th)!=inv);float best=0.;vec3 col=vec3(0.);for(int j=-6;j<=6;j++)for(int i=-6;i<=6;i++){vec2 o=vec2(float(i),float(j));if(length(o)>u_p2)continue;vec2 q=uv+o*u_px;if((L(q)<th)==inv)continue;float n[8];vec2 e=u_px;n[0]=L(q+vec2(0.,e.y));n[1]=L(q+e);n[2]=L(q+vec2(e.x,0.));n[3]=L(q+vec2(e.x,-e.y));n[4]=L(q-vec2(0.,e.y));n[5]=L(q-e);n[6]=L(q-vec2(e.x,0.));n[7]=L(q+vec2(-e.x,e.y));float B=0.,A=0.;for(int k=0;k<8;k++){float a=float((n[k]<th)!=inv),b=float((n[(k+1)%8]<th)!=inv);B+=a;A+=(a<.5&&b>.5)?1.:0.;}if(B==1.||A==1.&&B<=1.){best=1.;col=vec3(1.,.15,.1);}if(A>=3.){best=1.;col=vec3(0.,.85,1.);}}
  return vec4(best>0.?col:mix(vec3(1.),vec3(.15),on),1.);

filters.name: Local Binarization
filters.note: document / line-art binarization

filters.name: Screentone Removal
filters.note: manga / print descreen
passes: vec3 m=med9(uv,max(u_k,1.));return vec4(m,1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p0)*.6);
vec3 b=blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p0)*.6).rgb;vec3 o=O(uv).rgb;float e=smoothstep(.15,.5,length(sobelD(uv,R(u_p0))));return vec4(mix(b,b+(o-b)*.5,e*u_p1*.5),1.);

filters.name: Ink Extraction
filters.note: dark, unsaturated strokes
passes: vec3 h=rgb2hsv(c.rgb);float ink=(1.-smoothstep(u_p0-.08,u_p0+.08,luma(c.rgb)))*(1.-smoothstep(u_p1,u_p1+.15,h.y*h.z));int m=int(u_p2+.5);if(m==2)return vec4(vec3(ink),1.);vec3 bg=m==0?vec3(1.):mix(vec3(.75),vec3(.95),mod(floor(PX(uv).x/16.)+floor(PX(uv).y/16.),2.));return vec4(mix(bg,c.rgb*.6,ink),1.);

filters.name: Stroke Width Map
filters.note: thin = dark, thick = bright
passes: bool inv=u_p2>.5;if((L(uv)<u_p0)==inv)return vec4(vec3(0.),1.);float d=u_p1;for(int i=0;i<64;i++){float fi=float(i);float rr=sqrt((fi+.5)/64.)*R(u_p1)*.5;float a=fi*2.39996;if((L(uv+vec2(cos(a),sin(a))*rr*u_px)<u_p0)==inv)d=min(d,rr/u_k*2.);}return vec4(ramp(1,d/u_p1),1.);

filters.name: Gabor Filter Bank
filters.note: 8 orientations
passes: float best=0.,ba=0.;for(int k=0;k<8;k++){float th=float(k)*.3927;float acc=0.;for(int j=-6;j<=6;j++)for(int i=-6;i<=6;i++){vec2 o=vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_p0/6.;vec2 q=rot(o,-th);float w=exp(-dot(o,o)/(2.*u_p0*u_p0*.4))*cos(6.2832*q.x/u_p0);acc+=w*L(uv+o*u_k*u_px);}if(abs(acc)>best){best=abs(acc);ba=th;}}float v=clamp(best*u_p1*.02,0.,1.);return vec4(u_p2<.5?vec3(v):hsv2rgb(vec3(ba/PI,1.,v)),1.);

filters.name: Multi-scale Edges
filters.note: 1, 2 and 4 px scales
passes: float a=length(sobelD(uv,1.)),b=length(sobelD(uv,2.)),cc=length(sobelD(uv,4.))*.8;float v=u_p1<.5?max(a,max(b,cc)):(a+b+cc)/2.;return vec4(vec3(clamp(v*u_p0*.5,0.,1.)),1.);

filters.name: Zero-Crossings (Marr-Hildreth)
filters.note: LoG sign changes
passes: return vec4(vec3(luma(blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p0)*2.).rgb)),1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p0)*2.);
vec2 e=u_px*max(u_k,1.);float lap=T(uv+vec2(e.x,0.)).r+T(uv-vec2(e.x,0.)).r+T(uv+vec2(0.,e.y)).r+T(uv-vec2(0.,e.y)).r-4.*T(uv).r;return vec4(lap*20.+.5,0.,0.,1.);

vec2 e=u_px;float c0=T(uv).r-.5;float z=0.;for(int k=0;k<4;k++){vec2 d=k==0?vec2(e.x,0.):k==1?vec2(0.,e.y):k==2?e:vec2(e.x,-e.y);float a=T(uv+d).r-.5,b=T(uv-d).r-.5;if(a*b<0.&&abs(a-b)>u_p1)z=1.;if(c0*a<0.&&abs(c0-a)>u_p1)z=1.;}return vec4(vec3(z),1.);

filters.name: Edge Tangent Flow
filters.note: flow field as streaks
passes: vec2 p=uv;float acc=0.,w=0.;for(int dir=0;dir<2;dir++){p=uv;float sg=dir==0?1.:-1.;for(int i=0;i<16;i++){float a=0.,b=0.,cc=0.;for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int k=-1;k<=1;k++){vec2 g=sobel(p+vec2(float(k),float(j))*R(u_p0)*.5*u_px);a+=g.x*g.x;b+=g.x*g.y;cc+=g.y*g.y;}float l2=.5*(a+cc+sqrt(max((a-cc)*(a-cc)+4.*b*b,0.)));vec2 t=vec2(b,l2-a);t=length(t)>1e-6?normalize(vec2(-t.y,t.x)):vec2(1.,0.);acc+=hash(floor(PX(p)));w+=1.;p+=sg*t*R(u_p1)/16.*u_px;}}return vec4(vec3(acc/w),1.);

filters.name: Line Detector (oriented averages)
filters.note: Ricci & Perfetti 2007
passes: float sq=blurL(uv,R(u_p0)/4.);float best=-1.;for(int k=0;k<12;k++){float a=float(k)*.2618;vec2 d=vec2(cos(a),sin(a))*R(u_p0)*.5*u_px;float s=0.;for(int i=0;i<9;i++)s+=L(uv+d*(float(i)/4.-1.));s/=9.;best=max(best,u_p2<.5?sq-s:s-sq);}return vec4(vec3(clamp(best*u_p1,0.,1.)),1.);

filters.name: Rolling Guidance (structure only)
filters.note: Zhang 2014: texture removed, edges kept
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p0));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p0));

vec3 g=T(uv).rgb;vec3 acc=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;for(int j=-3;j<=3;j++)for(int i=-3;i<=3;i++){vec2 o=vec2(float(i),float(j))*R(u_p0)/3.;vec3 gs=T(uv+o*u_px).rgb;vec3 dd=gs-g;float w=exp(-dot(o,o)/(2.*R(u_p0)*R(u_p0)*.5+.01))*exp(-dot(dd,dd)/(2.*u_p1*u_p1));acc+=O(uv+o*u_px).rgb*w;ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,1.);

vec3 g=T(uv).rgb;vec3 acc=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;for(int j=-3;j<=3;j++)for(int i=-3;i<=3;i++){vec2 o=vec2(float(i),float(j))*R(u_p0)/3.;vec3 gs=T(uv+o*u_px).rgb;vec3 dd=gs-g;float w=exp(-dot(o,o)/(2.*R(u_p0)*R(u_p0)*.5+.01))*exp(-dot(dd,dd)/(2.*u_p1*u_p1));acc+=O(uv+o*u_px).rgb*w;ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,1.);

vec3 g=T(uv).rgb;vec3 acc=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;for(int j=-3;j<=3;j++)for(int i=-3;i<=3;i++){vec2 o=vec2(float(i),float(j))*R(u_p0)/3.;vec3 gs=T(uv+o*u_px).rgb;vec3 dd=gs-g;float w=exp(-dot(o,o)/(2.*R(u_p0)*R(u_p0)*.5+.01))*exp(-dot(dd,dd)/(2.*u_p1*u_p1));acc+=O(uv+o*u_px).rgb*w;ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,1.);

filters.name: Local Binary Patterns
filters.note: texture descriptor
passes: float c0=L(uv);float code=0.,tr=0.;float prev=step(c0,L(uv+vec2(R(u_p0),0.)*u_px));for(int k=0;k<8;k++){float a=float(k)*.7854;float b=step(c0,L(uv+vec2(cos(a),sin(a))*R(u_p0)*u_px));code+=b*exp2(float(k));if(k>0)tr+=abs(b-prev);prev=b;}int m=int(u_p1+.5);if(m==0)return vec4(vec3(code/255.),1.);if(m==1)return vec4(tr<=2.&&code>0.&&code<255.?hsv2rgb(vec3(code/255.,.7,1.)):vec3(.1),1.);return vec4(vec3(tr/8.),1.);

filters.name: HOG Glyphs
filters.note: histogram of oriented gradients
passes:
vec2 p=PX(uv)/u_p0;vec2 ip=floor(p);vec2 fq=fract(p)-.5;float hist[9];for(int i=0;i<9;i++)hist[i]=0.;for(int j=0;j<4;j++)for(int i=0;i<4;i++){vec2 q=fromPX((ip+(vec2(float(i),float(j))+.5)/4.)*u_p0);vec2 g=sobel(q);float a=mod(atan(g.y,g.x),PI);int b=int(min(a/PI*9.,8.));hist[b]+=length(g);}
  float v=0.;for(int b=0;b<9;b++){float a=(float(b)+.5)/9.*PI+1.5708;vec2 d=vec2(cos(a),sin(a));float dist=abs(dot(fq,vec2(-d.y,d.x)));float along=abs(dot(fq,d));v=max(v,hist[b]*u_p1*.03*(1.-smoothstep(.02,.06,dist))*step(along,.45));}return vec4(vec3(clamp(v,0.,1.)),1.);

filters.name: Local Entropy
filters.note: information per region
passes: float h[16];for(int i=0;i<16;i++)h[i]=0.;for(int j=-3;j<=3;j++)for(int i=-3;i<=3;i++)h[int(clamp(L(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*R(u_p0)/6.*u_px)*16.,0.,15.))]+=1.;float e=0.;for(int i=0;i<16;i++){float p=h[i]/49.;if(p>0.)e-=p*log2(p);}return vec4(vec3(clamp(e/4.*u_p1,0.,1.)),1.);

filters.name: Saliency (center-surround)
filters.note: Itti-style contrast
passes: vec3 c1=blur5(uv,R(u_p0)*.3),s1=blur5(uv,R(u_p0)*1.5),s2=blur5(uv,R(u_p0)*4.);vec3 o1=vec3(luma(c1),c1.r-c1.g,(c1.r+c1.g)*.5-c1.b),o2=vec3(luma(s1),s1.r-s1.g,(s1.r+s1.g)*.5-s1.b),o3=vec3(luma(s2),s2.r-s2.g,(s2.r+s2.g)*.5-s2.b);float sal=length(o1-o2)+length(o1-o3)*.7+length(sobelD(uv,R(u_p0)))*.15;return vec4(ramp(1,clamp(sal*u_p1,0.,1.)),1.);

filters.name: Local Statistics
filters.note: per-window stats
passes: float m=0.,s=0.,mn=1.,mx=0.;float v[25];int n=0;for(int j=-2;j<=2;j++)for(int i=-2;i<=2;i++){float l=L(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*R(u_p1)/4.*u_px);m+=l;s+=l*l;mn=min(mn,l);mx=max(mx,l);v[n++]=l;}m/=25.;int st=int(u_p0+.5);float r;if(st==0)r=m;else if(st==1)r=sqrt(max(s/25.-m*m,0.))*u_p2*3.;else if(st==2)r=mn;else if(st==3)r=mx;else if(st==4)r=(mx-mn)*u_p2;else{float cnt=0.;for(int i=0;i<25;i++)cnt+=step(v[i],m);r=mix(mn,mx,cnt/25.);}return vec4(vec3(clamp(r,0.,1.)),1.);

filters.name: Dark Channel
filters.note: haze / depth cue (He 2009)
passes: float dk=1.;for(int j=-2;j<=2;j++)for(int i=-2;i<=2;i++){vec3 s=T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*R(u_p0)*.5*u_px).rgb;dk=min(dk,min(s.r,min(s.g,s.b)));}return vec4(vec3(dk),1.);

filters.name: Specular Highlights
filters.note: glare / specular
passes: vec3 h=rgb2hsv(c.rgb);float m=smoothstep(u_p0,u_p0+.05,h.z)*(1.-smoothstep(u_p1,u_p1+.1,h.y));return vec4(u_p2<.5?vec3(m):mix(c.rgb*.4,vec3(1.,.9,.2),m),1.);

filters.name: Shadow Mask
filters.note: darker than surroundings, same chroma
passes: float l=L(uv);float m=blurL(uv,R(u_p1)*.5);vec3 ch=c.rgb/max(dot(c.rgb,vec3(1.)),.01);vec3 mc=blur5(uv,R(u_p1)*.5);vec3 chm=mc/max(dot(mc,vec3(1.)),.01);float sh=smoothstep(u_p0,u_p0+.1,m-l)*(1.-smoothstep(.04,.12,length(ch-chm)));return vec4(u_p2<.5?vec3(sh):mix(c.rgb,vec3(.2,.3,1.),sh*.6),1.);

filters.name: Focus / Blur Map
filters.note: variance of Laplacian
passes: float m=0.,s=0.;for(int j=-2;j<=2;j++)for(int i=-2;i<=2;i++){vec2 q=uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*R(u_p0)/4.*u_px;vec2 e=u_px;float lap=L(q+vec2(e.x,0.))+L(q-vec2(e.x,0.))+L(q+vec2(0.,e.y))+L(q-vec2(0.,e.y))-4.*L(q);m+=lap;s+=lap*lap;}m/=25.;float v=clamp(sqrt(max(s/25.-m*m,0.))*u_p1,0.,1.);return vec4(u_p2<.5?vec3(v):ramp(1,v),1.);

filters.name: JPEG Blockiness Map
filters.note: 8×8 grid discontinuities

filters.note: automatic white balance
passes:
int m=int(u_p0+.5);vec3 acc=vec3(0.);vec3 mx=vec3(0.);for(int j=0;j<16;j++)for(int i=0;i<16;i++){vec2 q=(vec2(float(i),float(j))+.5)/16.;vec3 s=O(q).rgb;if(m==0)acc+=s;else if(m==1)mx=max(mx,s);else if(m==2)acc+=pow(s,vec3(6.));else{vec2 e=vec2(.004);acc+=abs(O(q+vec2(e.x,0.)).rgb-O(q-vec2(e.x,0.)).rgb)+abs(O(q+vec2(0.,e.y)).rgb-O(q-vec2(0.,e.y)).rgb);}}

passes:
vec2 e=u_px*max(u_k,1.);float z=L(uv);float zx=(L(uv+vec2(e.x,0.))-L(uv-vec2(e.x,0.)))*.5,zy=(L(uv+vec2(0.,e.y))-L(uv-vec2(0.,e.y)))*.5;float zxx=L(uv+vec2(e.x,0.))+L(uv-vec2(e.x,0.))-2.*z,zyy=L(uv+vec2(0.,e.y))+L(uv-vec2(0.,e.y))-2.*z,zxy=(L(uv+e)+L(uv-e)-L(uv+vec2(e.x,-e.y))-L(uv+vec2(-e.x,e.y)))*.25;float p=zx*zx+zy*zy+1e-9;int m=int(u_p0+.5);

filters.note: horizon angles in 8 directions
passes: float h=L(uv)*u_p1;float acc=0.;for(int k=0;k<8;k++){vec2 d=vec2(cos(float(k)*.785),sin(float(k)*.785));float mx=0.;for(int s=1;s<=16;s++){float r=float(s)/16.*R(u_p0);float hh=L(uv+d*r*u_px)*u_p1;mx=max(mx,atan((hh-h)/(r/u_k)));}acc+=1.-sin(max(mx,0.));}return vec4(vec3(acc/8.),1.);

filters.name: Cast Shadows (sun)
filters.note: ray-marched toward the sun
passes: float az=radians(u_p0);vec2 d=vec2(cos(az),sin(az));float h=L(uv)*u_p2;float t=tan(radians(u_p1));float lit=1.;for(int s=1;s<=48;s++){float r=float(s)*float(s)*.35;vec2 q=uv+d*r*u_k*u_px;if(q.x<0.||q.y<0.||q.x>1.||q.y>1.)break;if(L(q)*u_p2>h+r*t){lit=0.;break;}}vec3 base=mix(vec3(.85),c.rgb,u_p3);return vec4(base*(.35+.65*lit),1.);

filters.name: Contourlet-style Directional Bands
filters.note: Do & Vetterli contourlet idea, spatial approx.: octave band-pass followed by 8 directional filters (elongated 2nd-derivative-across, Gaussian-along kernels at 22.5° steps); dominant direction as hue, the 8 bands around the band-pass in a 3×3 mosaic, or one band — no critically sampled DFB

filters.name: Riesz Pyramid (amplitude / phase / orientation)
filters.note: Wadhwa et al. 2014: Laplacian-pyramid band (G_l−1 − G_l, Gaussian approx.) plus the 3-tap Riesz approximation [½, 0, −½] at the level spacing → monogenic amplitude, phase and orientation

params.label: Output
opts: Phase as hue, amplitude as value

filters.name: Wavelet Denoise (BayesShrink, à trous)
filters.note: undecimated (à trous) detail levels as differences of the equivalent Gaussians of the B3 cascade (approx.), noise σ from the MAD of the finest level (64 samples, or set it), spatially adaptive BayesShrink soft threshold T = σ_n² / σ_x per level (σ_x from 5 local detail samples), subtracted level by level
passes: return int(u_p3+.5)==1?vec4(clamp(.5+(O(uv).rgb-c.rgb)*4.,0.,1.),1.):c;

filters.name: 2xSaI / Super 2xSaI / Super Eagle
filters.note: Kreed 2xSaI / Super 2xSaI / Super Eagle rules (snes9x), 2×2 sub-blocks per source pixel

filters.name: hqx (hq2x / hq3x / hq4x, approx.)
filters.note: approx.: hqx YUV-threshold neighbour tests (Y 48, U 7, V 6 /255) with generic corner-blend rules instead of the 256-case lookup table

filters.name: xBRZ (free scale)
filters.note: Zenju xBRZ: 4×4 corner pre-pass (dominant gradient), line / shallow / steep / corner blends; coverage rendered at any pixel size (freescale-style)

filters.name: MMPX (McGuire & Gagiu 2021)
filters.note: MMPX 2× rules: 1:1 slopes, intersections, triangle tips, 2:1 slopes (palette-preserving, no blending)

filters.name: SABR (Street)
filters.note: SABR v3.0 (Joshua Street): xBR-style edge rules with 30° / 45° / 60° smoothstep corner blends

filters.name: FSR 1 EASU Upscale (from N× grid)
filters.note: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1 EASU: 12-tap direction-adaptive Lanczos-like kernel, de-ringing clamp

filters.name: Bicubic Sharpener (from N× grid, approx.)
filters.note: approx. (no CNN): Catmull-Rom upsampling + edge-weighted detail boost with anti-ringing clamp, imitating FSRCNN-style crisp edges

filters.name: Super-xBR (2× lattice, approx. weights)
filters.note: Hyllian Super-xBR scheme: diagonal pass then orthogonal pass on the 45°-rotated grid, 4-tap directional filters, edge-strength blend, anti-ringing clamp; then bilinear to the block grid

filters.name: NEDI (New Edge-Directed Interpolation)
filters.note: Li & Orchard 2001: 4 interpolation weights per new pixel from local covariance (least squares over a 4×4 training window), diagonal then rotated pass; bilinear fallback in flat / ill-conditioned windows

filters.name: ICBI (Iterative Curvature-Based Interpolation, approx.)
filters.note: Giachetti & Asuni 2011: FCBI second-derivative direction choice, then 3 refinement iterations per step (approx.: curvature-continuity target per direction weighted by local curvature energy, instead of the full energy with isolevel term)

filters.name: Recursive Gaussian (Deriche)
filters.note: Deriche 1993 4th-order recursive-Gaussian impulse response (a0=1.68, a1=3.735, b0=1.783 …) applied as a separable truncated FIR (same response, GPU-parallel); derivatives by central differences of the smoothed image, σ-normalised
passes:
float sg=max(R(u_p0),.3);float st=max(1.,sg*4./48.);vec3 a=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;for(int k=-48;k<=48;k++){float x=float(k)*st;if(abs(x)>sg*4.+.5)continue;float t=abs(x)/sg;
    float h=(1.68*cos(.6318*t)+3.735*sin(.6318*t))*exp(-1.783*t)+(-.6803*cos(1.997*t)-.2598*sin(1.997*t))*exp(-1.723*t);a+=T(uv+vec2(x*u_px.x,0.)).rgb*h;ws+=h;}return vec4(a/ws,1.);

float sg=max(R(u_p0),.3);float st=max(1.,sg*4./48.);vec3 a=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;for(int k=-48;k<=48;k++){float x=float(k)*st;if(abs(x)>sg*4.+.5)continue;float t=abs(x)/sg;
    float h=(1.68*cos(.6318*t)+3.735*sin(.6318*t))*exp(-1.783*t)+(-.6803*cos(1.997*t)-.2598*sin(1.997*t))*exp(-1.723*t);a+=T(uv+vec2(0.,x*u_px.y)).rgb*h;ws+=h;}return vec4(a/ws,1.);

filters.name: Patch-Based Denoising (ITK-style)
filters.note: ITK PatchBasedDenoisingImageFilter-style: iterated patch-similarity weighted averaging (5×5 Gaussian-weighted patches, 25 candidates on a golden-angle spiral), bandwidth from an Immerkær noise estimate (approx.: no entropy-based bandwidth optimisation)

filters.name: Diffusion Flows (ITK)
filters.note: explicit iterations of the ITK PDEs: Perona-Malik with vector conductance, Whitaker MCDE |∇I|·div(c·∇I/|∇I|), level-set curvature flow κ|∇I|, Malladi-Sethian min/max switch (stencil radius 2)

filters.name: Confidence Connected (iterative)
filters.note: ITK ConfidenceConnected: seed-neighbourhood mean ± k·σ, connected growth (wall-checked jumps), then re-estimate mean/σ over the region (24×24 sample grid) and regrow from the seed, N iterations
passes:
vec2 sd=vec2(u_p0,1.-u_p1);float m=0.,q=0.;for(int j=-2;j<=2;j++)for(int i=-2;i<=2;i++){float l=luma(O(sd+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_k*u_px).rgb);m+=l;q+=l*l;}m/=25.;float sdv=sqrt(max(q/25.-m*m,0.));
    float hw=max(u_p2*sdv,.02);return vec4(length((uv-sd)*u_res)<2.5*max(u_k,1.)?1.:0.,m,hw,1.);

vec4 me=T(uv);if(0.>=u_p3)return me;float n=0.,m=0.,q=0.;for(int j=0;j<24;j++)for(int i=0;i<24;i++){vec2 p=(vec2(float(i),float(j))+.5)/24.;if(T(p).r>.5){float l=luma(O(p).rgb);n+=1.;m+=l;q+=l*l;}}
     vec2 sd=vec2(u_p0,1.-u_p1);float seed=length((uv-sd)*u_res)<2.5*max(u_k,1.)?1.:0.;if(n<6.)return vec4(seed,me.gb,1.);m/=n;float hw=max(u_p2*sqrt(max(q/n-m*m,0.)),.02);return vec4(seed,m,hw,1.);

vec4 me=T(uv);if(1.>=u_p3)return me;float n=0.,m=0.,q=0.;for(int j=0;j<24;j++)for(int i=0;i<24;i++){vec2 p=(vec2(float(i),float(j))+.5)/24.;if(T(p).r>.5){float l=luma(O(p).rgb);n+=1.;m+=l;q+=l*l;}}
     vec2 sd=vec2(u_p0,1.-u_p1);float seed=length((uv-sd)*u_res)<2.5*max(u_k,1.)?1.:0.;if(n<6.)return vec4(seed,me.gb,1.);m/=n;float hw=max(u_p2*sqrt(max(q/n-m*m,0.)),.02);return vec4(seed,m,hw,1.);

vec4 me=T(uv);if(2.>=u_p3)return me;float n=0.,m=0.,q=0.;for(int j=0;j<24;j++)for(int i=0;i<24;i++){vec2 p=(vec2(float(i),float(j))+.5)/24.;if(T(p).r>.5){float l=luma(O(p).rgb);n+=1.;m+=l;q+=l*l;}}
     vec2 sd=vec2(u_p0,1.-u_p1);float seed=length((uv-sd)*u_res)<2.5*max(u_k,1.)?1.:0.;if(n<6.)return vec4(seed,me.gb,1.);m/=n;float hw=max(u_p2*sqrt(max(q/n-m*m,0.)),.02);return vec4(seed,m,hw,1.);

filters.name: Level-Set Segmentation (Geodesic Active Contour / Shape Detection)
filters.note: level-set evolution φ_t = g(c + εκ)|∇φ| (+ ∇g·∇φ advection for GAC), g = 1/(1+|∇Gσ*I|²/K²), shrinking from a centred circle; 200 fixed iterations, clamped ±16 px band with Sussman-style reinitialisation
passes:
vec2 e=u_px;float gx=blurL(uv+vec2(e.x,0.),1.)-blurL(uv-vec2(e.x,0.),1.),gy=blurL(uv+vec2(0.,e.y),1.)-blurL(uv-vec2(0.,e.y),1.);float gm=length(vec2(gx,gy))*.5/max(u_k,1.);
  float gp=1./(1.+gm*gm/(.035*.035));vec2 p=(uv-.5)*u_res;float rad=u_p1*min(u_res.x,u_res.y);float ph=clamp(length(p)-rad,-16.,16.);return vec4(.5+ph/32.,gp,0.,1.);

float ph=T(uv).r-.5;vec3 o=O(uv).rgb;float ed=0.;for(int k=0;k<4;k++){vec2 d=(k==0?vec2(1.,0.):k==1?vec2(-1.,0.):k==2?vec2(0.,1.):vec2(0.,-1.))*u_px;ed=max(ed,step(0.,ph*(T(uv+d).r-.5)*-1.));}
    return vec4(mix(ph<0.?o:o*.4,vec3(1.,.15,.1),ed),1.);

filters.name: Distance Transform (Chamfer / Signed Maurer)
filters.note: jump-flooding nearest-feature transform for both phases, scored with the chosen metric (closed-form chamfer distances); signed output = Maurer convention, negative inside
passes:
#define BIN(q) (((luma(O(q).rgb)>(.5))!=((u_p0<.5?1.:0.)>.5))?1.:0.)
  float fg=BIN(uv);return vec4(fg>.5?uv:vec2(-1.),0.,1.);

filters.name: Label Contours
filters.note: ITK LabelContourImageFilter on colour-quantised labels: pixels with a differently labelled face / full neighbour

filters.name: Geodesic Distance (gray-weighted)
filters.note: distance from a seed point with local cost 1 + w·|∇I| (gray-weighted geodesic), min-plus propagation with path-integrated jumps (64 … 1 px, repeated)

filters.name: Leveling (Meyer)
filters.note: Meyer leveling λ(f, g): lower part by geodesic dilation of the marker under f, upper part by geodesic erosion above f (path-checked jumps, per channel); marker = Gaussian blur or flat-disc opening
passes: if(u_p1<.5)return vec4(blur5(uv,R(u_p0)*.5),1.);vec3 mn=vec3(1.);for(int j=-3;j<=3;j++)for(int i=-3;i<=3;i++){vec2 d=vec2(float(i),float(j))/3.;if(dot(d,d)>1.)continue;mn=min(mn,T(uv+d*R(u_p0)*u_px).rgb);}return vec4(mn,1.);

if(u_p1<.5)return T(uv);vec3 mx=vec3(0.);for(int j=-3;j<=3;j++)for(int i=-3;i<=3;i++){vec2 d=vec2(float(i),float(j))/3.;if(dot(d,d)>1.)continue;mx=max(mx,T(uv+d*R(u_p0)*u_px).rgb);}return vec4(mx,1.);
vec3 l=T(uv).rgb;int m=int(u_p2+.5);if(m==0)return vec4(l,1.);if(m==1)return vec4(clamp(.5+(O(uv).rgb-l)*2.,0.,1.),1.);return vec4(l,1.);

filters.name: Convex Hull (iterative)
filters.note: approx.: iterated segment closure — a pixel joins when object pixels lie on both sides of it along one of 12 line directions within the range (3 iterations ≈ Carathéodory closure); nearby objects within range merge
passes:
#define BIN(q) (((luma(O(q).rgb)>(.5))!=((u_p0<.5?1.:0.)>.5))?1.:0.)
  float b=BIN(uv);return vec4(b,b,0.,1.);
vec4 me=T(uv);int m=int(u_p2+.5);if(m==1)return vec4(vec3(me.r),1.);if(m==2)return vec4(mix(O(uv).rgb*.5,mix(O(uv).rgb,vec3(.2,.6,1.),.4),me.r),1.);return vec4(vec3(me.g>.5?0.:me.r>.5?.62:1.),1.);

filters.name: Howe Binarization (approx.)
filters.note: approx. of Howe 2013: Laplacian data term (+ local-mean term) with edge-cut pairwise smoothness, solved by mean-field iterations instead of graph cut; no automatic parameter tuning
passes: return vec4(vec3(T(uv).r>.5?0.:1.),1.);

filters.name: Dot Diffusion (Knuth)
filters.note: Knuth 1987: 8×8 class matrix, pixels quantised class by class (64 passes), error spread to not-yet-processed neighbours (orthogonal weight 2, diagonal 1); optional pre-sharpening

filters.name: Interlaced Field Blend
filters.note: static simulation: two fields captured with a motion offset between them, then blend / weave / bob deinterlacing (no real video fields)

filters.name: Handheld LCD Ghosting
filters.note: static simulation of slow LCD pixel response: each pixel = exponentially weighted history of an assumed uniform pan (real ghosting needs previous frames)

filters.name: Redscale Film
filters.note: film loaded backwards: exposure through the base reaches the red-sensitive layer first — red / orange / yellow monochrome with crushed blues

filters.name: Film Gate Weave
filters.note: one frame of projector / camera gate weave: random (seeded) sub-frame offset and tilt, directional softness, exposed gate edge — static frame only

filters.name: Emoji Mosaic (procedural glyphs)
filters.note: cells replaced by procedurally drawn emoji-like glyphs picked by cell colour (smiley, heart, tree, droplet, cloud, cookie, orange, moon, black circle) — no emoji font

filters.name: Kim-Kautz Consistent Tone Mapping
filters.note: Kim & Kautz 2008: log-luminance scaled by k(x) = (1 − k1)·G(x − μ) + k1, k1 = display / scene log range (0.3–300 cd/m²), σ = range / c1; mean anchored at 18 % grey; stats from a 16×16 sample grid

filters.name: iCAM06 (simplified)
filters.note: simplified iCAM06 (Kuang, Johnson & Fairchild 2007): bilateral base/detail split, local CAT02 adaptation to a blurred white, Hunt-Pointer-Estevez cone compression with F_L from the local adapting luminance, detail boost (F_L+0.8)^0.25; no rod term, IPT colourfulness or surround stages; white normalised to 2.5× the local adapting white instead of a 99th-percentile clip
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p1));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p1));

filters.name: Hable Piecewise Power Curves
filters.note: John Hable 2017 “Filmic Tonemapping with Piecewise Power Curves”: toe power segment, linear mid, shoulder power segment from toe/shoulder strength & length (white point = 2^shoulder strength), per channel

filters.name: CAM16-UCS (J′ a′ b′)
filters.note: Li et al. 2017 CAM16 forward model (M16 adaptation, D from L_A and surround, Y_b = 20, D65 white) → CAM16-UCS J′ = 1.7J/(1+0.007J), M′ = ln(1+0.0228M)/0.0228, a′b′ = M′(cos h, sin h)

filters.name: KAZE / AKAZE Nonlinear Scale Space
filters.note: Alcantarilla et al.: Perona-Malik g2 diffusion with contrast factor k = 70th percentile of |∇L| (sampled), evolution time t = σ²/2; KAZE uses AOS (here: 40 explicit steps, approx.), AKAZE uses Fast Explicit Diffusion cycles (n = 5, τmax = 0.25, reordered steps, conductance fixed per cycle; up to 8 cycles, t ≤ 20); scale-normalised Hessian determinant and single-scale 3×3 maxima
passes:
vec4 me=T(uv);vec2 e=u_px;float l=me.r;float lxx=T(uv+vec2(e.x,0.)).r+T(uv-vec2(e.x,0.)).r-2.*l,lyy=T(uv+vec2(0.,e.y)).r+T(uv-vec2(0.,e.y)).r-2.*l,lxy=(T(uv+e).r+T(uv-e).r-T(uv+vec2(e.x,-e.y)).r-T(uv+vec2(-e.x,e.y)).r)*.25;
    float sg=R(u_p1);return vec4(l,me.g,(lxx*lyy-lxy*lxy)*sg*sg*sg*sg,1.);

filters.name: Log-Gabor Filter Bank (spatial approx.)
filters.note: approx.: log-Gabor bank (4 orientations, up to 4 scales, scale factor 2.1) emulated in the spatial domain with zero-mean Gaussian-windowed quadrature pairs of matched ~2-octave bandwidth (true log-Gabor needs the FFT); phase congruency = Kovesi energy / Σ amplitude with a fixed noise floor

filters.name: Superpixels II (SEEDS / LSC, approx.)
filters.note: approx.: labels start on a regular grid and boundary pixels hill-climb (checkerboard updates, 16 iterations) between neighbouring labels; SEEDS = colour-histogram likelihood (4³ bins, sampled members) + 3×3 boundary prior, no block levels; LSC = assignment to the nearest weighted mean in the 10-D cosine feature space φ(L,a,b,x,y) with weights w = φ·φ̄ (Li & Chen 2015), cluster means estimated from sampled members

filters.name: Core Image Distortions
filters.note: CIHoleDistortion, CILightTunnel, CICircleSplashDistortion, CICircularWrap, CIGlassLozenge, CITorusLensDistortion, CIVortexDistortion, CIBumpDistortionLinear — centred at the image centre; Radius in image heights; lozenge/torus refract through a glass dome (refraction = ior−1); approx. of Apple's kernels (hole/wrap outside → black)

filters.name: Core Image Tiles
filters.note: CIOpTile, CIParallelogramTile, CIPerspectiveTile, CIEightfoldReflectedTile (p4m), CIFourfoldRotatedTile (p4), CIFourfoldTranslatedTile, CIGlideReflectedTile (pg), CISixfoldRotatedTile (p6), CITwelvefoldReflectedTile (p6m), CITriangleKaleidoscope (mirror walk into an equilateral triangle), CITriangleTile (orientation-preserving copies), CIAffineClamp (scaled/rotated with clamped edges); source tile = the region of Width around the image centre; approx.

filters.name: Stretch Crop (Core Image)
filters.note: CIStretchCrop: fits the image to a new aspect (shown letterboxed in the frame) by cropping a share of the change and stretching the rest; center stretch 0 keeps the centre at native scale and stretches the sides (cubic map); approx.

filters.name: Gloom / Edge Work / Circular Screen
filters.note: CIGloom (dulls highlights: image × its Gaussian blur, the inverse of a screen bloom, darken-only), CIEdgeWork (black where darker than the local Gaussian mean → woodblock cut), CICircularScreen (concentric-ring halftone around the centre, sharpness = edge hardness); approx.
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p1));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p1));

filters.name: Height Field from Mask / Shaded Material
filters.note: CIHeightFieldFromMask (mask = luma > threshold; height rises smoothly from 0 at the mask edge, quarter-circle profile over a Gaussian-blurred mask, approx. of Apple's rounded field) and CIShadedMaterial (normals of that height field look up a shading sphere: procedural chrome / plastic, or the image itself as the shading image)
passes: float m=smoothstep(u_p1-.03,u_p1+.03,luma(O(uv).rgb));return vec4(vec3(m),1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Spot Light / Halo / Star Shine / Hot Spot
filters.note: CISpotLight (cone light above the image plane aimed at Position, Lambert × cone falloff, no ambient), CILenticularHaloGenerator (RGB-offset halo ring with noisy striations), CIStarShineGenerator (core + 4-point cross rays at 0.6 rad), Fusion Hot Spot (hot-spot glow + secondary reflections along the axis through the centre), composited additively; approx.

filters.name: Lens Reflections (from highlights)
filters.note: Resolve Lens Reflections: highlights (above Threshold) are mirrored through the optical centre at several scales as tinted ghosts with RGB dispersion, plus a halo ring (screen-space pseudo lens flare, Chapman 2013 style); approx.
passes: {vec3 c=O(uv).rgb;float l=max(c.r,max(c.g,c.b));return vec4(c*smoothstep(u_p0,min(u_p0+.15,1.),l),1.);}return c;
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(5.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(5.));

filters.name: Prism Blur
filters.note: Resolve Prism Blur: the image is smeared along a radial or linear direction and the smear is split into red→green→blue spectral bands (each band normalised, so neutrals stay neutral); Softness widens the bands

filters.name: Core Image Photo Effects
filters.note: CIPhotoEffectChrome / Fade / Instant / Process / Tonal / Transfer (the Photos-app looks): Apple ships them as 3D LUTs, these are hand-matched approximations (contrast, saturation, black lift, tint)

filters.name: Color Cross Polynomial
filters.note: CIColorCrossPolynomial: out = linear + square (r², g², b²) + cross-product (rg, gb, br) terms per channel; the 30 coefficients are reduced to 4 symmetric controls that leave greys unchanged except Square terms (a tone curve)
passes:
{vec3 c=O(uv).rgb;vec3 o=c;o+=u_p0*((c.gbr+c.brg)*.5-c);o+=u_p1*(c*c-c);float pm=(c.r*c.g+c.g*c.b+c.b*c.r)/3.;o+=u_p2*(c.gbr*c.brg-pm);o+=u_p3*(c.gbr-c.brg);
 return vec4(clamp(o,0.,1.),1.);}return c;

filters.name: Linear ↔ sRGB Tone Curve
filters.note: CILinearToSRGBToneCurve / CISRGBToneCurveToLinear: exact IEC 61966-2-1 piecewise sRGB transfer function

filters.name: Lift / Gamma / Gain
filters.note: Resolve / ASC-style primaries: out = (gain·(x + lift·(1−x)))^(1/gamma), master or one channel (lift pivots at white, gain at black)
passes:
{vec3 c=O(uv).rgb;int m=int(u_p0+.5);vec3 k=m==0?vec3(1.):m==1?vec3(1.,0.,0.):m==2?vec3(0.,1.,0.):vec3(0.,0.,1.);
 vec3 y=clamp(u_p3*(c+u_p1*(1.-c)),0.,1.);y=pow(y,vec3(1./u_p2));return vec4(mix(c,y,k),1.);}return c;

filters.name: Printer Lights
filters.note: Resolve printer-light offsets: each point = 0.025 log exposure ≈ 1/12 stop applied per channel in linear light (lab printer-point convention; Resolve lets the step be changed)
passes: {vec3 c=clamp(O(uv).rgb,0.,1.);vec3 li=mix(c/12.92,pow((c+.055)/1.055,vec3(2.4)),step(vec3(.04045),c));li*=exp2((vec3(u_p0,u_p1,u_p2)+u_p3)/12.);li=clamp(li,0.,1.);return vec4(mix(li*12.92,1.055*pow(max(li,vec3(0.)),vec3(1./2.4))-.055,step(vec3(.0031308),li)),1.);}return c;

filters.name: Color Density / Compressor / Gamut Limiter
filters.note: Resolve Color Density / subtractive saturation (more saturation, saturated colours darken like dye density), Color Compressor (hues within Range of the target are pulled toward it, saturation evened), Gamut Limiter (BT.709 Y′CbCr chroma soft-limited with a knee, then out-of-gamut RGB desaturated toward luma); approx.

filters.name: Pseudo Color (Fusion)
filters.note: Fusion Pseudo Color: each output channel is a sine wave of the luminance (wavelength, phase, amplitude around a 0.5 mean), channels phase-shifted by Channel spread
passes: float l=luma(O(uv).rgb);vec3 k=vec3(0.,1.,2.)*u_p2;return vec4(clamp(.5+u_p3*sin(6.2831853*(l/u_p0+u_p1+k)),0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Blanking Fill
filters.note: Resolve Blanking Fill: the blanking bars (given size) are filled with a blurred, dimmed, zoomed copy of the active picture so the frame has no black bars
passes: float z=1.-2.*u_p1;return vec4(O(.5+(uv-.5)*z).rgb,1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Drip (Fusion)
filters.note: Fusion Drip: ripple displacement along the gradient of a shape field (circular, square, random-warped, horizontal, vertical, exponential spacing, star, radial/angular), damped with distance

filters.name: Patch Replacer
filters.note: Resolve Patch Replacer: a circular patch at the image centre is replaced by the region at the source offset; Clone copies it, Adaptive blend adds the boundary colour difference interpolated inside the patch (Shepard / membrane approx. of Poisson blending); feathered edge

filters.name: Film Look Creator
filters.note: Resolve Film Look Creator (approx.): halation (red-orange glow of highlights) + bloom, a print-style tone curve and colour look, vignette and luminance-weighted film grain
passes: {vec3 c=O(uv).rgb;return vec4(c*smoothstep(.55,1.,luma(c)),1.);}return c;
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(20.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(20.));

filters.name: Gabor Gradients

filters.name: AdaptiveSharpen (bacondither)
filters.note: mpv AdaptiveSharpen idea: edge map from the 3×3 blur residual (pass 1), luma sharpening against an edge-similarity weighted 12-tap diamond blur, stronger on edges than flat areas, with soft-compressed overshoot beyond the local min/max (approx., not the exact tuned curves)

filters.note: wide-gamut content shown on sRGB: the input values are read as P3 / BT.2020 / Adobe RGB (sRGB transfer) and converted; libplacebo perceptual = IPT(PQ) blend toward the saturation-mapped colour near the hue cusp (deadzone .3) + Mobius softclip (knee .7) of saturated channels; highlight = out-of-gamut pixels get I+0.1 and inverted P/T; IPT uses Hunt LMS + Dolby PQ-IPT matrix, cusps approximated per pixel (approx.)

filters.name: AV1 Film Grain Synthesis
filters.note: AV1 spec film grain model: Gaussian 82×73 grain templates (Y, Cb, Cr), lag-2 auto-regressive shaping (12 causal coefficients, solved by 10 Jacobi iterations instead of the sequential raster scan), 32×32 blocks read at random 2-px-aligned template offsets, piecewise-linear luma scaling function; no block-overlap blending (approx.)
passes: vec2 w=floor(uv*u_res);if(w.x>=82.||w.y>=73.)return vec4(.5,.5,.5,1.);vec3 n=vec3(0.);for(int k=0;k<3;k++){float u1=max(hash(w+vec2(.17+float(k)*7.3,.31)),1e-6),u2=hash(w+vec2(3.7+float(k)*7.3,9.1));n[k]=sqrt(-2.*log(u1))*cos(6.2831853*u2);}return vec4(.5+n/16.,1.);

filters.name: H.274 Film Grain (frequency-filtering model)
filters.note: ITU-T H.274 / SEI film grain, frequency-filtering model as in FFmpeg h274.c: 64×64 grain pattern = inverse DCT of random coefficients up to freq ((cutoff+3)·4−1) in each direction (DC removed), horizontal-edge attenuation every 8 rows, 16×16 blocks read at random offsets (x multiple of 4, y multiple of 8) with random sign, vertical block-edge deblocking, intensity (midtone) weight; single intensity interval, luma only (approx.)

filters.name: Alternative Process II (albumen, ambrotype, carbon, iron & gold prints, toners)

filters.name: Retro Bit Depth & Fixed Palettes
filters.note: RGB555 (5 bits per channel, rounding), PS1 GPU 15-bit dithering (its 4x4 matrix -4..+3 added in 8-bit before the >>3 truncation), Mega Drive / Genesis VDP 3-bit DAC levels 0/52/87/116/144/172/206/255 (normal mode, no shadow/highlight), web-safe 6x6x6 cube, BBC Micro Mode 2 (1-bit RGB, 2:1 wide pixels, flashing colours unused), SweetFX Nostalgia 1.3 (C64 palette matched in linear light, checkerboard dither, type-1 scanlines)

filters.name: Adaptive Retro Palettes (Atari ST / Amiga)
filters.note: per-image palette like a converter would pick: 7 k-means (Lloyd) iterations over a 16x16 sample grid seeded from the grid (EHB clusters accept pixels matching their half-brite copy), entries rounded to the hardware DAC (Atari ST 3 bits, STE / Amiga 4 bits per channel; EHB halves are the 4-bit value >> 1), then nearest-entry mapping with optional ordered dither. Palette is stored in the first row of a scratch pass (needs width >= 32); no per-scanline palette changes (approx.)

filters.name: Mode 7 Floor (SNES)
filters.note: SNES Mode 7 floor: per-scanline affine map of the image as a ground plane seen in perspective (distance = height / rows below the horizon), rotated about the camera at the image centre, nearest-texel sampling, 16-band gradient backdrop above the horizon

filters.name: Retro 3D Texture Filtering (N64 3-point / bilinear / point)
filters.note: image box-averaged into texels, then magnified: N64 RDP 3-point filter (texel quad split along the diagonal, barycentric blend of 3 texels: the characteristic triangular / blocky-smooth look), standard bilinear, or PS1-style point sampling; optional 16-bit framebuffer with the RDP magic-square dither
passes: float ts=R(u_p1);vec2 j=floor(uv*u_res/ts);vec3 a=vec3(0.);for(int y_=0;y_<4;y_++)for(int x_=0;x_<4;x_++)a+=O((j+(vec2(float(x_),float(y_))+.5)/4.)*ts/u_res).rgb;return vec4(a/16.,1.);

filters.name: LED Matrix / E-ink / Game Boy Camera
filters.note: LED matrix: one round LED per cell (cell-averaged colour, 4-bit PWM levels, dark unlit LEDs, Gaussian bloom from the 3x3 neighbouring LEDs); E-ink: 16 grey levels with ordered dither on a grey paper (white ~ 0.86, black ~ 0.17) and a faint offset / inverted residue standing in for the previous page ghost (approx.); Game Boy Camera: M64282FP-style edge enhancement (centre minus 4-neighbour mean), contrast, 4 shades by 4x4 ordered dither, DMG green with pixel grid or printer greys
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p1*.35));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p1*.35));

filters.name: Thermal Receipt / Fax / Dot-Matrix / Mimeograph
filters.note: Thermal: 1-bit ordered dots on the head grid, weak columns / streaky fading along the feed (wear), grey-black print on cream paper. Fax: G3 standard resolution (cells 1 x 2, i.e. 204 x 98 dpi), hard 1-bit threshold (all outputs auto-levelled to the image black / white points like a scanner driver), scan-line slips, flipped bits and dropout lines. Dot-matrix: round overlapping dots on a 4x4 ordered dither, 8-row head passes with per-pass misregistration and ribbon wear, green-bar paper. Mimeograph / ditto: thresholded slightly spread ink with blotchy fbm density, offset smudge, purple spirit-duplicator variant (look approximations)

filters.name: ImageMagick Statistic (Nonpeak / RMS / ...)
filters.note: ImageMagick -statistic type WxH, per channel on a W×H window (8-bit quantised values). Nonpeak = the median, except when the median is the window minimum (then the next higher distinct value) or the maximum (next lower) — as in IM GetNonpeakPixelList; RMS = sqrt(mean of squares); Contrast = |max-min|/(max+min)

filters.name: ImageMagick Morphology: EdgeIn / EdgeOut / Thicken
filters.note: ImageMagick -morphology: EdgeIn = image − erode, EdgeOut = dilate − image (per channel, flat Diamond/Square/Disk/Plus kernel); Thicken ConvexHull = hit-and-miss thickening of the binarised image (foreground = light or dark pixels, threshold 0.5) with IM's ConvexHull kernel "1,1,-;1,0,-;1,-,0" plus its transpose, 4 rotations each — the 8 kernels are applied together each iteration (IM applies them in sequence), up to 40 iterations
passes: return u_p0>2.5?vec4(1.-T(uv).rgb,1.):T(uv);

filters.name: ImageMagick Blur Kernels (Comet / Binomial / Adaptive)
filters.note: ImageMagick kernels: Comet:{width}x{sigma}+{angle} = one-sided 1-D Gaussian (the -motion-blur kernel), Binomial:{radius} = outer product of Pascal-triangle rows (radius ≤ 7), -adaptive-blur = Gaussian whose sigma shrinks toward 0 near edges (edge strength = local Sobel normalised by 4× the image mean; approx. of IM's edge-image kernel selection)

filters.name: ImageMagick Point Ops (Blue Shift / Random Threshold / Modulus / Cycle)
filters.note: ImageMagick: -blue-shift factor (exact BlueShiftImage: each channel averaged with factor×min(RGB), then with factor×max(RGB) — a dim, desaturated moonlight look); -random-threshold low,high per channel (low/high = 0.5 ∓ Amount/2); -evaluate AddModulus/SubtractModulus value (wraps around); -cycle shifts a colour map by Amount×N entries — for true-colour input the map is N luminance bins whose colours are the bin means of a 16×16 sample grid (interpretation)

filters.name: ImageMagick Raise (3D Button Edge)
filters.note: ImageMagick RaiseImage: top band blended toward white with the accentuate factor 135/255, left band with highlight 190/255, right band toward black with shadow 190/255, bottom band with trough 135/255; 45° mitred corners; +raise swaps light and dark

filters.name: ImageMagick Arc / Cylinder Distortions
filters.note: ImageMagick -distort Arc angle,rotate,top_radius,bottom_radius (top row on the outer radius, default radii top = W/angle + H/2, bottom = top − H; result fitted to the frame) and Cylinder2Plane / Plane2Cylinder fov (r = W/fov; plane x = r·tan θ, y scaled by 1/cos θ); IM enlarges the canvas, here the result is scaled to fit

filters.name: ImageMagick Shepards / Polynomial Distortion
filters.note: ImageMagick -distort Shepards / Polynomial with control points = a G×G grid moved by seeded random jitter (press New random seed). Shepards: each output pixel takes the inverse-distance^power weighted mean of the control displacements (-define shepards:power); Polynomial: least-squares fit of the destination→source mapping with IM's term order (1, x, y, xy, x², y², x³, x²y, xy², y³)

filters.name: ImageMagick Sparse Color
filters.note: ImageMagick -sparse-color with N seeded points whose colours are sampled from the image: Shepards (inverse distance^power, -define shepards:power), Inverse (power 1), Voronoi (nearest, Euclidean), Manhattan (nearest, L1), Barycentric (least-squares affine colour gradient through all points)

filters.name: ImageMagick +noise (incl. Laplacian)
filters.note: ImageMagick GenerateDifferentialNoise with its constants (× attenuate): uniform 1/64, Gaussian σ 1/64·√p + τ 5/64, multiplicative ½, impulse 1/10, Laplacian 5/128 (p + σ·ln 2α, mirrored), Poisson 12.5 (Knuth product method), random 1 (replaces the pixel)

filters.name: Intensity Slicing & Pseudocolor (G&W)
filters.note: Gonzalez & Woods §3.2.4 intensity-level slicing (binary or preserving the rest) and §6.3.1 intensity slicing pseudocolour (N equal slices of the gray scale coloured blue→red, or one slice highlighted in yellow on gray, as in the weld example); input reduced to Rec.709 luma

params.label: Mode
opts: Level slice: range white, rest black
Level slice: range white, rest unchanged

filters.name: Piecewise-Linear Contrast Stretch (G&W)
filters.note: Gonzalez & Woods §3.2.4 contrast stretching through (0,0)-(r1,s1)-(r2,s2)-(1,1), per channel; r1 = r2, s1 = 0, s2 = 1 gives thresholding

filters.name: Color Slicing / chromahold
filters.note: Gonzalez & Woods §6.5.2 colour slicing: pixels outside a cube of width W (or sphere of radius R0) around the prototype colour become neutral gray; FFmpeg chromahold: chroma (BT.601 Cb/Cr) is removed where sqrt((du²+dv²)/2) > similarity, with a linear blend band. Prototype colour = mean of the image pixels within ±20° of the target hue (16×16 sample grid), else a mid-saturated hue

filters.name: Highboost & Cubic Unsharp Masking
filters.note: Gonzalez & Woods §3.6: highboost g = f + k·(f − Gaussian blur) (k > 1) and the Laplacian composite g = f − (k/2)·∇²f (8-neighbour); Ramponi 1998 cubic unsharp masking: the Laplacian term in each direction is weighted by the squared local difference (x₋ − x₊)², so noise in flat areas is not amplified (λ = 12k for 0..1 data)
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Median Variants & Adaptive Filters (G&W)
filters.note: Hybrid median (Nieminen 1987): median of {median of the + arms, median of the × arms, centre}; truncated median (Davies 1988): the distribution is cut on the far side of the median at the same distance as the near extreme, then the median of the rest (moves toward the mode); adaptive median (G&W §5.3, stages A/B, window grows to S_max); adaptive local noise reduction (G&W eq. 5.3-12) f = g − (σ²η/σ²L)(g − mL), ratio ≤ 1, σ²η auto = 10th-percentile 3×3 local variance of a 10×10 sample grid

filters.name: Edge-Preserving Smoothing (Nagao / Tomita-Tsuji / GIW / KNN / sab / yaepblur)
filters.note: Nagao & Matsuyama 1979 (centre 3×3 + 4 pentagonal + 4 hexagonal 7-pixel regions in 5×5: mean of the least-variance region); Tomita & Tsuji 1977 (five 3×3 squares); Wang, Vagnucci & Li 1981 gradient inverse weighting (weights 1/|Δ| in 8-bit units, centre 1/2); Davis & Rosenfeld 1978 K-nearest-neighbour mean (K = 1 + fraction·(n−1), by luma); FFmpeg sab ≈ joint bilateral with a 3×3-prefiltered luma guide (approx.); FFmpeg yaepblur: (σ·mean + var·x)/(var + σ), σ = 128·(2·strength)² in 8-bit² units; all iterable

filters.name: Edge-Avoiding A-Trous Wavelets (Dammertz)
filters.note: Dammertz et al. 2010: à-trous B3 5×5 kernel with hole spacing 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 px, each tap weighted by exp(−|Δcolour|²/σ²) with σ halved per level (colour edge-stopping only, no normal/position buffers for a single image)
passes:
if(0.>=u_p0)return T(uv);float st=1.*u_k;float sc=u_p1*pow(2.,-0.);vec3 me=T(uv).rgb;float hk[5]=float[5](.0625,.25,.375,.25,.0625);vec3 acc=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;
  for(int j=0;j<5;j++)for(int i=0;i<5;i++){vec3 q=T(uv+vec2(float(i-2),float(j-2))*st*u_px).rgb;vec3 d=q-me;float w=hk[i]*hk[j]*exp(-dot(d,d)/(sc*sc));acc+=q*w;ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,1.);

if(1.>=u_p0)return T(uv);float st=2.*u_k;float sc=u_p1*pow(2.,-1.);vec3 me=T(uv).rgb;float hk[5]=float[5](.0625,.25,.375,.25,.0625);vec3 acc=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;
  for(int j=0;j<5;j++)for(int i=0;i<5;i++){vec3 q=T(uv+vec2(float(i-2),float(j-2))*st*u_px).rgb;vec3 d=q-me;float w=hk[i]*hk[j]*exp(-dot(d,d)/(sc*sc));acc+=q*w;ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,1.);

if(2.>=u_p0)return T(uv);float st=4.*u_k;float sc=u_p1*pow(2.,-2.);vec3 me=T(uv).rgb;float hk[5]=float[5](.0625,.25,.375,.25,.0625);vec3 acc=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;
  for(int j=0;j<5;j++)for(int i=0;i<5;i++){vec3 q=T(uv+vec2(float(i-2),float(j-2))*st*u_px).rgb;vec3 d=q-me;float w=hk[i]*hk[j]*exp(-dot(d,d)/(sc*sc));acc+=q*w;ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,1.);

if(3.>=u_p0)return T(uv);float st=8.*u_k;float sc=u_p1*pow(2.,-3.);vec3 me=T(uv).rgb;float hk[5]=float[5](.0625,.25,.375,.25,.0625);vec3 acc=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;
  for(int j=0;j<5;j++)for(int i=0;i<5;i++){vec3 q=T(uv+vec2(float(i-2),float(j-2))*st*u_px).rgb;vec3 d=q-me;float w=hk[i]*hk[j]*exp(-dot(d,d)/(sc*sc));acc+=q*w;ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,1.);

if(4.>=u_p0)return T(uv);float st=16.*u_k;float sc=u_p1*pow(2.,-4.);vec3 me=T(uv).rgb;float hk[5]=float[5](.0625,.25,.375,.25,.0625);vec3 acc=vec3(0.);float ws=0.;
  for(int j=0;j<5;j++)for(int i=0;i<5;i++){vec3 q=T(uv+vec2(float(i-2),float(j-2))*st*u_px).rgb;vec3 d=q-me;float w=hk[i]*hk[j]*exp(-dot(d,d)/(sc*sc));acc+=q*w;ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,1.);

filters.name: Bilateral Grid (Chen-Paris-Durand)
filters.note: Chen, Paris & Durand 2007: splat colour + weight into a 3-D grid (cell × cell pixels × luma bin, nearest-bin), blur the grid with [1 2 1]³, slice with trilinear interpolation at (x, y, luma) and divide by the weight; spatial sigma ≈ cell size, range sigma ≈ 1/bins

filters.name: Di Zenzo Color Gradient
filters.note: Di Zenzo 1986: 2×2 colour structure tensor from per-channel Sobel derivatives, gradient magnitude = √λmax, direction = ½·atan2(2gxy, gxx − gyy) (optionally box-smoothed tensor); third output shows where the colour gradient exceeds the gradient of luma alone (isoluminant edges)

filters.name: GIST Descriptor (Oliva-Torralba, glyphs)
filters.note: Oliva & Torralba 2001 GIST, approx.: Gabor energy at 4 scales (wavelength 4-32 px, σ = λ/2) × 8 orientations averaged over each cell of a 4×4 (or 8×8) grid; each cell drawn as a polar glyph in the frequency plane (outer ring = finest scale, angle = wave-vector orientation). Spatial Gabor taps on the unfiltered image (no pre-whitening, coarse scales may alias)

filters.name: chromanr (FFmpeg Chroma Noise Reduction)
filters.note: FFmpeg chromanr: the chroma (BT.601 Cb/Cr) of each pixel is replaced by the mean chroma of the window samples (radius Size, every Step-th pixel) whose |ΔY|+|ΔU|+|ΔV| (or Euclidean) distance is below Threshold (8-bit units); luma untouched

filters.name: pp7 Deblock (FFmpeg, 7-point DCT)
filters.note: FFmpeg pp7 (approx.): for every pixel an orthonormal 7×7 DCT of its neighbourhood in Y/Cb/Cr, AC coefficients hard / soft / medium-thresholded (medium: |c| ≤ T → 0, T..2T → 2(|c|−T), above kept, as pp7), and only the centre sample is reconstructed (odd basis functions vanish there, so 16 coefficients suffice); threshold T = 1.2·QP/255 replaces pp7's integer DCT factors

filters.name: hqdn3d Spatial Denoise (FFmpeg)
filters.note: FFmpeg hqdn3d spatial part: causal recursive low-pass along each row (left→right) and then down each column on the row result, new = cur + (prev − cur)·(1 − |Δ|/255)^γ with γ = ln 0.25 / ln(1 − strength/255), in Y/Cb/Cr; recursion truncated to 32 px (approx.); the temporal part needs previous frames and is not included

filters.name: RemoveGrain Modes (AviSynth)
filters.note: AviSynth RemoveGrain (Kassandro) per RGB channel on the 3×3 neighbourhood: rank clipping (1-4), line-sensitive clipping over the 4 opposite-neighbour pairs (5-9, 18), nearest value (10), binomial blur (11/12), pair-extreme clip (17), means (19, 20), pair-average clip (21) and the halo/edge removers 23/24; field-interpolation modes 13-16 and 25-28 omitted; repeatable

filters.name: Delogo (FFmpeg)
filters.note: FFmpeg delogo: every pixel inside the rectangle is rebuilt from the rectangle's border — 3-tap averages of the left, right, top and bottom border pixels in its row/column, each weighted by the product of the distances to the other three sides

filters.name: CIE Chromaticity Scope (FFmpeg ciescope)
filters.note: FFmpeg ciescope-style chromaticity plot: image colours (36×36 sample grid, sRGB → XYZ) splatted into the CIE 1931 xy or 1976 u′v′ diagram over the spectral-locus horseshoe (380-700 nm, 29 tabulated points) with a gamut triangle and the D65 white point

filters.name: v360 Equirectangular / Cubemap / Flat (FFmpeg)
filters.note: FFmpeg v360 conversions (bilinear): equirectangular → 3×2 cubemap (face order r l u / d f b as v360 c3x2 "rludfb"), the inverse, and equirectangular → rectilinear view, with yaw / pitch rotation; face orientation conventions are this filter's own (round-trip consistent)

filters.name: AviSynth Sharpeners (LSFmod / SeeSaw / FineSharp / ContraSharpening)
filters.note: AviSynth sharpening scripts, single-frame: LSFmod Smode 3 (nonlinear ((|d|/16)^¼·16) with low/high damping 4/48 on a 3×3 binomial blur, limited to the 3×3 min/max ± overshoot); SeeSaw (Didée: denoised frame "tamed" to ±2 of the source, sharpen2 with Sstr 1.5, Szp 16, Spower 4, damping 5/24, limited to ±Slimit); FineSharp mode 1 (RemoveGrain 11 → 4 base, lstr 1.49, pstr 1.272, equalisation and XSharpen 0.19, approx.); ContraSharpening (Didée: minblur(denoised) minus its blur, clamped to the 3×3 range of what the denoiser removed). The denoised input is an internal Gaussian of the given sigma; temporal soothing omitted
passes: if(int(u_p0+.5)==2)return vec4(med9(uv,u_k),1.);return c;

filters.name: aWarpSharp2 / FastLineDarkenMOD (AviSynth)
filters.note: aWarpSharp2 (approx.): Sobel edge mask capped at the threshold, blurred twice, then each pixel is resampled from p − depth·∇mask (depth 16 × strength), which pulls edges together and thins lines; FastLineDarkenMOD: luma closing (3×3 max then min) capped at 191; where it exceeds the pixel by more than the threshold the pixel is darkened by (strength 48/128)·difference (thinning omitted)
passes: int m=int(u_p0+.5);if(m==0)return vec4(vec3(min(length(sobel(uv))*1.5,u_p2/255.)),1.);float mx=0.;for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++)mx=max(mx,L(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_k*u_px));return vec4(vec3(mx),1.);

if(u_p0>.5)return c;return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(3.));
if(u_p0>.5)return c;return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(3.));

vec3 o=O(uv).rgb;if(u_p0<.5){vec2 e=u_k*u_px;vec2 g=vec2(T(uv-vec2(e.x,0.)).r-T(uv+vec2(e.x,0.)).r,T(uv-vec2(0.,e.y)).r-T(uv+vec2(0.,e.y)).r);float dp=16.*u_p1;return O(uv+g*dp*.5*u_k*u_px);}

filters.name: RGB Spectral Indices II
filters.note: published formulas on chromatic coords r,g,b = R,G,B/(R+G+B): ExR = 1.4r - g (Meyer et al. 1998); ExB = 1.4b - g = (1.4B - G)/(R+G+B) (Mao et al. 2003); VEG = g/(r^0.667 b^0.333) (Hague et al. 2006); COM = 0.25 ExG + 0.30 ExGR + 0.33 CIVE + 0.12 VEG (Guijarro et al. 2011); GCC = G/(R+G+B) (Gillespie 1987, PhenoCam); WI = (G-B)/(R-G) (Woebbecke et al. 1995, shown as atan); MExG = 1.262g - 0.884r - 0.311b (Burgos-Artizzu et al. 2011); IKAW = (R-B)/(R+B) (Kawashima & Nakatani 1998); NGBDI = (G-B)/(G+B); RGRI = R/G (Gamon & Surfus 1999); RI = R^2/(B G^3) (Madeira et al. 1997); NDTI = (R-G)/(R+G) (Lacaux et al. 2007); ratio indices shown as log; display = index minus its value for neutral grey of the same brightness, times Gain

filters.name: Generalized Hyperbolic Stretch (GHS)
filters.note: Payne & Cranfield 2021 (PixInsight / Siril GHS): b = -1 log, b < 0 integral, b = 0 exponential, b > 0 hyperbolic (b = 1 harmonic) branches, mirrored below SP, linear above HP (continuous slope), normalised to 0..1; LP fixed at 0; per channel (RGB/K)

filters.name: Luminosity Masks (Lights / Darks / Midtones)
filters.note: Kuyper-style luminosity masks: Lights n = L^n (n-fold self-intersection), Darks n = (1-L)^n, Midtones n = 1 - Lights(n+1) - Darks(n+1); adjustment applied through the mask
passes:
float l=clamp(luma(c.rgb),0.,1.);float n=floor(u_p1+.5);int m=int(u_p0+.5);float mk=m==0?pow(l,n):m==1?pow(1.-l,n):clamp(1.-pow(l,n+1.)-pow(1.-l,n+1.),0.,1.);int o=int(u_p2+.5);
  if(o==0)return vec4(vec3(mk),1.);if(o==1)return vec4(mix(c.rgb*.6,vec3(1.,.15,.1),mk*.65),1.);if(o==2)return vec4(c.rgb+(1.-c.rgb)*mk*u_p3*.7,1.);return vec4(c.rgb*(1.-mk*u_p3*.7),1.);

filters.name: ACDNR (Adaptive Contrast-Driven Noise Reduction)
filters.note: PixInsight ACDNR idea, approx.: Gaussian smoothing (std dev) whose per-pixel change is cut where it exceeds the edge-protection threshold (fades out between 1x and 2x), weighted by an inverted lightness mask so dark low-SNR areas get the most; single pass, no structure-size or iteration controls
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p0*2.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p0*2.));
vec3 o=O(uv).rgb,d=T(uv).rgb-o;vec3 w=1.-smoothstep(vec3(u_p2),vec3(u_p2*2.),abs(d));float mk=mix(1.,1.-smoothstep(.1,.9,luma(o)),u_p3);return vec4(o+d*w*u_p1*mk,1.);

filters.name: Enhanced Lee / Frost (SAR speckle)
filters.note: Lopes, Touzi & Nezry 1990: Cu = 1/sqrt(ENL), Cmax = sqrt(1 + 2/ENL), Ci = local std/mean; Ci <= Cu -> local mean, Ci >= Cmax -> original, between: Lee w = exp(-K (Ci-Cu)/(Cmax-Ci)) mixes mean and pixel, Frost kernel exp(-K (Ci-Cu)/(Cmax-Ci) |d|); per channel

filters.name: Dark Structure Enhance
filters.note: after the PixInsight DarkStructureEnhance script, approx.: dark-structure mask = large-scale background (the wavelet residual; here a Gaussian of the structure scale) minus lightness, then the image is darkened through that mask
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p0));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p0));
vec3 o=O(uv).rgb;float l=luma(o),bg=luma(T(uv).rgb);float mk=clamp((bg-l)*u_p2,0.,1.);mk=mk*mk*(3.-2.*mk);if(u_p3>.5)return vec4(vec3(mk),1.);return vec4(o*(1.-u_p1*mk),1.);

filters.name: Range Selection Mask
filters.note: PixInsight RangeSelection: 1 between the lower and upper lightness limits, fuzziness = soft transition half-width, smoothness = Gaussian blur of the mask; lower > upper selects outside the range (invert)
passes: float l=luma(c.rgb);float lo=min(u_p0,u_p1),hi=max(u_p0,u_p1),fz=max(u_p2,1e-4);float m=smoothstep(lo-fz,lo+fz,l)*(1.-smoothstep(hi-fz,hi+fz,l));if(u_p0>u_p1)m=1.-m;return vec4(vec3(m),1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p3));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p3));

filters.name: Bataineh Binarization
filters.note: Bataineh, Abdullah & Omar 2011: T = m - m^2 s / ((M + s)(s_a + s)), m, s = window mean / std, M = global mean, s_a = (s - s_min)/(s_max - s_min); fixed window (the paper picks the window size per image), 11x11 sparse window, global stats from a 16x16 grid
passes: float r=R(u_p0*.5);float st=r/5.;float s=0.,s2=0.;for(int j=-5;j<=5;j++)for(int i=-5;i<=5;i++){float v=L(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*st*u_px);s+=v;s2+=v*v;}s/=121.;return vec4(s,sqrt(max(s2/121.-s*s,0.))*2.,0.,1.);

filters.name: Unpurple (Star Halo)
filters.note: after Siril Unpurple, approx.: star mask (luminance above local background) dilated to the halo radius; inside it the blue excess over green and the magenta (min(R,B) over G) excess are removed, so violet halos from refractor / filter chromatic aberration turn neutral

filters.name: Vector Ruggedness Measure (VRM)
filters.note: Sappington, Longshore & Thompson 2007: unit surface normals summed over the window, VRM = 1 - |sum|/n (0 = flat or uniform slope)
passes:

filters.name: Convergence Index
filters.note: Koethe & Lehmeier 1996 (SAGA Convergence Index): mean over 8 neighbours of (angle between the neighbour aspect and the direction to the centre) - 90 deg; negative = convergent (valleys, dark / blue), positive = divergent (ridges)
passes:
float dd=R(u_p0);float acc=0.;for(int k=0;k<8;k++){float an=float(k)*.7854;vec2 dv=vec2(cos(an),sin(an));vec2 g=sobelD(uv+dv*dd*u_px,max(dd*.5,1.));float lg=length(g);acc+=lg<1e-5?0.:acos(clamp(dot(-g/lg,-dv),-1.,1.))-1.5708;}

filters.name: Morphometric Features (Wood)
filters.note: Wood 1996 (GRASS r.param.scale): least-squares quadratic z = ax2+by2+cxy+dx+ey+f over the window; sloped cells by cross-sectional curvature (ridge / channel / planar), flat cells by max/min curvature (peak / pass / ridge / pit / channel / planar); colours: planar grey, pit black, channel blue, pass green, ridge yellow, peak red

filters.name: Geomorphons
filters.note: Jasiewicz & Stepinski 2013 (GRASS r.geomorphon): 8-direction line-of-sight zenith / nadir angles within the search radius -> ternary pattern (higher / lower / flat by the flatness threshold) -> 10 landforms from the (#lower, #higher) lookup table: flat, peak, ridge, shoulder, spur, slope, hollow, footslope, valley, pit (r.geomorphon colours)

filters.name: Deviation from Mean Elevation (DEV)

filters.name: Color Contrast (Lab a/b steepness)

filters.name: RGB Primaries (darktable)

filters.name: Nik Color Efex: Colour Filters (Bi-Color, Brilliance, Cross Balance, Foliage, Indian Summer, Skylight, Sunlight, Polarization, Reflector)

filters.name: Nik Color Efex: Colour Tools (Remove Color Cast, White Neutralizer, Color Stylizer, Contrast Color Range, Photo Stylizer, Ink, Paper Toner)

filters.name: Nik Color Efex: Contrast (Detail Extractor, Dark Contrasts, Pro Contrast, High Key, Low Key)
filters.note: DxO Nik Color Efex (user guide controls; Effect radius = size of the local-contrast surround): detail = luma minus Gaussian surround, amplified with a soft limit (strong edges compressed so fine detail gains most); Detail Extractor = detail amplified and the large-scale tone pulled toward middle grey (local tone balancing); Dark Contrasts = detail boost with denser (darkened, gamma) tones and slightly muted colour; Pro Contrast = automatic colour-cast correction (grey-world on a 12x12 grid) + automatic contrast stretch (grid min / max) + dynamic local contrast; High Key = brightened, flattened tones with soft glow of the light areas; Low Key = darkened tones with glowing highlights; Saturation applied last; approx.

filters.name: Procedural Noise III

filters.name: Sensor Pattern Noise (FPN / Banding / Amp Glow)

filters.name: Realistic Film Grain (Newson)

filters.name: Panini Projection (Unity / Unreal)

filters.name: Screen-Space Global Illumination

(single image + depth, the image taken as outgoing radiance): 12 cosine-weighted hemisphere rays per pixel ray-marched against the depth buffer; hit colours (weighted by the hit surface facing the ray) give one bounce of indirect light multiplied by the pixel albedo (chromaticity), misses add nothing and hits also occlude (soft AO term)

passes: if(0.>u_p0-.5)return c;vec2 o=vec2(0.5)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;return (T(uv+o)+T(uv-o)+T(uv+vec2(o.x,-o.y))+T(uv+vec2(-o.x,o.y)))*.25;

if(3.>u_p0-.5)return c;vec2 o=vec2(2.5)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;return (T(uv+o)+T(uv-o)+T(uv+vec2(o.x,-o.y))+T(uv+vec2(-o.x,o.y)))*.25;
if(4.>u_p0-.5)return c;vec2 o=vec2(3.5)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;return (T(uv+o)+T(uv-o)+T(uv+vec2(o.x,-o.y))+T(uv+vec2(-o.x,o.y)))*.25;
if(5.>u_p0-.5)return c;vec2 o=vec2(4.5)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;return (T(uv+o)+T(uv-o)+T(uv+vec2(o.x,-o.y))+T(uv+vec2(-o.x,o.y)))*.25;
if(6.>u_p0-.5)return c;vec2 o=vec2(4.5)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;return (T(uv+o)+T(uv-o)+T(uv+vec2(o.x,-o.y))+T(uv+vec2(-o.x,o.y)))*.25;
if(7.>u_p0-.5)return c;vec2 o=vec2(5.5)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;return (T(uv+o)+T(uv-o)+T(uv+vec2(o.x,-o.y))+T(uv+vec2(-o.x,o.y)))*.25;

filters.name: Dual Kawase Blur
filters.note: Bjorge 2015 (ARM, SIGGRAPH "Bandwidth-efficient rendering") dual filter: downsample = 4 x centre + 4 diagonal half-pixel taps / 8, upsample = 4 axis taps at 2 half-pixels + 4 diagonal taps x 2 / 12; approx.: the half-resolution pyramid is emulated at full resolution with the tap offsets doubled per level
passes: if(1.>u_p0+.5)return c;vec2 h=vec2(0.5)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;return (T(uv)*4.+T(uv+h)+T(uv-h)+T(uv+vec2(h.x,-h.y))+T(uv+vec2(-h.x,h.y)))/8.;

if(4.>u_p0+.5)return c;vec2 h=vec2(4)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;return (T(uv)*4.+T(uv+h)+T(uv-h)+T(uv+vec2(h.x,-h.y))+T(uv+vec2(-h.x,h.y)))/8.;
if(5.>u_p0+.5)return c;vec2 h=vec2(8)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;return (T(uv)*4.+T(uv+h)+T(uv-h)+T(uv+vec2(h.x,-h.y))+T(uv+vec2(-h.x,h.y)))/8.;
