if(2.>u_p0+.5)return c;vec2 h=vec2(1)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;vec4 s=T(uv+vec2(-h.x*2.,0.))+T(uv+vec2(h.x*2.,0.))+T(uv+vec2(0.,h.y*2.))+T(uv+vec2(0.,-h.y*2.));s+=(T(uv+h)+T(uv-h)+T(uv+vec2(h.x,-h.y))+T(uv+vec2(-h.x,h.y)))*2.;return s/12.;

if(1.>u_p0+.5)return c;vec2 h=vec2(0.5)*u_p1*u_k*u_px;vec4 s=T(uv+vec2(-h.x*2.,0.))+T(uv+vec2(h.x*2.,0.))+T(uv+vec2(0.,h.y*2.))+T(uv+vec2(0.,-h.y*2.));s+=(T(uv+h)+T(uv-h)+T(uv+vec2(h.x,-h.y))+T(uv+vec2(-h.x,h.y)))*2.;return s/12.;

filters.name: Circular Separable DOF (Garcia)
filters.note: Garcia 2017 (EA, "Circular separable convolution depth of field"), 1-component complex Gaussian kernel exp(-a x^2) e^(i b x^2), a = 0.862325, b = 1.624835, weights A = 0.767583, B = 1.862321 (Niemitalo), filter radius 1.2: horizontal complex pass + vertical complex pass per channel (R,G then B), Re/Im recombined into a disc; linear light with highlight boost; depth mode blends sharp/blurred by |depth - focus| (single-radius layer, approx.)

filters.name: Display Rendering Transform (OpenDRT / TCAMv2)
filters.note: approx.: the sRGB image is linearised and exposed as scene-linear, then a Daniele-Siragusano Michaelis-Menten tonescale (grey 0.18 -> 0.1 display, flare 0.01, Contrast = power) is applied. OpenDRT: on the RGB euclidean norm with RGB ratios kept and a path to white that grows with the tonescale; TCAMv2: on luminance with hue-preserving chroma scaled down in the highlights and limited to the display gamut (look approximation of FilmLight's DRT)

filters.name: Advanced Blur (albumentations)
filters.note: albumentations AdvancedBlur: generalised Gaussian kernel exp(-0.5 (d^T Sigma^-1 d)^beta) with anisotropic sigma X / Y rotated by the angle (beta < 1 heavy-tailed, > 1 plateau-shaped), every kernel weight multiplied by noise in 0.75..1.25 (seeded)

filters.name: Grid Elastic Deform (albumentations)
filters.note: albumentations GridElasticDeform: the image is cut into a Grid X x Grid Y mesh, interior vertices get random integer offsets in +-Magnitude px (border vertices fixed), and each output cell samples its distorted source quad bilinearly (PIL MeshTransform)

filters.name: H&E Stain Augmentation (albumentations HEStain)
filters.note: albumentations HEStain (method "matrix", Ruifrok & Johnston H&E vectors + orthogonal residual): RGB -> optical density -log((I+1)/256), stain concentrations by the inverse stain matrix, H and E concentrations scaled and shifted, reconstructed; background (bright, untissued) pixels kept as with augment_background = False (soft luminance mask, approx.)

filters.name: Policy Augment (RandAugment / TrivialAugment / AutoAugment / AugMix)
filters.note: torchvision policies over the PIL op set (Identity, ShearX/Y, TranslateX/Y, Rotate, Brightness, Color, Contrast, Sharpness, Posterize, Solarize, AutoContrast, Equalize, Invert; nearest sampling, black fill): RandAugment (N ops, magnitude bin of 31), TrivialAugmentWide (1 op, random bin, wide ranges), AutoAugment ImageNet policy (25 two-op sub-policies with probabilities), AugMix (3 chains of depth 1-3 at severity = Magnitude/3, Dirichlet(1) mixing weights, Beta(1,1) skip blend); randomness from the seed and Variant; approx.: image statistics for Contrast / AutoContrast / Equalize from a 16x16 sample grid, ignoring earlier geometric ops

filters.name: Random Linear / Gaussian Illumination (kornia)
filters.note: kornia RandomLinearIllumination (additive ramp 0..1 from the chosen side, gain x sign) and RandomGaussianIllumination (additive Gaussian of the given sigma in normalised coordinates, centre offset toward the chosen side); result clamped to 0..1

filters.name: Fast Snowy Landscape (imgaug)
filters.note: imgaug FastSnowyLandscape: RGB -> HLS, lightness below the threshold multiplied (clipped at 255), back to RGB - turns greens / greys of a landscape snow-white
passes: vec3 h=rgb2hsl(c.rgb);float L=h.z*255.;if(L<u_p0)h.z=min(L*u_p1,255.)/255.;return vec4(hsl2rgb(h),1.);

filters.name: Alpha Blend: Frequency Noise / Some Colors (imgaug)
filters.note: imgaug BlendAlphaFrequencyNoise / BlendAlphaSomeColors with a fixed foreground branch: frequency-noise mask = noise with amplitude ~ f^exponent on a grid of Noise size cells, linearly upscaled (approx.: octave sum instead of an inverse FFT, no random sigmoid); some-colors mask = hue split into N bins (random rotation) each randomly on / off, smoothed at the bin borders; alpha 1 = foreground

filters.name: Optical Bokeh (Lensbaby / Petzval / Cat's-eye / Onion / STF / Anamorphic / Coma)
filters.note: gathered lens PSFs (144 Vogel-spiral pupil samples, linear light, highlight boost): Lensbaby = sharp sweet spot with blur growing toward the edges (slightly radial); Petzval = background blur whose disc is squeezed radially toward the edges (tangential swirl); cat's-eye = aperture disc clipped by the shifted rear-element disc (shift grows with field radius); onion-ring = concentric ripple + bright rim from aspherical polishing marks; STF = Gaussian apodization filter (soft-edged discs); anamorphic = horizontally squeezed oval (squeeze 1 + amount); coma = third-order coma spot (rho^2 (2 + cos 2phi), rho^2 sin 2phi) growing linearly with field radius; approx.: PSF taken at the output pixel (gather)

filters.name: Pro-Mist Diffusion Filter
filters.note: diffusion filter as linear-light scattering of a fraction of the light into a wide Gaussian halo (strength 1 ~ grade 1/2 x 2): white Pro-Mist scatters everything (veiling glare lifts the blacks, lower contrast); Black Pro-Mist, whose black particles absorb part of the scatter, only adds the halo where it is brighter than the pixel (glow around highlights, blacks kept)
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Split Diopter
filters.note: split-field diopter: one side of the line (diopter half) is focused at Diopter focus depth, the other at the far background (depth 0.15); disc blur radius = Aperture x |depth - focus| (64-tap gather, linear light, approx.) with the soft blurred seam of the diopter edge

filters.name: Airy Disk Diffraction Blur
filters.note: Fraunhofer diffraction of a circular aperture: PSF (2 J1(x)/x)^2 with first zero at 1.22 lambda N (converted to pixels by the pixel pitch), per-channel wavelengths, convolved in linear light out to ~3 rings (J1 by the Numerical Recipes rational / asymptotic approximation)

filters.name: Stack Blur (Klingemann)
filters.note: Mario Klingemann 2004 StackBlur: separable triangular (tent) kernel of weights r + 1 - |i| per axis on the raw channel values (the stack is just an incremental way to compute it)
passes: float r=floor(R(u_p0)+.5);vec4 a=vec4(0.);float w=0.;for(int i=-64;i<=64;i++){float fi=float(i);if(abs(fi)>r)continue;float k=r+1.-abs(fi);a+=T(uv+vec2(fi,0.)*u_px)*k;w+=k;}return a/w;
float r=floor(R(u_p0)+.5);vec4 a=vec4(0.);float w=0.;for(int i=-64;i<=64;i++){float fi=float(i);if(abs(fi)>r)continue;float k=r+1.-abs(fi);a+=T(uv+vec2(0.,fi)*u_px)*k;w+=k;}return a/w;

filters.name: Sensor Dust Spots
filters.note: shadows of dust on the sensor cover glass: each particle is a disc whose shadow is blurred by the light cone (blur width ~ 1/f-number), so stopped down the spots are small, dark and crisp (irregular outline) and wide open they spread into faint large rings; multiplicative in linear light (absorbed light conserved: peak opacity ~ a^2 / (a + b)^2)

filters.name: Mobius Transformation
filters.note: w = e^(i theta) (z - a) / (1 - conj(a) z), the Mobius map that is an automorphism of the unit disc (unit circle = image height), inverted per output pixel; a = pole (the point sent to the centre), zoom on the output; outside the frame the image is mirror-tiled

filters.name: Map Projections (Mercator / Mollweide / ...)
filters.note: exact map projections with the image taken as an equirectangular (plate carree) world map, or (reverse) as a full-frame map in the chosen projection: Mercator y = ln tan(pi/4 + phi/2) cut at the max latitude; Mollweide (auxiliary angle by Newton); Lambert cylindrical equal-area; sinusoidal; Hammer-Aitoff; orthographic globe tilted by the latitude parameter; Equal Earth (Savric, Patterson & Jenny 2018 polynomial); central meridian shifts longitudes, the forward map is fitted uniformly into the frame

filters.name: Inverse Perspective Mapping (Bird's-Eye)
filters.note: IPM: the image is a pinhole view (given vertical FOV) of a flat ground plane from a camera at height 1 pitched down by the given angle; each output pixel is a ground point (X, Z), Z from the nearest visible ground to View range further, projected back into the image (homography); parts not seen by the camera are black

filters.name: Log-Polar Transform
filters.note: OpenCV warpPolar with WARP_POLAR_LOG: radius along x as rho = Kmag ln r, Kmag = width / ln(maxRadius) (maxRadius = farthest corner), angle 0..360 deg down the rows; reverse = WARP_INVERSE_MAP

filters.name: Mustache Distortion (Brown-Conrady)
filters.note: Brown-Conrady radial lens model r_d = r_u (1 + k1 r_u^2 + k2 r_u^4) (r = 1 at the corner): the image is the undistorted scene, each output pixel inverts the model by Newton iteration; k1 < 0 with k2 > 0 = mustache (barrel in the centre, pincushion toward the edges); Scale zooms the output

filters.name: Gravitational Lensing
filters.note: thin-lens equation beta = theta - alpha(theta): point mass alpha = theta_E^2 theta / |theta|^2 (Einstein ring at theta_E, two images per source), singular isothermal sphere alpha = theta_E theta / |theta|; the image is the background source plane (mirror-tiled outside the frame)

filters.name: Fluted (Reeded) Glass
filters.note: reeded / fluted glass panel: parallel convex cylindrical ribs, each refracting by the slope of its circular profile (each rib shows a compressed, edge-reversed slice of the scene), frost = random scatter; with soft shading, a specular streak per rib and dark seams (approx.)

filters.name: Frames II (Negative Carrier / Deckle / Mat / Stamp)
filters.note: negative carrier = filed-out carrier print: film rebate prints as a black band with rough, irregular inner and outer edges on white paper; deckle edge = torn / deckled paper with a white margin on a dark ground (Tone = ground lightness); passe-partout = mat board (Tone = board lightness) with a 45-degree bevelled window showing the white core lit from the top-left and a soft shadow on the picture; postage stamp = white stamp margin with a frame line and perforation holes on a dark ground; the picture is scaled (cropped) to fit inside

filters.name: Letterbox / Pillarbox Bars
filters.note: cinema aspect masking: bars (grey level and opacity adjustable, default opaque black) cover the image outside the target aspect ratio - letterbox when the target is wider than the image, pillarbox when narrower
passes:
int a=int(u_p0+.5);float ta=a==0?2.39:a==1?2.:a==2?1.85:a==3?16./9.:a==4?4./3.:1.;float ia=asp();vec2 box=ta>ia?vec2(1.,ia/ta):vec2(ta/ia,1.);vec2 d=abs(uv-.5)*2.;
  if(d.x>box.x||d.y>box.y)return vec4(mix(c.rgb,vec3(u_p1),u_p2),1.);return c;

filters.name: Glint (Nuke)
filters.note: Nuke Glint: star-shaped rays (one-sided, evenly spaced from Rotation) grow out of every pixel brighter than Tolerance, fading quadratically over Length, added to the image (rays combined by maximum, not summed); gathered from a lightly blurred bright pass (approx. of the from/to colour ramp: rays keep the source colour)
passes: vec3 o=O(uv).rgb;return vec4(o*smoothstep(u_p2,min(u_p2+.12,1.001),luma(o)),1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p1/40.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p1/40.));

filters.name: EdgeBlur (Nuke)
filters.note: Nuke EdgeBlur: blurs the image only in a band around the matte edges (band = where the blurred matte is neither 0 nor 1, widened by Edge mult); the matte is made from a channel threshold because the images here have no alpha
passes: vec3 o=O(uv).rgb;int s=int(u_p2+.5);float v=s==0?luma(o):s==1?o.r:s==2?o.g:s==3?o.b:rgb2hsv(o).y;return vec4(o,smoothstep(u_p3-.03,u_p3+.03,v));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p0));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p0));
vec4 b=T(uv);float z=clamp((1.-abs(2.*b.a-1.))*u_p1,0.,1.);return vec4(mix(O(uv).rgb,b.rgb,z),1.);

filters.name: Log2Lin (Nuke, Cineon)
filters.note: Nuke Log2Lin Cineon formula: lin = (10^((code - white) 0.002 / gamma) - offset) / (1 - offset), offset = 10^((black - white) 0.002 / gamma), code = value x 1023 (defaults 95 / 685 / 0.6); Log to Lin shows the linear result through an sRGB view transform, Lin to Log decodes sRGB to linear and writes raw log code values

filters.name: Toe (Nuke)
filters.note: Nuke Toe: lifts black (0 -> Lift) with a rolloff so whites stay put; approx.: out = in + lift (1 - in)^rolloff in linear light (Nuke does not publish its curve)

filters.name: HueCorrect (Nuke)
filters.note: Nuke HueCorrect with one curve point: a raised-cosine bump (Hue, Width) on the chosen curve (1 = identity); sat / lum / r / g / b multiply, the suppress curves limit that channel toward max of the other two (despill) as the value drops below 1; weighted down for near-grey pixels

filters.name: Glare (Blender: Streaks / Fog Glow / Ghosts)
filters.note: Blender Glare node (mix 0 = image + glare, in linear light): threshold keeps luminance >= Threshold, minus threshold (normalised here and scaled by Strength since 8-bit images never exceed 1); Streaks = n directions, each a one-sided exponential tail (Blender iterates taps at 4^k spacing with weight fade^d: the same kernel, gathered here) with colour modulation; Fog Glow = Blender kernel exp(-9 (scale r^2)^(1/8)) x raised-cosine window over 2 x Size, polar-sampled; Ghosts = blurred highlights mirrored / scaled through the centre with tints (approx. scale set)
passes: vec3 l=mix(c.rgb/12.92,pow((c.rgb+.055)/1.055,vec3(2.4)),step(vec3(.04045),c.rgb));float th=u_p1;float tl=th<=.04045?th/12.92:pow((th+.055)/1.055,2.4);vec3 b=luma(l)>=tl?max(l-tl,0.)/max(1.-tl,.02):vec3(0.);return vec4(b*u_p3,1.);

filters.name: Box Sharpen / Mean Removal
filters.note: Blender Filter node Box Sharpen = Krita Mean Removal: 3x3 kernel (-1 x 8, centre 9), Factor mixes with the input (Diamond Sharpen = the 5-point kernel of Sharpen)
passes: vec2 p=u_px;vec3 s=c.rgb*9.;for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){if(i==0&&j==0)continue;s-=T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*p).rgb;}return vec4(clamp(mix(c.rgb,s,u_p0),0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Anti-Aliasing (SMAA / FXAA)
filters.note: SMAA 1x as in Blender's Anti-Aliasing node, approx.: luma edge detection with local contrast adaptation (exact SMAA rule: edge kept if contrast limit x delta >= max neighbouring delta), edge-end search (16 px each way) and crossing-edge classification, but the pattern areas are integrated analytically (line through the crossing-edge midpoints, U shapes split at the middle) instead of the precomputed area texture, no diagonal / corner-rounding passes; FXAA 3.11 quality preset (12-step search, subpixel 0.75, threshold = edge threshold)

filters.name: Rh Simple Tone Map (Blender)
filters.note: Blender Tonemap node, Rh Simple (Reinhard): al = key / exp(mean log luminance) (16x16 sample grid), p = c al, p / (p + offset), then ^(1/gamma); computed on the linearised image
passes:
float ls=0.;for(int j=0;j<16;j++)for(int i=0;i<16;i++){vec3 q=O((vec2(float(i),float(j))+.5)/16.).rgb;vec3 lq=mix(q/12.92,pow((q+.055)/1.055,vec3(2.4)),step(vec3(.04045),q));ls+=log(luma(lq)+1e-5);}
  float al=u_p0/exp(ls/256.);vec3 l=mix(c.rgb/12.92,pow((c.rgb+.055)/1.055,vec3(2.4)),step(vec3(.04045),c.rgb))*al;l/=l+u_p1;l=pow(max(l,vec3(0.)),vec3(1./max(u_p2,.01)));return vec4(mix(clamp(l,0.,1.)*12.92,1.055*pow(max(clamp(l,0.,1.),vec3(0.)),vec3(1./2.4))-.055,step(vec3(.0031308),clamp(l,0.,1.))),1.);

filters.name: Alien Map (GEGL)
filters.note: GEGL alien-map: out = 0.5 (1 + sin((2 in - 1) freq pi + phase)) per channel on non-linear RGB or on H, S, L; one frequency for all channels, phases = shift + k x step
passes:
vec3 x=u_p0<.5?c.rgb:rgb2hsl(c.rgb);vec3 ph=radians(vec3(u_p2,u_p2+u_p3,u_p2+2.*u_p3));vec3 y=.5*(1.+sin((2.*x-1.)*u_p1*PI+ph));
  if(u_p0>.5)y=hsl2rgb(vec3(fract(y.x),y.y,y.z));return vec4(clamp(y,0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Color Enhance (GEGL)
filters.note: GEGL color-enhance: in CIE LCh(ab) the chroma is stretched so the image's minimum maps to 0 and maximum to 100 (lightness and hue kept); min / max from a 16x16 sample grid, D65 Lab

filters.name: Predator (GIMP)
filters.note: GIMP Script-Fu Predator: Sobel edge detect (per channel, x amount) -> optional pixelize -> Maximum RGB (only the largest channel kept) -> edge detect again
passes:
vec2 p=u_px;vec3 tl=T(uv+vec2(-p.x,p.y)).rgb,t=T(uv+vec2(0.,p.y)).rgb,tr=T(uv+p).rgb,l=T(uv-vec2(p.x,0.)).rgb,r=T(uv+vec2(p.x,0.)).rgb,bl=T(uv-p).rgb,b=T(uv-vec2(0.,p.y)).rgb,br=T(uv+vec2(p.x,-p.y)).rgb;
   vec3 gx=(tr+2.*r+br)-(tl+2.*l+bl),gy=(tl+2.*t+tr)-(bl+2.*b+br);return vec4(clamp(sqrt(gx*gx+gy*gy)*u_p0*.25,0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Inverse Gaussian Gradient (scikit-image)
filters.note: skimage.segmentation.inverse_gaussian_gradient: 1/sqrt(1 + alpha·|∇(G_sigma * I)|) with scipy gaussian_gradient_magnitude (Gaussian-derivative kernels truncated at 4 sigma, nearest border) — the edge-stopping map for morphological geodesic active contours

filters.name: Tubeness (Fiji)
filters.note: Fiji Tubeness (Sato et al. 1998, TubenessProcessor 2-D): Hessian of the Gaussian-smoothed image (kernel 2·int(3σ+.5)+1, [1,−2,1] and 4-corner differences, scaled by σ² as in ComputeCurvatures); tubeness = |λ| of the larger-magnitude eigenvalue when it is negative, else 0. Values in 0..1 image units (Fiji 8-bit = ×255)

filters.name: Objectness Measure (ITK, Antiga)
filters.note: ITK HessianToObjectnessMeasureImageFilter (Antiga 2007) on a Gaussian-derivative Hessian at sigma: eigenvalues sorted by magnitude, sign constraint for bright/dark, R_A (blobs) or R_B (lines) term with alpha = beta = 0.5, structureness 1−exp(−S²/2γ²), ScaleObjectnessMeasure on (× largest |λ|); display = value × σ² × gain; γ in 8-bit units

filters.name: Directional Filtering (MorphoLibJ)
filters.note: MorphoLibJ Directional Filtering (Heneghan 2002 style): the operation along an oriented line structuring element (MorphoLibJ OrientedLineStrel pixel shifts: major-axis steps, rounded minor offsets, half-length round((L·max(|cos|,|sin|)−1)/2)) at nDirections angles i·180°/n, combined by max or min; on luma. Opening/closing use one sampled line of 4·half+1 pixels with sliding-window min/max (approx. — exact for axis-aligned and diagonal lines, ±1 px rounding otherwise)

filters.name: Shape Index / Curvedness (Koenderink)
filters.note: skimage.feature.shape_index (Koenderink & van Doorn 1992): s = (2/π)·arctan((λ2+λ1)/(λ2−λ1)) from the Hessian of the Gaussian-smoothed image (truncate 4σ, np.gradient twice); curvedness C = sqrt((λ1²+λ2²)/2) (shown × σ² × gain). Grey: −1 black (cup) … +1 white (cap); flat (NaN in skimage) = 0.5

filters.name: Multiscale Basic Features (scikit-image)
filters.note: one channel of skimage.feature.multiscale_basic_features at one sigma (sigma_min 0.5 … here up to 8): intensity = gaussian(img, sigma), edges = filters.sobel of it (sqrt((h²+v²)/2), [1,2,1]/4 ⊗ [1,0,−1]), texture = Hessian eigenvalues from np.gradient twice; eigenvalues shown as 0.5 + value × σ² × gain; on luma

filters.name: Peak Local Max (scikit-image)
filters.note: skimage.feature.peak_local_max as a mask: pixel == maximum_filter(size 2·min_distance+1) and > max(image min, threshold_rel × image max), exclude_border = min_distance; a peak is dropped when an equal-valued candidate earlier in row-major order lies within min_distance (approx. of the greedy ensure_spacing); global min/max by a two-pass block reduction; optional Gaussian pre-blur (0 = exact on luma)

filters.name: Remove Outliers (ImageJ)
filters.note: ImageJ Process › Noise › Remove Outliers (RankFilters OUTLIERS): circular kernel exactly as ImageJ (r² → int(r²)+1, radius 1.5→1.75 and 2.5→2.85 quirks), exact median per RGB channel (bisection + snap), a pixel is replaced by the median when it is brighter (or darker) than median ± threshold; threshold in 8-bit levels

filters.name: edgetaper (MATLAB)
filters.note: MATLAB edgetaper(I, PSF) with a Gaussian PSF (size 2·ceil(3σ)+1): J = α·I + (1−α)·(I ⊛ PSF) with circular (wrap-around) convolution, α = (1 − z_x)(1 − z_y), z = normalised autocorrelation of the PSF projection at the circular distance to the frame edge — prepares an image for FFT deconvolution; the final clip to [min I, max I] is a no-op for this convex blend

filters.name: bwmorph hbreak / bridge (MATLAB)
filters.note: MATLAB bwmorph(BW, "hbreak") — removes the centre of H-connected 3×3 patterns (both orientations) — and bwmorph(BW, "bridge") — sets a 0 pixel to 1 when its 8 neighbours form two or more unconnected 8-connected groups; one iteration (n = 1); highlighted: added red, removed blue

filters.name: PIQE Quality Map (MATLAB)
filters.note: MATLAB piqe (Venkatanath et al. 2015) block masks: grey = 8-bit rgb2gray rescaled to 0..255 by the image max (two-pass block reduction; exact up to 512 px, sub-sampled above), MSCN with a 7×7 Gaussian (σ 7/6, C = 1); 16×16 blocks (symmetric padding): active if MSCN variance > 0.1; noticeable artifact if any 6-pixel edge segment has std < 0.1; noise if block σ > 2β (centre columns 8–9 vs surround std ratio); block score = artifact·(1−var) + noise·var

filters.name: Rank Filters: Autolevel / Contrast / Bilateral Mean (scikit-image)
filters.note: skimage.filters.rank on a disk(r) footprint: autolevel = (g − local min)/(local max − local min); enhance_contrast = local max if the pixel is closer to the max than to the min, else local min; mean_bilateral = mean of the footprint values strictly within (g − s0, g + s1) (s in 8-bit levels); skimage works on 8-bit grey — here float, per RGB channel or on luma

filters.name: Bounded Reciprocal (ITK)
filters.note: ITK BoundedReciprocalImageFilter: out = 1/(1 + x) per channel (x = value × input scale; scale 255 treats the image as 8-bit); optional stretch of the [1/(1+scale), 1] output range to 0..1
passes: vec3 y=1./(1.+max(c.rgb,0.)*u_p0);if(u_p1>.5){float lo=1./(1.+u_p0);y=(y-lo)/(1.-lo);}return vec4(y,1.);

filters.name: Voting Binary Hole Filling (ITK)
filters.note: ITK VotingBinaryHoleFillingImageFilter (one iteration): a background pixel becomes foreground when at least (N−1)/2 + majority of the N−1 neighbours in the (2r+1)² box are foreground; foreground pixels are kept; input binarised at the threshold

filters.name: DCT Denoising (OpenCV, Yu-Sapiro)
filters.note: OpenCV xphoto::dctDenoising (Yu & Sapiro, IPOL 2011): RGB → orthonormal opponent space, sliding 8×8 DCT patches (OpenCV default psize is 16), coefficients with |c| ≤ 3·sigma zeroed, inverse DCT, all overlapping patch estimates averaged; sigma in 8-bit levels; the fast mode averages 16 of the 64 shifts (approx.)

filters.name: Bilateral Texture Filter (OpenCV)
filters.note: OpenCV ximgproc::bilateralTextureFilter (Cho, Lee, Kang & Lee 2014), one iteration: box mean B and modified relative total variation mRTV per (2fr+1)² patch, guidance G = B of the min-mRTV patch containing the pixel (OpenCV scan order), blended with B by α = 2(sigmoid(σα·ΔmRTV) − 0.5), then a joint bilateral filter (radius 2fr, spatial σ = 2fr, range σ_avg) of the image guided by it

filters.name: Paillou Gradient (OpenCV)
filters.note: OpenCV ximgproc GradientPaillouX / GradientPaillouY (Paillou 1997 SAR step-edge operator): the causal + anticausal 2nd-order recursions (poles e^(−α±ω)) applied as their exact impulse responses, truncated where they fall below 1e-4 (border handling differs from the recursion start values); derivative along one axis, Paillou smoothing along the other; on luma; omega < alpha

filters.name: Weighted Median Filter (OpenCV)
filters.note: OpenCV ximgproc::weightedMedianFilter with the image as its own joint image: per RGB channel the weighted median over the (2r+1)² box, weights from the colour difference to the centre (WMF_EXP exp(−|Δ|²/2σ²), IV1 1/(|Δ|₁+σ), IV2 1/(|Δ|²+σ²), COS, JAC, OFF); sigma in 0..1 units (OpenCV 25.5 = 0.1). OpenCV clusters the joint colours into 256 k-means centres and quantises values to 256 levels — here exact colours (approx. of that quantisation)

filters.name: BrightEdges (OpenCV)

filters.name: Sum-Modified Laplacian (SML)
filters.note: Nayar & Nakagawa 1994 shape-from-focus measure: modified Laplacian ML = |2I − I(x−s) − I(x+s)| + |2I − I(y−s) − I(y+s)|, summed over the (2N+1)² window where ML ≥ T; shown as window mean × gain (inferno)

filters.name: Warper (ResolveFX)
filters.note: ResolveFX Warper (point warp), approx.: one control point dragged from (X, Y) by (Drag X, Drag Y) with the frame border pinned; displacement field = Shepard inverse-distance² blend of the drag and the zero border, sampled backwards from the destination

filters.name: photon-rs Filter Presets
filters.note: photon-rs filters.rs ported on 8-bit values: mix_with_colour (out = colour*opacity + px*(1-opacity), truncated) for Oceanic/Islands/Marine/Seagreen/Flagblue (0.2), Diamante (0.1), Perfume, Serenity; Golden = mix(235,145,50,.2)+adjust_contrast 30; Pastel Pink = alter_channels(80,12,20)+contrast 30; Cali = mix(255,45,75,.1)+contrast 50; Firenze = mix(255,47,78,.1)+inc_brightness 30+contrast 50; Cinematic = contrast 35, amber mix .12, film_grain .15 (midtone-weighted, per channel; hash instead of XorShift32), vignette .65 (1 - d^2/dmax^2); Radio/Twenties/Rosetint/Mauve/Bluechrome = monochrome(avg + offsets 5,40,20 / 18,12,20 / 80,20,31 / 90,40,80 / 20,30,60); Obsidian = average grey + contrast 25. adjust_contrast factor = 259(c+255)/(255(259-c))

filters.name: photon-rs Channel Effects (Neue / Lix / Ryo / Primary)
filters.note: photon-rs filters.rs / effects.rs: neue = 255 - blue where blue < 255; lix = invert red and green; ryo = invert red and blue; primary = each channel > 128 -> 255 else 0. Upstream primary() reads pixel 0 for every pixel (whole image becomes one colour) and its blue branch sets green to 255 while leaving blue unchanged; "upstream quirk" keeps the blue/green quirk but evaluates per pixel

filters.name: photon-rs Horizontal / Vertical Strips
filters.note: photon-rs effects.rs horizontal_strips / color_horizontal_strips (and the vertical twins): the frame is cut into 2n-1 slots of floor(H/(2n-1)) px and the strips are painted in the strip colour. Alternating = every second slot (the documented "series of equal-width strips"); upstream code = what draw_horizontal_strips actually paints, slots 1..n-1 at i*height_strip, i.e. one contiguous block

filters.name: VEGAS Black Restore / Fill Light / Soft Contrast
filters.note: VEGAS Pro plug-ins (manual): Black Restore = any colour whose weighted RGB average (BT.601) is below Threshold (Amount x 0.25) is set to black (exact rule); Fill Light = shadow fill weighted by a blurred luminance mask (Softness = diffusion radius, Balance = deviation, negative lights darker regions more), applied as 1-(1-x)^(1+k) so whites never clip (approx.; tint hue not exposed); Soft Contrast = stretch range + S-curve contrast with low/high trim (Balance <0 lifts darks, >0 holds highlights) and diffusion of the blurred highlights (approx.; the vignette tab is not included)

filters.name: VEGAS Min and Max
filters.note: VEGAS Min and Max: every pixel takes the darkest (Min) or brightest (Max) pixel, chosen by BT.601 brightness, of the Horizontal x Vertical range around it (square or circular area); Fixed blocks applies the same choice once per block, the pixelate reading of the manual

filters.name: VEGAS Radial Pixelate
filters.note: VEGAS Radial Pixelate: pixelation in polar coordinates about Center (0,0 = lower left): Radial = the angle is quantised into sectors so colours streak outward from the centre in straight lines, Circular = the radius is quantised into concentric rings; Level = cell size (approx. of the plug-in scale)

filters.name: VEGAS TV Simulator
filters.note: VEGAS TV Simulator (manual controls, approx.): aperture grill = vertical RGB phosphor stripes, interlacing = alternate 2-line bands darkened, static = per-pixel random snow; Disturbance picks one of line sync (row jitter + waving), vertical sync (rolled frame with a black blanking bar), scan phasing (rolling light band) and phosphorescence (blue phosphor glow); detail zoom fixed at 1; seeded

filters.name: VEGAS Cookie Cutter
filters.note: VEGAS Cookie Cutter: a centred shape (circle, oval, square, diamond, triangles - signed-distance shapes) with feathered edge; "cut everything apart from section" keeps the video inside the shape, "cut section" removes it; optional white border band; the cut-away area is black here (transparent in VEGAS); repeat X/Y and centre not exposed

filters.name: ImageMagick -function Arcsin / Arctan
filters.note: ImageMagick ApplyFunction (statistic.c), per channel, bias 0.5: Arcsin width,center,range: t = 2/width*(v-center), out = range/pi*asin(t)+bias, pegged at bias +- range/2 outside |t|<1; Arctan slope,center,range: out = range/pi*atan(pi*slope*(v-center))+bias

filters.name: ImageMagick -range-threshold
filters.note: ImageMagick RangeThresholdImage (threshold.c): on the pixel intensity (Rec.709 luma, IM default) - 0 below low-black, linear ramp up to low-white, 1 up to high-white, linear ramp down to 0 at high-black, 0 above (a soft band-pass threshold)

filters.name: ImageMagick -white-threshold / -color-threshold
filters.note: ImageMagick threshold.c: WhiteThresholdImage - pixels whose intensity (Rec.709 luma) exceeds the threshold become white, others unchanged (per channel when a channel mask is set); ColorThresholdImage start-stop - pixels with every channel inside the [start,stop] RGB box become white, all others black. The box is given here by a named preset (start/stop sRGB colours) that Widen grows or shrinks

filters.name: ImageMagick Peaks Kernel (Hit-and-Miss)
filters.note: ImageMagick -morphology HitAndMiss Peaks:r1,r2 (morphology.c): kernel = centre pixel foreground, ring of pixels with r1^2 < u^2+v^2 <= r2^2 background (default ring 7 < d^2 <= 11); grey hit-and-miss = min(foreground) - max(background), never negative, per channel; Gain scales the (usually faint) response, Valleys runs it on the negated image

filters.name: Topaz Precision Contrast
filters.note: Topaz Studio 2 Precision Contrast (approx.): luminance split into a Gaussian band stack (sigma 1.5 / 5 / 16 px): micro, small and medium bands are amplified with a magnitude-dependent gain d*(1+3a/(1+10|d|)) so strong edges get little extra (no halos), negative values flatten a band; High contrast is a soft S-curve on the base layer; the luminance change is added to RGB

filters.name: Topaz Precision Detail
filters.note: Topaz Studio 2 Precision Detail (approx. of Topaz Detail): luminance band stack (sigma 0.8 / 2.5 / 7 px) with small, medium and large detail sliders; Detail mode = gain softly limited on strong edges, Boost = gain concentrated on low-amplitude detail (weak texture lifted, strong edges left alone); negative values soften that band

filters.name: Topaz Edge Exposure
filters.note: Topaz Studio 2 Edge Exposure (approx.): exposure change in EV applied in linear light along the frame edges - all four, top and bottom, left and right, top, bottom or an elliptical vignette - with Edge size = band width and Transition = softness of the ramp; negative darkens (drama), positive brightens (light leak)

filters.name: Topaz Radiance
filters.note: Topaz Studio 2 Radiance (approx. from the product description): image contours (Sobel magnitude x sensitivity, smoothstep) coloured by the saturated image, diffused by a Gaussian of Diffusion px and screened over the photo (Light: glowing, neon-like contours) or multiplied in as shadow (Dark: somber fibre webs)
passes:
float e=clamp(length(sobel(uv))*u_p3*.5,0.,1.);e=e*e*(3.-2.*e);vec3 col=T(uv).rgb;vec3 s=clamp(mix(vec3(luma(col)),col,1.6),0.,1.);
   return vec4(u_p0<.5?(s*.6+.4)*e:vec3(e),1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: uberOOZE (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge uberOOZE by uberzev (approx. from its controls Distortion, Intricacy, Smoothness, Shading): a domain-warped multi-octave noise height field (Intricacy = scale and octaves, Smoothness = lower persistence) whose gradient refracts the image like a layer of runny goo, lit with diffuse + specular shading from the same field; seeded

filters.name: sphere town (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge sphere town by voldemort ("spherical deform of your photo without a height map", controls Repeat / Curve Sector / Invert; approx.): inside a centred disc the radius is mapped through a sphere profile (asin, Curve = amount), repeated Repeat times with mirrored rings and optionally folded into angular sectors, then shaded as a glossy ball over a dimmed background

filters.name: Marbled Papers (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge Marbled Papers by ThreeDee (approx.): the image is combed like ink on a marbling bath with three rakes, inverted in reverse order - Rake 1 vertical tines alternately pulling up/down, Rake 2 horizontal tines pulling sideways, Rake 3 a wavy (sinusoidal) stroke; each tine uses the Jaffer-Lu tine-line displacement A*lambda/(d+lambda), which keeps distance to the line so the inverse is exact; mirrored edges

filters.name: Lens Diffusion (BCC+ Net / Silk / Center Spot / Low Contrast)
filters.note: BCC+ (DFT 55mm-style) optical diffusion filters: Net = diffusion mixed into the image by opacity with soft highlight halos; Silk = edge-aware (bilateral) smoothing of fine detail; Center Spot = sharp central spot, blurred surround; Low Contrast = light from bright areas spread into the shadows (blurred highlights added to dark tones). Colour-correct / warming groups omitted
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Smear Blur (BCC+)
filters.note: BCC+ Smear Blur: pixels smeared forward and backward along Z (zoom from scale 1−Scale to 1+Scale) with an optional spiral rotation about the centre; 41 taps, edge mode Repeat

filters.name: Tone Tools (BCC+ F Stop / Fluorescent / High Contrast / Selective Saturation / Flashing / Reflector / Color Infrared)
filters.note: BCC+ colour & tone tools. F Stop: exposure in stops (Amount×2) in linear light, weighted to a tonal band (Position ± Range; Range 1 ≈ global). Fluorescent: removes the fluorescent green cast (red + blue up, green down, luminance kept). High Contrast: normalised sigmoid about Position, Amount = contrast + mix. Selective Saturation: saturation × (1 + 2·Amount) in the tonal band. Flashing: lab flashing — shadows lifted with a warm flash colour, whites softened (negative = reverse). Reflector: silver / gold bounce light added to shadow tones selected by Position / Range. Color Infrared: false-colour CIR film (R ← near-IR estimated from foliage green, G ← red, B ← green), Range = contrast, Position = hue shift (approx.)

filters.name: Grads & Tints (BCC+ Gels / Dual Gradient / Radial Tint / Color Spot / Radial Exposure)
filters.note: BCC+ grads & tints as photographic colour filters (multiply by the filter colour with exposure compensation, highlights preserved). Gels: whole-frame gel. Dual Gradient: Hue on top, complementary hue at the bottom, transition band = Size. Radial Tint: four quadrant colours (Hue + 0/90/180/270°) as a radial gradient growing outward. Color Spot: tint everywhere except a clear central spot (negative Amount = inverted spot). Radial Exposure: ± 2 stops outside the central spot (vignette / anti-vignette). Gradient corner pins omitted

filters.name: Lights (BCC+ Key Light / Eye Light / Overexpose / BCC Reverse Spotlight)
filters.note: BCC+ Key Light: relight in linear light, point type (+Strength stops at the light, −Strength far away) or parallel type (directional ramp, direction = centre → light point). Eye Light: soft elliptical catch-light screened at the point, surround slightly darkened. Overexpose: over-exposed film look (exposure boost + blurred highlight bleed, soft-clipped, slightly desaturated). Reverse Spotlight: ambient lowered and a soft elliptical spotlit region at the point (edge-light group omitted; approx.)
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(14.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(14.));

filters.name: Glows (BCC+ Film Glow / Colorize Glow / Glow Alpha Edges / Atmospheric Glow)
filters.note: BCC+ Film Glow: thresholded highlights blurred (Gaussian, Radius) and screened (Glow Apply Mode default Screen). Colorize Glow: luma glow map tinted with a gradient (inferno-type fire preset) and screened. Glow Alpha Edges: the luma-keyed shape (key = Threshold; dark shapes when the image is mostly bright) glows outward under the image (Apply Mode Under; gold glow colour so it shows on white too). Atmospheric Glow: film glow + volumetric rays from the upper centre + fog + vignette + grain (flicker / orbs / animation omitted)
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Rays (BCC Rays Puffy / Rays Radiant Edges)
filters.note: BCC Rays: light built from the image (Puffy: luma above a soft threshold, image colours; Radiant Edges: Sobel edges tinted warm) is smeared radially toward the light source (48-tap decaying march + 16-tap smoothing) and screened over the source; "fat" = rays from a blurred source (less distinct). String/shimmer textures omitted
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R((mod(u_p0,2.)>.5?7.:0.)));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R((mod(u_p0,2.)>.5?7.:0.)));
vec2 lp=vec2(u_p2,1.-u_p3);vec3 acc=vec3(0.);float w=0.;for(int i=0;i<48;i++){float t=float(i)/48.;float k=1.-t;acc+=T(mix(uv,lp,t*u_p1)).rgb*k;w+=k;}return vec4(acc/w,1.);

vec2 lp=vec2(u_p2,1.-u_p3);vec3 acc=vec3(0.);for(int i=0;i<16;i++){float t=float(i)/16.;acc+=T(mix(uv,lp,t*u_p1*.08)).rgb;}acc/=16.;
 int m=int(u_p0+.5);vec3 o=O(uv).rgb;float gain=m<2?2.2:1.5;return vec4(clamp(screen(o,clamp(acc*gain,0.,1.)),0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Optical Elements (BCC+ Ice Halos / Multi-Star / Chroma Bands / Orbs)
filters.note: BCC+ optical elements placed at the brightest point of the image (16×16 search, matte placement approx.), screened over the image. Ice Halos: 22° halo (red inner edge), faint 46° halo, upper tangent arc, parhelia (sundogs; distance grows with sun altitude) and parhelic circle. Multi-Star: 4/6/8-spoke star streaks from the highlight matte, rotated by Angle. Chroma Bands: rainbow diffraction rings with ray texture (Angle rotates). Orbs: random soft bokeh orbs with brighter rims around the light (Angle = density; seed varies layout; no motion/flicker)

filters.name: Color Stylize (BCC Artists Poster / Color Choker / Color Shadow / Multitone Mix / RGB Edges)
filters.note: BCC stylize looks on a pre-blurred image. Artists Poster: each channel thresholded → the 8 pure colours (RGBCMYKW) pulled to NTSC-safe levels, Variant = colour soften. Color Choker: per-channel posterize to 3+Variant levels with a choke softness (Threshold) on the blurred image. Color Shadow: high-contrast threshold image with a top→bottom two-colour gradient over a background colour (Variant = palette). Multitone Mix: luma mapped through black / colour 1 / midpoint / colour 3 / white (Threshold = midpoint level, Variant = palette). RGB Edges: directional edges found per RGB channel independently (light direction 45° + 60°·Variant, Threshold = edge floor) added to the source
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Noise & Scatter (BCC Spray Paint Noise / RGB PixelNoise / Scatterize / Edge Grunge)
filters.note: BCC Spray Paint Noise: Amount = share of pixels covered by flat paint specks (colour hue = Angle) with random opacity 35–100 %. RGB PixelNoise: Amount = share of pixels, Size/60 = noise amplitude, independent per channel or luma-only, clipped. Scatterize: Amount = scatter percentage, Size = variance, uncontrolled / directional (Angle) / radial from the centre. Edge Grunge: the frame edge (no alpha) eroded by Size with a grunge fBm texture, burn coloured in 4 bands (yellow → orange → red → brown) with an outer glow (approx.)

filters.name: Multi-Shadow / Edge Lighting (BCC)
filters.note: BCC Multi Shadow: three drop shadows (distance ×1/×2/×3, angles Angle / +15° / −15°, black / dark blue / dark red, opacity 65/40/25 %, blurred by Softness) cast by a luma key, luma-inverse key or cartoon edges; the opaque source stays in front (shadows fall on non-subject pixels). BCC Edge Lighting: highlights and shadows along edges of the blurred luma facing / away from a light at Angle, Strength = Distance
passes: int m=int(u_p0+.5);float l=luma(c.rgb);float k=m==0?smoothstep(.45,.75,l):m==1?smoothstep(.55,.25,l):m==2?smoothstep(.12,.35,length(sobelD(uv,R(1.)))):l;return vec4(vec3(k),1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(max(u_p2,.6)));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(max(u_p2,.6)));

filters.name: Heartfelt (rain on window)
filters.note: Shadertoy "Heartfelt" (BigWings / Martijn Steinrucken 2017, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0): rain on a window — static droplets plus two layers of sliding drops with trails (same grid / saw / wiggle construction); drop normals by finite differences refract the view; the background is fogged (Gaussian Fog blur standing in for the mip-level blur) except where drops and trails have wiped the glass. Single frame at Time; the original heart-shaped wipe / lightning / zoom animation omitted
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p1));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p1));

filters.name: Colormap: IDL LOADCT 0-20
filters.note: IDL LOADCT tables (colors1.tbl, ITT/Harris; byte values via GDL initct.cpp): value snapped to the 256-entry index, piecewise-linear knots reproduce every entry within 1 level; Levels posterizes

filters.name: Colormap: IDL LOADCT 21-30
filters.note: IDL LOADCT tables (colors1.tbl, ITT/Harris; byte values via GDL initct.cpp): value snapped to the 256-entry index, piecewise-linear knots reproduce every entry within 1 level; Levels posterizes

filters.name: Colormap: IDL LOADCT 31-40
filters.note: IDL LOADCT tables (colors1.tbl, ITT/Harris; byte values via GDL initct.cpp): value snapped to the 256-entry index, piecewise-linear knots reproduce every entry within 1 level; Levels posterizes

filters.name: Swiss Hillshading (Imhof)
filters.note: Swiss-style shaded relief after Imhof (1965) / Jenny (2001): NW oblique light, aerial perspective (contrast falls and tone lightens toward low elevations), hypsometric base tint, warm yellow lights and blue-violet shadows (approx.; no manual generalisation)

filters.name: Multi-directional Oblique Weighted (MDOW)
filters.note: Mark (1992, USGS OF 92-422) as in GDAL -multidirectional: hillshades from 225/270/315/360 deg weighted sin^2(aspect - azimuth) and averaged (weights sum to 2); Mark used 30 deg altitude

filters.name: Topographic Openness (Yokoyama)
filters.note: Yokoyama, Shirasawa & Pike 2002: mean over 8 azimuths of the zenith angle to the horizon within radius L (positive = 90 - max elevation angle, negative = 90 + min elevation angle, i.e. openness of the inverted surface); shown as a linear stretch (95 - span .. 95 deg) like RVT

filters.name: Waterlining
filters.note: cartographic waterlining: concentric lines parallel to the shore inside water (luma < sea level), spacing growing outward and fading; shore distance from a 24-ray search (approx. Euclidean distance)

filters.name: Plan Oblique Relief
filters.note: Jenny & Patterson 2007 plan oblique relief: each point shifted north by elevation x cot(inclination), hidden parts removed by marching the column from the south (y-buffer equivalent); the south map edge shows as a dark wall; 90 deg = plain plan view

filters.name: Texture Shading (Leland Brown)
filters.note: Brown 2010/2014 texture shading = fractional Laplacian |k|^alpha of the DEM; approx.: three Gaussian band-pass layers (ratio 4) weighted 4^(-alpha k) instead of the FFT filter, normalised by RMS (Brown stretches by percentiles)
passes:
float s3=R(u_p1),s2=s3*.25,s1=s3*.0625;vec3 acc=vec3(0.),ws=vec3(0.);for(int j=-12;j<=12+int(u_p0*0.);j++){float fj=float(j)*.25;vec3 w=exp(-.5*vec3(fj*fj));
   acc+=w*vec3(luma(O(uv+vec2(fj*s1*u_px.x,0.)).rgb),luma(O(uv+vec2(fj*s2*u_px.x,0.)).rgb),luma(O(uv+vec2(fj*s3*u_px.x,0.)).rgb));ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,luma(c.rgb));

float s3=R(u_p1),s2=s3*.25,s1=s3*.0625;vec3 acc=vec3(0.),ws=vec3(0.);for(int j=-12;j<=12+int(u_p0*0.);j++){float fj=float(j)*.25;vec3 w=exp(-.5*vec3(fj*fj));
   acc+=w*vec3(T(uv+vec2(0.,fj*s1*u_px.y)).r,T(uv+vec2(0.,fj*s2*u_px.y)).g,T(uv+vec2(0.,fj*s3*u_px.y)).b);ws+=w;}return vec4(acc/ws,T(uv).a);

filters.name: Cliff Shading
filters.note: Swiss-style cliff / rock depiction (approx.): areas steeper than the cliff slope drawn as oblique-lit hachures along the fall line (density = shadow tone) or high-contrast tone, gentle terrain as a light low-contrast hillshade

filters.name: Rotozoomer
filters.note: classic rotozoomer: the image used as an infinitely tiled texture, rotated and scaled about the screen centre (one frame)
passes:
float a=radians(u_p0);vec2 p=(uv-.5)*vec2(asp(),1.);p=mat2(cos(a),sin(a),-sin(a),cos(a))*p/u_p1;vec2 q=p/vec2(asp(),1.)+.5+u_p2;
  q=u_p3>.5?1.-abs(mod(q,2.)-1.):fract(q);return vec4(O(q).rgb,1.);

filters.name: Raster Bars (copper bars)
filters.note: Amiga copper raster bars: horizontal bars on sine paths (nearer bars in front), one colour per scanline with a bright core; each bar takes its hue from the image row it crosses

filters.name: Kefrens Bars
filters.note: Kefrens bars (Kefrens 1990): per scanline one shaded vertical bar is drawn into a line buffer that is never cleared, so each line shows every earlier bar - rendered by finding the latest scanline whose bar covers the pixel; bar colours sampled from the image

filters.name: Starfield Overlay
filters.note: demoscene 3D starfield: 8 depth layers of hashed stars in perspective, motion streaks along the radial flight direction (longer and brighter when near), screen-blended over the image

filters.name: Metaballs
filters.note: demoscene metaballs: one ball per grid cell (jittered), radius and colour from the image cell, Wyvill (1-d^2/R^2)^3 field summed and cut at the threshold, shaded from the field gradient

filters.name: Voxel Space Terrain (Comanche)
filters.note: Comanche (NovaLogic 1992) Voxel Space: image = colour map, brightness = height map (tiled); per screen column a front-to-back march of the view frustum projects each height to the screen and the first sample reaching the pixel row wins (the y-buffer rule), fog toward the far plane

filters.name: Sapphire Glows (Orthicon / Rings / Rainbow / Noise)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_GlowOrthicon (darkens a wide area around brights, bright cores protected), S_GlowRings (ring-shaped kernel per channel at radii 1 / .82 / .64 x Width, so colour shifts with distance), S_GlowRainbow (glow coloured by a spectrum that cycles with distance from the bright edge), S_GlowNoise (gaussian glow modulated by a fizzing noise texture); polar gather of the thresholded image, screen combine
passes: vec3 b=max(c.rgb-u_p1,0.)/max(1.-u_p1,.05);return vec4(b,1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2)*.08);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2)*.08);

filters.name: Glint Rainbow (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_GlintRainbow: 4-way star glints (X, Y and two weaker diagonals) from pixels above Threshold, each ray running white at the core into a spectrum toward its tip; screen combine
passes: vec3 b=max(c.rgb-u_p1,0.)/max(1.-u_p1,.05);return vec4(b,1.);

filters.name: Edge Rays (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_EdgeRays: Sobel edges (coloured by the source) emit light beams radiating away from Center (negative length beams inward), red/green/blue lengths slightly different for fringing; added to the source
passes: vec2 g=sobel(uv);float e=clamp(length(g)*1.5,0.,1.);return vec4(c.rgb*e+e*.1,1.);

filters.name: Z Glow (depth-varying glow, Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_ZGlow: glow width interpolated from Width Near to Width Far by the depth of the glowing pixel (scatter-as-gather: each source sample spreads with its own depth-dependent gaussian), red wider than blue so glow colour shifts with distance; screen combine
passes: vec3 b=max(c.rgb-u_p2,0.)/max(1.-u_p2,.05);return vec4(b,1.);

filters.name: Sapphire Edge Effects (Colorize / Double / In Direction)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_EdgeColorize (edges coloured by the direction they face: top yellow, right cyan, bottom pink, left green; Angle rotates the colours), S_EdgeDetectDouble (edge detect run twice: the edges of the edge image, giving double-stranded lines), S_EdgesInDirection (only edges whose gradient points along Angle); Edge Smooth = gaussian pre-blur that thickens the edges
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p1));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p1));

if(int(u_p0+.5)!=1)return c;vec3 gx=(T(uv+vec2(u_px.x,0.)).rgb-T(uv-vec2(u_px.x,0.)).rgb)*.5,gy=(T(uv+vec2(0.,u_px.y)).rgb-T(uv-vec2(0.,u_px.y)).rgb)*.5;
   return vec4(clamp(sqrt(gx*gx+gy*gy)*2.5,0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Blur Chroma (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_BlurChroma: image split into Rec.709 luma and chroma (Cb, Cr), each gaussian-blurred by its own amount, chroma scaled, recombined; Mix With Source blends back the original
passes:
vec3 v=c.rgb;float yy=v.x;vec2 cc=(v.yz-.5)*u_p2;float rr=yy+1.5748*cc.y,bb=yy+1.8556*cc.x,gg=(yy-.2126*rr-.0722*bb)/.7152;
   return vec4(mix(clamp(vec3(rr,gg,bb),0.,1.),O(uv).rgb,u_p3),1.);

filters.name: Defocus Prism (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_DefocusPrism: lens defocus with a circular or polygonal iris (100-tap disc gather in linear light), the red / green / blue discs of different widths (Chroma Sep) so bokeh and edges split into colour rings, highlights above ~0.7 boosted before the blur

filters.name: Warp Repeat / Mo Curves Blur / Warp Chroma (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_WarpRepeat (average of the image under 40 transforms interpolated from identity to the From transform: Z Dist zoom, Rotate and Shift X about the centre), S_BlurMoCurves (Transform and Blur: image moved to the transform and motion-blurred over the last half of its path, exposure ramped toward the end; a still has no animation curves, so the transform stands for one frame of motion), S_WarpChroma (each step tinted by a spectrum, red at From to blue at To, per-channel normalised so unwarped areas stay neutral)

filters.name: Dog Vision (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_DogVision: two-channel (dichromat) vision: the two confused primaries are averaged into one complementary channel (Yellow-Blue = dog vision: (R+G)/2 shown as yellow, B as blue), slight acuity blur, optional hue rotation of the two channels
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p1));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p1));

filters.name: Clamp Chroma (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_ClampChroma: Rec.709 YCbCr; chroma magnitude (2 x |CbCr|, about 1 for a pure primary) scaled then limited to Clamp Chroma without changing hue (broadcast-safe style); luma scaled then limited to Clamp Luma
passes:
float yy=luma(c.rgb);vec2 cc=vec2((c.b-yy)/1.8556,(c.r-yy)/1.5748)*u_p1;float ch=length(cc)*2.;if(ch>u_p0)cc*=u_p0/max(ch,1e-5);yy=min(yy*u_p3,u_p2);
  float rr=yy+1.5748*cc.y,bb=yy+1.8556*cc.x,gg=(yy-.2126*rr-.0722*bb)/.7152;return vec4(clamp(vec3(rr,gg,bb),0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Laser Beam (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_LaserBeam (single frame, Smooth shape): a beam segment travelling along a path through the frame centre at Angle (start and stop just outside the frame), Position = progress along the path, white core + red edge + dusty atmospheric halo, screen combine

filters.name: Flys Eye Hex (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_FlysEyeHex: hexagonal tiles (Tile Frequency across the width); each tile shows the image zoomed about the tile (Inside Z Dist, >1 zooms out) taken from the tile position scaled toward the centre (Overall Z Dist; 0 = every tile shows the same image); reflect wrap; Edge Softness darkens the seams (approx.)

filters.name: Kaleido Diamonds (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_Kaleido:Diamonds: space folded by mirrors along a rotated diamond (rhombus) lattice, each diamond a reflected copy of the area at the centre; Rel Height stretches the diamonds (affine, approx. for non-square diamonds), Kaleido Amount blends from the source (0) to the full kaleidoscope (1)

filters.name: Warp Puddle / Warp Drops (Sapphire)
filters.note: Boris FX Sapphire S_WarpPuddle (concentric sine waves from the centre displacing the image radially, faded in near the centre and out at Outer Radius) and S_WarpDrops (each bright region above Threshold, found on a 12x12 grid of the blurred image, is a wave centre weighted by its brightness; ripples summed, approx.); single frame (no phase animation), reflect wrap
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(12.));

filters.name: Camera ISP Raw Stages (black level, DPC, green imbalance, binning, remosaic, HA demosaic, FCS)
filters.note: single-image ISP simulation: the input (taken as sRGB, linearised with gamma 2.2) is mosaicked into an RGGB raw (Quad Bayer: 2x2 same-colour blocks) carrying the impairment the stage fixes (Impairment = strength), the stage is applied in the CFA domain, then demosaiced. Black level: pedestal bl = 0.25 x Impairment added, then (raw - bl) / (white - bl). DPC: openISP-style detection (pixel differs from all 8 same-colour neighbours at distance 2 by > threshold, same sign) and replacement by the mean along the smallest-gradient direction (vertical, horizontal, two diagonals). Green imbalance: Gb gain mismatch; flat-area Gr/Gb equalisation with the 4 diagonal (other-type) greens. Binning: 2x2 same-colour average into a half-resolution Bayer (shown at full size). Quad Bayer remosaic: Gaussian-weighted same-colour interpolation into standard RGGB (vendor remosaic algorithms are proprietary - approx.); Uncorrected = the quad mosaic demosaiced as if Bayer. Hamilton-Adams 1997: green by the direction of the smaller gradient |dG| + |2X - X-2 - X+2| with Laplacian correction, R/B from colour differences (diagonal direction chosen the same way); Uncorrected = bilinear. False colour suppression: chroma scaled down by an edge gain from the luma high-pass (openISP FCS idea).

filters.name: Camera Colour Matrices (CCM, DNG ColorMatrix, ForwardMatrix)
filters.note: camera colour pipeline with real Adobe DNG ColorMatrix (XYZ D65 -> camera, from LibRaw colordata) for 4 cameras. sRGB scene input: linear sRGB -> XYZ -> camera RGB (ColorMatrix) and white-balanced by the camera neutral CM x D65 white; camera-RGB input: the image itself is taken as white-balanced camera RGB. CCM = XYZ->sRGB x ColorMatrix^-1 x diag(neutral) (white preserved); Camera to XYZ = ColorMatrix^-1 path (DNG spec); ForwardMatrix = Bradford D65->D50 x ColorMatrix^-1 x diag(neutral), rescaled so (1,1,1) maps to D50 white (a derived FM: real DNGs ship separately calibrated ones), then D50 -> D65 Bradford -> sRGB; Uncorrected = white-balanced camera RGB shown directly (the raw look without a CCM). Intermediate view shows camera RGB / XYZ / XYZ D50 (normalised to white) as RGB. A scene round trip through any rendered path reproduces the input (the matrices are exact inverses).

filters.name: OtisFX Directional Depth Blur / Depth Darkness / Magic Border

The 1/16 and 1/64-resolution blur layers are emulated with wide full-resolution blurs and the colour of layers 2-3 is taken from layer 1 (approx.)

filters.name: AviSynth Spatial Cleaners (MinBlur / SPresso / FluxSmooth / SmoothUV / FixChromaBleeding)
filters.note: AviSynth spatial cleaners on the working-pixel grid. MinBlur (Didee): per channel, d1 = x - RemoveGrain(11)[then 20, 20] blur (3x3 binomial; 5x5 [1 3 4 3 1]; 7x7 [1 4 8 10 8 4 1]) and d2 = x - median (RG4 3x3 / MedianBlur 5x5 / 7x7); out = x - (0 if signs differ else the smaller-magnitude difference). SPresso (Didee 2006, luma only): RG4 median y; if x = y keep, if x+LIM1 < y then x+limit, if x-LIM1 > y then x-limit, else (x(100-bias)+y bias)/100, LIM1 = round(limit 100/bias - 1); default limit 2. FluxSmoothS: FluxSmoothST spatial averaging (centre plus the 8 neighbours within the threshold, default 7, per Y/Cb/Cr) applied to "fluctuating" pixels, with the temporal prev/next test replaced by a spatial one (both opposite neighbour pairs on the same side) - approx. SmoothUV (Kurosu, derainbow): chroma replaced by the mean chroma of the radius window whose |dCb|+|dCr| is within the threshold (default 30; luma untouched) - approx. FixChromaBleeding (ajordan script): mask of extreme Cr (sat x4 clipped, i.e. |Cr| >= ~32/255), dilated by a shifted 7x7 window (approx. of the half-res GeneralConvolution + resize), where chroma is shifted 4 px left and desaturated to 0.8

filters.name: aSharp (AviSynth adaptive sharpening)
filters.note: ASharp (Marc FD, AviSynth+ port by Asd-g), luma only, 8-bit integer arithmetic as in asharp_run_c: diff = x - round(3x3 mean), dev = max |neighbour - x| (hqbf: only neighbours inside the same 8x8 block); T2 = ((dev 128 D2) >> 16 + Da) 16 with T = T 512, D = D 512, Da = -32 + D >> 7, clamped to [-32, T]; B > 0 lowers D2 near 8x8 block borders (x, y mod 8 = 6/1 by 256 - 48B, 7/0 by 256 - 64B); out = x + diff T2 / 512. Flat areas (small dev) are slightly softened, edges sharpened up to T

filters.name: MSharpen (AviSynth masked sharpening)
filters.note: MSharpen (neuron2, reimplementation by tp7), RGB path: 3x3 mean blur per channel; edge mask where any channel of the blur differs by >= threshold from the pixel below or to the right (High quality) or across the two diagonals (fast); masked pixels become (strength (4x - 3 blur) + (255 - strength) x) / 256 with 4x - 3 blur clipped; Mask shows the edge map

filters.name: eedi3 (edge-directed field interpolation, AviSynth)
filters.note: eedi3 (tritical; VapourSynth eedi3m doc): keeps one field (every other working-pixel row) and rebuilds the missing rows; for each missing pixel the connection direction d in [-mdis, mdis] minimises alpha x neighbourhood similarity (sum of |up(x+d+u) - down(x-d+u)|, u = -2..2, nrad 2) + beta x vertical difference created (|interp - up| + |interp - down|) + (1 - alpha - beta) |d|, in 8-bit luma units, and the pixel is the 2-point average along d. Simplified (approx.): gamma = 0 (no dynamic-programming smoothness along the row, so directions are chosen per pixel), cost3 off, ucubic off, vcheck 0; direction chosen on luma and applied to RGB

filters.name: GrainFactory3 (AviSynth luma-zoned grain)
filters.note: GrainFactory3 (Didee 2008) defaults: three grain layers (dark / mid / bright) of AddGrainC Gaussian noise with variance g1-3str 13/15/25 generated at size 1.5/1.2/0.9 (lattice spacing in source pixels) and bicubic-resized back with b = shrp/-50 + 1, c = (1 - b)/2 for shrp 60/66/80 (b halved for size > 1.5, single resize - approx.), optional texture = gtex/100 x (g - g of the diagonal neighbour) as the mt_edge bump kernel; blended by luma zones th1-th4 = 24/56/128/160 (dark->mid and mid->bright ramps) and added to luma only. Strength / Size scale multiply all three; temporal averaging and ontop_grain need video and are omitted

filters.name: DeScratch (AviSynth vertical scratch removal)
filters.note: DeScratch (Fizick, AviSynth+ port): detection on a vertically blurred copy (blurlen 15), local horizontal extremes of luma darker (low) / brighter (high) than both neighbours at width/2+1 by mindif with neighbour asymmetry < 10 (maxwidth 3), kept only where the run of extremes through the pixel (searched up and down in 2 px steps, 1 px horizontal slack per step, gaps up to 3 px closed) is at least minlen long (approx. of the length / gap / maxangle test); removal with keep = 100: the smooth (blurred) scratch offset is subtracted, so image detail inside the scratch is kept; the detected width (1 or 3) is corrected. Mark shows dark scratches black, bright white
passes: return vec4(vec3(luma(box1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(15.)).rgb)),1.);

filters.name: Forensically Noise Analysis / Luminance Gradient
filters.note: Forensically (Jonas Wagner): Noise Analysis isolates noise with a separable 3-tap median (rows, then columns) and shows |image - median| x amplitude per channel ("removes the rest of the image"); Equalize histogram = per-channel histogram equalisation of that layer (CDF estimated from a 16x16 grid of samples - approx.). Luminance Gradient: brightness change along x and y shown as R = 0.5 + dx, G = 0.5 + dy, B = magnitude (colour encoding approx.); similar surfaces at similar angles to the light should look alike
passes: if(u_p2<.5)return c;vec3 cnt=vec3(0.);for(int j=0;j<16+int(u_p0*0.);j++)for(int i=0;i<16+int(u_p0*0.);i++){vec3 s=T((vec2(float(i),float(j))+.5)/16.).rgb;cnt+=step(s,c.rgb);}return vec4(cnt/256.,1.);

filters.name: Forensically Level Sweep
filters.note: Forensically Level Sweep: a slice of the histogram of width Width (8-bit levels) around position Sweep is stretched to the full output range (position 0.5, width 32: 127 - 16 maps to 0), revealing edges of pasted regions that differ in level; Opacity mixes with the original
passes: vec3 v=c.rgb*255.;float lo=u_p0*255.-u_p1*.5;vec3 o=clamp((v-lo)/u_p1,0.,1.);return vec4(mix(c.rgb,o,u_p2),1.);

filters.name: Forensically Magnifier (enhancement)
filters.note: Forensically Magnifier: shows the region around (Center X, Center Y) enlarged Zoom times with an enhancement computed from the visible region: Histogram Equalization (per channel, CDF from a 16x16 sample grid - approx.), Auto Contrast (one min-max stretch from luminance extremes, keeps colours) or Auto Contrast by Channel (per-channel min-max stretch, can shift colours); bilinear magnification

filters.name: Pop Art Fill (Painter)
filters.note: Corel Painter Effects > Esoterica > Pop Art Fill using Image Luminance: covers the image with pseudo-halftone dots (45-degree screen) in the Dab colour on the Background colour; Scale = dot cell size, Contrast mixes in the luminance (0 = uniform dots), Invert flips the source

filters.name: Grid Paper (Painter)
filters.note: Corel Painter Effects > Esoterica > Grid Paper: rectangular grid, vertical lines, horizontal lines or dot grid at the given spacing and line thickness (blue grid colour), drawn over the image (transparent background) or on paper colour

filters.name: Glass Distortion (Painter)
filters.note: Corel Painter Effects > Focus > Glass Distortion: displaces the image as if seen through glass whose relief comes from the image luminance or a paper texture (procedural paper grain here); Softness blurs the relief; Map: Refraction (offset along the relief gradient), Vector displacement (offset along a fixed diagonal by luminance), Angle displacement (luminance sets the offset direction); approx.

filters.name: Wallpaper Groups (17 plane symmetry groups)
filters.note: exact wallpaper-group orbit folding: each output point is mapped by the group operations (translations, 2/3/4/6-fold rotations, mirrors, glides) into one fundamental domain, which samples a cell cut from the image centre (square lattice for p1..p4g, hexagonal for p3..p6m; Conway: o 2222 ** xx *x 22* 22x 2*22 442 *442 4*2 333 *333 3*3 632 *632)

filters.name: Frieze Groups (7 strip symmetry groups)
filters.note: the 7 frieze groups (Conway names): a strip of the image centre folded into one fundamental domain by the group operations (translation, glide, vertical / horizontal mirrors, half-turns); bands stacked by plain translation or shown alone

filters.name: Dichromacy Simulation (Brettel 1997 / Vienot 1999)
filters.note: DaltonLens (libDaltonLens) precomputed linear-RGB matrices: Brettel, Vienot & Mollon 1997 two half-plane projection (separation-plane normal picks the half-plane), Vienot, Brettel & Mollon 1999 single-plane projection (inaccurate for tritan, as DaltonLens warns); sRGB decoded to linear, severity = linear interpolation

filters.name: CT Window Presets (Lung / Bone / ...)
filters.note: standard radiology display windows (Radiopaedia values): grey = input luma mapped linearly to Hounsfield units (default 12-bit CT range -1024..3071), then linear window (L - W/2 .. L + W/2) to black..white

filters.name: Weighted Gray-Edge Color Constancy
filters.note: Gijsenij, Gevers & van de Weijer 2012 (PAMI) weighted gray-edge: illuminant e = (sum w^kappa |grad f|^p)^(1/p) per channel on Gaussian-derivative edges of the linear image (16x16 sample grid), w = share of the edge energy in the specular (illuminant direction), shadow-shading (pixel colour direction) or material (residual) quasi-invariant, iterated 4x from a white start; von Kries correction in linear RGB
passes: return vec4(mix(c.rgb/12.92,pow((c.rgb+.055)/1.055,vec3(2.4)),step(vec3(.04045),c.rgb)),1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(2.*u_p0));

filters.name: B-COSFIRE Vessel / Line Filter
filters.note: Azzopardi, Strisciuglio, Vento & Petkov 2015 B-COSFIRE (symmetric bar configuration): rectified centre-on DoG (sigma, 0.5 sigma) responses taken at points rho = 0, +-2, +-4 ... along a line, each blurred (Gaussian-weighted max with sigma' growing with rho, approx. 5-tap) and combined by the Gaussian-weighted geometric mean; rotation tolerance = max over 12 orientations

filters.name: DullRazor Hair Removal
filters.note: Lee, Ng, Gallagher, Coldman & McLean 1997 DullRazor: generalized grey closing per RGB channel with linear structuring elements at 0, 45 and 90 degrees (max of the three closings), hair mask = |original - closing| > threshold (any channel, 3x3 dilated); hair pixels replaced by linear interpolation between the nearest non-hair pixels along the shortest of 4 line directions, then a 3x3 median on the replaced pixels; the thin/long shape verification step is omitted (approx.)
passes: float m=0.;for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++)m=max(m,step(u_p1,T(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*u_px).a));return vec4(O(uv).rgb,m);

filters.name: Edge And Tones (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge library filter, look approximation from its name and category (the user-made node graph is not public): smoothed image posterized into N luminance tones (hue kept), dark outline from the gradient of the smoothed luma
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(2.*u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(2.*u_p2));

filters.name: Patterned Dithering (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge library filter, look approximation from its name and category (the user-made node graph is not public): ordered dithering with a tiled shape threshold map (tone-correct: each pattern's threshold is its own area CDF, so coverage = tone)

filters.name: Pixel Halftone (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge library filter, look approximation from its name and category (the user-made node graph is not public): per-cell average colour drawn as a halftone dot rasterised on a coarse sub-pixel grid (blocky "pixel" dots), dot area = ink coverage

filters.name: Adaptive Dots (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge library filter, look approximation from its name and category (the user-made node graph is not public): quadtree halftone, cells split (up to 3 times) while the luma standard deviation inside the cell exceeds the detail threshold, one round dot per cell with area = ink coverage

filters.name: Cimoc (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge library filter, look approximation from its name and category (the user-made node graph is not public) ("comic" reversed): HSV-posterized flat colours from a smoothed image, black ink outlines from the luma gradient, 45-degree Ben-Day dot shading in the darker tones
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(3.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(3.));

filters.name: Multicolor Printing (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge library filter, look approximation from its name and category (the user-made node graph is not public): image separated into 3 flat spot / process inks plus black, each plate posterized to a few ink levels, given a grainy ink texture and its own registration offset, overprinted multiplicatively on off-white paper

filters.name: Dynamic Bleed / Color Leak (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge library filter, look approximation from its name and category (the user-made node graph is not public): Dynamic Bleed = darker / saturated colours bleed downstream along a noise-bent flow with noise-varying reach (min-blend, like ink spreading); Color leak = chroma of strong colours leaks in one direction with exponential decay while each pixel keeps its own luminance

filters.name: Tri-Color (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge library filter, look approximation from its name and category (the user-made node graph is not public): luminance split by two thresholds into three flat poster colours (shadow / mid / highlight) with adjustable edge softness

filters.name: Gothic FX / Romantic Grunge (Filter Forge)
filters.note: Filter Forge library filter, look approximation from its name and category (the user-made node graph is not public): Gothic FX = mostly desaturated, cold-shadowed, hard S-curve contrast with a cool highlight glow, dark grunge stains and scratches, heavy vignette; Romantic Grunge = warm faded colour, strong soft glow, lifted blacks, brown paper stains and scratches, warm vignette
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(14.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(14.));

filters.name: CCTV Camera (GenArts M_CCTV)
filters.note: look approximation of a security-camera feed: barrel lens, low vertical resolution with soft horizontal bandwidth, per-line sync jitter, monochrome / green-phosphor / washed colour, crushed contrast, interlace lines, slow rolling brightness bar, snow noise, heavy vignette (no timestamp text)

filters.name: Edge Leak (GenArts M_EdgeLeak)
filters.note: look approximation: light leaking in from the four frame edges, coloured by the (brightness-weighted) pixels along each edge, exponential falloff with noise-varying reach

filters.name: Pool3D / Puddle3D (GenArts Monsters)
filters.note: look approximations: Pool3D = image seen through a moving water surface (directional swell + fbm height field; refraction offset = surface gradient, caustics = inverse area ratio 1/|1 + d * laplacian| of the refracted light (bright lines where rays focus), slight cyan); Puddle3D = puddles (noise patches on a perspective ground plane below the horizon) reflecting the image above the horizon, disturbed by concentric ripple rings

filters.name: ClipTex / PatchTex (GenArts Monsters)
filters.note: look approximations: ClipTex = fbm noise hard-clipped into flat bands (texture layers with sharp clip edges) tinted and modulated by the image; PatchTex = patchwork of square patches (randomly subdivided) each filled with the image content from a random offset, with darkened seams

filters.name: Cumulus Clouds (GenArts M_Cumulo)
filters.note: look approximation of rendered cumulus: domain-warped fbm density with coverage threshold, self-shadowing by a 6-step march toward the sun (Beer-Lambert), grey-blue shadowed bases and bright silver-lined edges, composited over the image by density

filters.name: Handheld LCD Shaders II (agb001 / ags001 / authentic_gbc / sameboy / simpletex / lcd1x_psp / retro-v3 / mega-blocks)
filters.note: ports of RetroArch handheld/ shaders at their preset defaults, applied to a virtual low-res source (Source pixel size = one console pixel): agb001 / ags001 (endrift, mGBA): 4x subpixel stripes RGB+grey with darker 4th row, AGB gamma .8^1.8 +.16 lift, bilinear stock upscale; ags001-light frontlight bleed + reflection .07 at 0.025; authentic_gbc v2.2 (linearised, analytic blurred-rectangle coverage of notched subpixels, brightness .6, smoothing .3); sameboy-lcd (6-step subpixel ramp, colour low .8, scanline depth .1); simpletex_lcd (zfast line weighting, grid .65/.65/bias .6, darken .05; the paper PNG replaced by procedural paper - approx.); lcd1x_psp (sine LCD 4 / scanline 16 at one cycle per source pixel + PSP colour matrix, gamma 2.21); retro-v3 (quintic pixel interpolation, pixel size .5, boost 1.36); mega-blocks brick (bevel .27, highlight .9, light from top-left) / dome (radial stud field)

float Bw=max(R(u_p1),1.);vec2 SS=ceil(u_res/Bw);vec2 w=floor(uv*u_res);if(w.x>=SS.x||w.y>=SS.y)return vec4(0.,0.,0.,1.);

filters.name: Handheld LCD Lighting (pixel_transparency / sunlight_shimmer / frontlit-reflective)
filters.note: ports of RetroArch handheld/shaders/pixel_transparency v2.3 (Mr. Hylian-style reflective backing: bright pixels let a grainy warm/neutral backing show through (base alpha .2), dark pixels cast a blurred drop shadow offset 3,3 px at 640x480 reference scale, palette tint, smooth 9-tap shadow blur), sunlight_shimmer (adds glare .15 / spread .25 and the quarter-wave-plate rainbow film tint: 7 wavelengths, retardation 275 nm, splotchy film noise .5) and frontlit-reflective (ambient .15 + Gaussian point light .65 at (.72,.89), black lift / gamma shift, green bias, negative-image falloff; the dirt LUT texture is replaced by procedural fbm smudges - approx.); Light shift moves the glare / point light; no accelerometer / animation

filters.name: NTSC Shaders II (mame-ntsc / blastem / tiny_ntsc / ntsc-xot / artifact-colors / ntsc-adaptive / patchy / analog_overshoot)
filters.note: ports of RetroArch ntsc/ shaders on a virtual console source (Source pixel size = one console pixel; console line width assumed 320 px for mame-ntsc / blastem, 256 px (3-line phase) for tiny_ntsc / ntsc-adaptive, 640 samples per 320 px for ntsc-xot / artifact-colors): mame-ntsc = MAME HLSL encode (Y + I cos + Q sin, 52.6 us line, 3.5975 MHz) and 64-tap windowed-sinc notch / I 1.2 / Q 0.6 MHz decode, postproc deconvergence (-.4/.4/.2), saturation 1.4, scanlines .175, 60 Hz roll bar frame 0; ntsc-blastem 7-tap comb decoder (comb .8 x Artifacts; its y_above line offset kept as written); tiny_ntsc (NINTENDO mode, comb .4, blackman luma / gaussian chroma); ntsc-xot (21-tap blackman sinc per RGB channel, quarter-rate subcarrier, hue 1 rad as shipped; out-of-range taps = 0); artifact-colors (Fs/4 carrier, 29-tap luma LP .16667 + bandpass BW 1/50, chroma LP, saturation 30); ntsc-adaptive (guest advanced NTSC: 3-phase + merged fields, modified Maister luma filters, anti-ringing .5); patchy-snes / patchy-blastem = approx. of patchy-ntsc presets (composite at 4 / 8 samples per pixel, 47.7 us line, SNES 1/3 line phase + RGB blur, Genesis .7 initial phase; sinc luma 2.15 MHz, 3.55-3.6 MHz bandpass, full-phase demod; jungle-chip axes, RF noise, jailbars and phosphor LUT omitted); analog_overshoot with decode-separately off (its shipped default 1 is a pass-through), Hermite taps 1 source pixel apart, tension .25 / bias .75
passes:
float Bw=max(R(u_p1),1.);vec2 SS=ceil(u_res/Bw);vec2 w=floor(uv*u_res);if(w.x>=SS.x||w.y>=SS.y)return vec4(0.,0.,0.,1.);
 vec3 a=vec3(0.);for(int j=0;j<4;j++)for(int i=0;i<4;i++){vec2 q=floor(w*Bw+(vec2(float(i),float(j))+.5)*Bw*.25)+.5;a+=O(min(q,u_res-.5)/u_res).rgb;}return vec4(a/16.,1.);

filters.name: Rays: Fan / Spiral / Random Spikes / Radial Streaks (DFT)
filters.note: Digital Film Tools Rays-style ray types (look approx.): highlights above a soft threshold plus a glow at the centre are gathered radially toward the centre (48 taps, exponential decay), then masked by a fan-shaped stripe pattern (Fan), log-spiral stripes (Spiral), seeded random thin spikes of random length (Random Spikes) or left unmasked (Radial Streaks), screen-blended
passes: vec3 v=O(uv).rgb;float l=luma(v);float k=smoothstep(.55,.95,l);vec2 d=(uv-vec2(u_p1,u_p2))*vec2(asp(),1.);float g=exp(-dot(d,d)*40.);return vec4(v*k+vec3(1.,.95,.85)*g*.6,1.);

filters.name: Ozone Zone Grading (DFT)
filters.note: Ozone-style 11-zone (Ansel Adams zone system) grading, approx.: linear luminance mapped to zones (zone V = 18% grey, one stop per zone, 0-X), shadow / midtone / highlight zone groups shifted by whole or fractional zones with smooth (Zone softness) group boundaries, colour scaled by the luminance ratio

filters.name: Telecine Transfer (DFT)
filters.note: look approximation of a film-to-video telecine transfer (DFT Telecine): slightly soft scan (Gaussian Softness), lifted / flashed blacks, soft exponential highlight knee, faint warm halation around highlights, slightly reduced saturation and cool video balance

return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p3));

filters.name: Screen Smoother / DeArtifact (DFT zMatte)
filters.note: DFT zMatte helpers (approx.): Screen Smoother evens out unevenly lit green / blue screens - a screen-masked (key-colour dominance) separable average gives the local screen colour, screen pixels are rescaled by global screen mean / local screen colour; DeArtifact restores compressed (4:1:1 / 4:2:0 / DV) chroma before keying - chroma is replaced by a luma-guided (cross-bilateral) separable average while luma is kept

filters.name: Multi-block LBP / Haar-like Features / Rank Noise Filter (scikit-image)
filters.note: scikit-image: feature.multiblock_lbp (Zhang et al. 2007) evaluated densely - 3x3 grid of BxB block sums around each pixel, bit set when a neighbour block sum >= the centre (TL=128 clockwise to L=1), shown as code/255; feature.haar_like_feature full-window features with blocks BxB centred on the pixel (2-x right-left, 2-y bottom-top, 3-x / 3-y middle-outer, type-4 anti-diagonal minus diagonal; shown 0.5 + Gain x sum / (4 x 255 B^2)); filters.rank.noise_filter on 8-bit luma with a disk footprint of radius B (centre excluded): 0 when a neighbour equals the centre, else the distance to the nearest occupied grey level (x Gain / 255); measured against skimage 0.26 on 8-bit grey input (see note in report)

filters.name: Fourier Uniform / Ellipsoid / Edge Enhance More (scipy / Pillow)
filters.note: scipy.ndimage.fourier_uniform / fourier_ellipsoid applied as in the usual ifftn(fourier_x(fftn(img), size)) round trip, implemented in the spatial domain: a size-wide box (separable) / a disk of diameter size, both with wrap-around borders (the FFT is periodic) and linear partial-pixel edge weights (approx. for even / fractional sizes); Pillow EDGE_ENHANCE_MORE = 3x3 kernel (-1 x8, centre 9, scale 1), 8-bit rounding, outermost pixel ring left unfiltered as in Pillow
passes:
