filters.name: ImageOps.deform (Pillow mesh warp)
filters.note: Pillow ImageOps.deform(image, deformer): the deformer getmesh() returns a G x G grid of target rectangles, each mapped to a source quadrilateral with Image.transform(MESH) - the QUAD transform is the bilinear map x = a0 + a1 u + a2 v + a3 u v of the four source corners (bilinear resampling, outside = black). Deformers here: wave (corner offset = Amount x sin(2 pi y / 4 cells), and the same for x), seeded random corner jitter (+-Amount), swirl about the centre

filters.name: Curved Surface / Convert to Panoramic / Geometric Distortion (Clip Studio)
filters.note: Clip Studio Paint 3 distortion filters (approx.): Curved surface = the picture wrapped on a cylinder (axis rotated by Angle; Tilt adds vertical bulge) or a sphere seen from the front (orthographic, Amount = covered arc up to 90 deg, mild Lambert shading); Convert to panoramic = the image read as a rectilinear photo (horizontal field of view 30-150 deg from Amount) re-projected to an equirectangular / spherical panorama view panned by Angle and tilted by Tilt; Geometric distortion = 4-corner pin (top edge narrowed by Amount, right edge raised / lowered by Angle, bottom skew by Tilt) as an exact projective homography; outside = black

filters.name: Adjust Line Width (Clip Studio)
filters.note: Clip Studio Paint Filter > Correct line > Adjust line width: the whole line drawing is thickened or thinned by a fixed width - grey / colour morphology with an anti-aliased disk: thicken dark lines = take the darkest (by luma) pixel within the radius, thin = the lightest; "Light on dark" swaps the roles

filters.name: Artistic (Clip Studio)
filters.note: Clip Studio Paint Filter > Effect > Artistic (photo to illustration), approx.: colour areas flattened by a 4-sector Kuwahara filter (Brush size), saturation boost and partial posterisation to Colour levels, dark outlines where the gradient of the flattened image exceeds Line threshold

filters.name: Remove Shading (AwesomeBump)
filters.note: AwesomeBump diffuse "Remove shading": remove-low-frequency filter colour + (image mean - Gaussian blur) blended by LF blending (exact formula of mode_remove_low_freq_filter), then AO cancellation colour + (1 - AO) x amount (mode_ao_cancellation_filter with an opaque AO map); the AO here is a 48-tap height-difference occlusion estimate from luminance-as-height, not AwesomeBump's own SSAO pass (approx.)

filters.name: Colour Space Swap (Joan Rake)
filters.note: G'MIC csswap: the pixels are read as if they were in colour space A and converted A->RGB, then converted RGB->B and shown as RGB (G'MIC 8-bit scalings for Lab8/LCH8/YIQ8/YUV8/XYZ8/HSx8, illuminant E for XYZ/Lab); the non-8-bit variants and Kodak/Jzazbz/Oklab/HCY/RYB spaces are not included

filters.name: Sawtoother (Joan Rake)
filters.note: G'MIC Sawtoother [RGB/CMY/HSX/LCH8/YIQ8/XYZ8/YUV8/YCbCr/sRGB/Lab8]: image converted to the space, every channel mapped to a sawtooth wave ((v + phase) mod (256/factor)) x factor x multiplier, clipped, converted back; one set of controls for all channels; per-channel smoothness / shift and tone-range mixing omitted

filters.name: Hue Lighten/Darken (Iain Fergusson)
filters.note: Fergusson: per-hue offset of HSV value (or HSL lightness) through an 18-knot hue curve, blended back through a mask from saturation (bottom 100, top 255) x value; here one band of the curve (centre + width, smooth bump) instead of 18 sliders; optional B&W output

filters.name: Saturation EQ (Iain Fergusson)
filters.note: Fergusson Saturation EQ: HSL8 saturation offset by two 9-knot curves (lightness bands 0..255, hue bands every 45 deg, Rotate shifts the hue bands), offset x2 added to S; one band at a time here (Catmull-Rom spline through the knots)

filters.name: Dark Sky (afre)
filters.note: afre darksky: mask = min(G - B, 0) + 127 (blue-dominant pixels below mid-grey), smoothed and contrast-adjusted, soft-light / overlay blended onto the luminance, image recoloured by the new / old luminance ratio (approx.: box-free Gaussian smoothing instead of median, no final range renormalisation)

filters.name: Constrained Sharpen / Local Variance Normalization / YAG

filters.name: Rainbowify (Reptorian)

filters.name: BCC Mixed Colors / Organic Strands / Pin Art 3D

filters.name: Perspective Blur (Procreate)
filters.note: Procreate Adjustments > Perspective Blur: Positional = blur radiating from the puck (zoom blur whose streak length grows with distance from it); Directional = linear streaks along the puck direction (puck offset from the centre gives the angle), stronger away from the puck. 48 jittered taps (approx.)

filters.name: Glitch (Procreate: Artifact / Wave / Signal / Diverge)

filters.name: Local Sigma / Bit Error (ENVI) and Pixel Fixer (BCC)
filters.note: ENVI adaptive filters per band: Local Sigma (Lee 1983 local-sigma: mean of the window pixels within +- k local standard deviations of the centre); Bit Error (spikes deviating from the window mean, centre excluded, by more than k sigma are replaced by the mean of the valid in-range pixels; approx. of ENVI's implementation); BCC Pixel Fixer automatic mode (approx.: isolated dead / hot / stuck pixels outside their 8-neighbour range replaced by the neighbour mean)

filters.name: Color Gamut Reinterpretation (prod80)
filters.note: prod80 PD80_01_Color_Gamut: linearise sRGB, sRGB->XYZ (D65), Bradford-style white adaptation to D50 / E / C where the target space uses it, XYZ->target RGB, re-encode as sRGB, i.e. shows the sRGB image as if its numbers were in the wider/narrower space (matrices from the shader, pre-multiplied)

filters.name: ReShade Colour Looks (Color Gradients / Sunset / Retro Tint / Palette Map)
filters.note: Color Gradients (prod80): shadow / midtone weights from the RGB average (harsh separation), light-scene tints (orange soft light + 30% blue lighten) and dark-scene tints (blue / deep-blue soft light) mixed by the image-average max-channel luminance (smoothstep 0.125..0.3; one still image, no temporal adaptation), highlights pass through as in the shader, final mix 1/3 x Spread x 1.5. Sunset Filter (Fubax): tilted (-7 deg) linear mask through its overlay curve, screen of a red-to-black gradient in linear light (Spread = scale). Retro Tint (Daodan): screen with (0.1,0,0.3). Palette Map (Zenteon): soft nearest-palette weights exp(-10 s^2 d^2) in OKLab over its 8-colour default palette + black/white, keeps the pixel lightness and chroma and takes the palette hue. Hue shift rotates the look colours

filters.name: Watch Dogs Tonemap / Whitepoint Fixer
filters.note: Watch Dogs tonemap (GShade WatchDogs.fx): per-channel Hable-style curve A .55/.50/.45, B .30/.27/.22, C .1, D .10/.07/.03, E .01, F .3, white 2.8/2.9/3.1, output (curve x 1.25 x Amount / white)^1.25. Whitepoint Fixer (luluco250, mode 2): colour divided by the brightest grey (average) of a 16x16 downsample; if that is under 0.8 x Amount it is remapped to 1 (no temporal smoothing on a still). Manual mode: divide by Amount

filters.name: HDR Bloom (SOLARIS / Magic HDR / Bessel Bloom)
filters.note: SOLARIS (iMMERSE): sdr_to_hdr (cone overlap k=0.132, square, whitepoint 2^W compression, x128), equal-weight pyramid of 8 octaves (here a sum of 8 Gaussians sigma 1.5..192 px at 1080p, separable so cross terms make it slightly star-shaped, approx.), blends: energy-conserving lerp (int^2/2), HDR drama overlay-style, dreamy multiply, then hdr_to_sdr; intensity default 1.5x the shader. Magic HDR (luluco250): inverse Reinhard, x e^3 bloom brightness, 7 blur levels weighted by a normal distribution (mean 5.6, var 3.5) and divided by 7, lerp by log10(0.3+1), BakingLab ACES. Bessel Bloom (Insane): gamma 2.2, soft-knee threshold, its 2nd-order Bessel IIR run forward+backward replaced by the exact zero-phase impulse response as an FIR kernel (K=128 at 1080p), added in linear light

filters.name: Lens Ghosts (Unreal Lens / Liquid Lens / Hex Lens Flare)
filters.note: luluco250 FXShaders. Unreal Lens: point-mirrored image zoomed out 4x, inverse BakingLab ACES, edge mask, saturation 0.7, per-channel threshold, x0.01 brightness, hexagonal bokeh from three 9-tap blurs 60 deg apart (75/15/-45 deg), then 5 ghosts sampled at scales 0.6/0.2/0.1/0.05/-1 (x4) added in HDR and re-tonemapped. Liquid Lens: same prepare (threshold, x0.1), 9-tap Gaussian blur, 7 rainbow-tinted ghosts at scales 0.01..0.07 (x4) through its fisheye (amount -1, zoom 3). Hex Lens Flare: 4 thresholded ghosts (x1, x3, x9, mirrored x0.666) in green / blue / orange / cyan, hexagonal blur (here three sequential 16-tap box blurs at 0/60/120 deg = a hexagon, approx.), screen blend. Outside-the-image samples are black (the shaders clamp), sizes relative to 1080p

filters.name: Tracking Rays / Flair Streaks
filters.note: Tracking Rays (luluco250): brightest point of a 16x16 coarse grid (neighbours within 0.1 are merged), 13-step zoom blur toward it (scale 1+(10-1)/13x0.1), pow curve 3, screen. Flair (AstrayFX): pixels with luma above the threshold (shader default 0.999), coloured from a blurred colour map with saturation x5, streaked with its 25-tap Gaussian weights at odd offsets x1.1 (spread 0.5) in the chosen star / cross / skew / horizontal / vertical pattern, added; one still frame so the temporal alternation of tap offsets is not used; sizes relative to 1080p

filters.name: ReShade Posters (Colorful / Multi Tone / Posterize Pixelate / Virtual Resolution / Bilateral Comic)
filters.note: Colorful Poster (Daodan): luma posterized with sigmoid steps (slope 13), chroma re-added and overlaid with a CMYK-shifted (+0.2 C, -0.1 M, -0.2 Y, K=0) colour mask. Multi Tone Poster (Daodan): 7 luma bands of its 4 default colours with square / square / horizontal-stripe dither patterns between them. Posterize Pixelate (prod80): power-of-two mip block (box average), floor(c x L)/(L-1) posterize (no dither, no border). filters.name: Artistic Vignette / Magical Rectangle
filters.note: Artistic Vignette (luluco250): distance shapes (radial x pi/2, top/bottom, left/right, box, sky = from bottom centre, ground = from top centre) through smoothstep(start, end), mixed to its default black. Magical Rectangle (prod80): soft rectangle / circle in its rotated, diagonal-normalised layer coordinates, layer = image pushed toward the rectangle colour value (default grey 0.5) and recoloured to its hue / saturation (grey), default normal blend; rotation, depth fade and the in-layer exposure / contrast controls are left at their defaults (off)

filters.name: Perfect Perspective / Flexible CA
filters.note: Perfect Perspective (Fubax, arXiv:2003.10558 / 2010.04077): input taken as a rectilinear game frame of horizontal FOV 90 x Amount; each output radius is mapped through the azimuthal projection family k (1 rectilinear, 0.5 stereographic, 0 equidistant, -0.5 equisolid, -1 orthographic): theta = atan(k r f)/k (asin for k<0), source radius = tan(theta) / tan(half FOV), natural vignetting sin(theta)/(r f), mirrored edges; the cropping / aximorphic (separate horizontal/vertical k) options are replaced by a Zoom. Flexible CA (luluco250): per-channel translate (ratio -1/0/1 x 1.5 px x amount) or scale about the centre (1 + amount x 4 px-diagonal, lerped to its reciprocal by ratio)

filters.name: Sharp Contrast / Filmic Anamorph Sharpen
filters.note: Sharp Contrast (Insane-Shaders): gamma-squared luma, 7x7 generalised Kuwahara over 6 angular sectors (sector weight 1/(1+var^4) in its x1023 edge-bias scale), edge multiplier 1-(max-min)/max with distance-weighted extremes, y = c + (c - kuwahara) x 0.667 x strength x edge x 1.5, sqrt, recombined with the original Cb/Cr. Filmic Anamorph Sharpen (Fubax): linear-light high pass from 4 neighbours at its 0.1 px offset (bilinear, so the offset scales the response), x60 strength around 0.5, clamped to [1-clamp, clamp] (0.65), overlay-blended per channel

filters.name: DLAA Plus / CMAA 2 (approx.)
filters.note: DLAA Plus (AstrayFX, after Andreev DLAA GDC 2011): prefilter stores the 4-neighbour edge strength, short-edge pass blends to the 3-tap H/V blur where lambda x contrast exceeds the opposite blur luma (lambda = 5 x short-edge mask), long-edge pass compares 8-tap half-pixel H/V averages of the edge map and slides the pixel toward its neighbours along long edges; text (max channel > 0.994) and dark pixels are preserved. CMAA 2 (approx.): CMAA2-style luma edge detection (threshold 0.07 x 2 x setting, local-contrast adaptation against neighbouring edges), then MLAA-like shape blending: edge runs traced up to 8 px each way, Z / U / L shapes from the crossing edges at both ends, coverage of the reconstructed line at the pixel centre blended with the neighbour across the edge (not the exact Intel shape-handling / deferred-blend compute pipeline)

filters.name: Smart DeNoise / Noise Blur
filters.note: Smart DeNoise (Michele Morrone, GShade port): circular Gaussian (sigma, radius 1.5 sigma) x Gaussian colour-distance weight (threshold), normalised. Noise Blur (CShade): 4x4 concentric-disk taps rotated per pixel by interleaved gradient noise, radius 0.5 x 3 % of the frame, scaled by a radial falloff that leaves the centre sharp (its vignette mask approximated by a linear radial ramp)

filters.name: GREYCstoration (anisotropic LIC smoothing)

filters.name: Repaired HSV Separation / Siril grey_flat
filters.note: RepairedHSVSeparation (PixInsight script, approx.): HSV split where pixels at or above the repair level (saturated star cores) get hue and saturation rebuilt from the nearest ring of unsaturated pixels (saturation-weighted circular hue mean), V kept; outputs the recombined RGB or a single channel. Siril grey_flat: on a mono CFA (flat) image the mean of the R, G (both greens) and B photosites is measured (16x16 grid of 2x2 cells) and R / B sites are scaled to the green mean, equalizing the CFA channels as Siril does for flats with "equalize CFA"

filters.name: ReShade Depth FX (Mesh Edges / Hole Filler / Retro Fog / Volumetric Fog)
filters.note: Linear depth = 1 - D (0 near). Hole Filler (NiceGuy): pixels deeper than >= 2 of their 4 neighbours by T (0.1) get those neighbours averaged in. Retro Fog (luluco250): curved distance fog (x spread by depth), quantized to 255 and 1-bit Bayer 8x8 dithered, its auto fog colour (mean of the 8 border points); Start is offset so the default centre sits at the camera (shader start 0.45), depth span floored at 0.05 against 8-bit depth steps. Volumetric Fog V2 (NiceGuy): 5 a-trous 3x3 passes (radii 81/27/9/3/1 x radius x depth x 8 px at 1080p) taking only samples not nearer than depth-0.1, boosted c/(1+1/boost-c), mixed in by depth^(1-power)

filters.name: Anaglyph to Side-by-Side / Top-Bottom (Depth3D)
filters.note: Depth3D Anaglyph_to_SBS_or_TAB: splits an anaglyph into its two eye views by the glasses filter pair (lens-filtered colour or the scheme mono intensity), packed side-by-side or top-and-bottom (optionally swapped), each eye shifted by half the horizontal separation; zoom / stretch / custom luma weights omitted

filters.name: CMYK Separation (GCR / UCR / UCA / Ink Limit / Hexachrome)
filters.note: Separation from RGB through a density-additive ink model (approx., not an ICC profile): pixel density per R/G/B channel (re paper) -> black generation (UCR = K only in neutral shadows; GCR light/medium/heavy/maximum = increasing grey component replaced by K; UCA adds CMY back under neutral shadows; rich black puts 60/40/40 under solid black) -> CMY solved by inverting the 3x3 ink density matrix; Hexachrome adds orange + green inks (CMYKOG, Pantone 1995), CMYKOGV adds violet, each taking over 85% of its two-ink overlap before CMY is re-solved; total area coverage limit scales the colour inks so C+M+Y(+O+G+V)+K stays under the limit. Views: press proof (inks multiplied on paper), separation plates (each plate printed alone in its ink), total ink coverage before the limit (cyan hatching = over the TAC), proof difference

filters.name: Press Proof (Dot Gain / Misregistration / Trapping / Overprint)
filters.note: Press simulation on a CMYK separation (GCR medium, 300% TAC, density-additive ink model, approx.): dot gain = parabolic tone value increase a + 4g a(1-a) (g = TVI at 50%), compensated = the inverse curve applied to the plates before printing; misregistration shifts the C/M/Y plates 120 deg apart against K; black objects (dark neutral pixels) are set as 100% K and either knock out the colour plates (white/colour gaps appear when misregistered), get trapped (each lighter-colour plate spreads into darker neighbours by the trap width = spread/choke, hiding the gaps) or overprint (overprint preview: the surrounding colour plates continue under the black, no knockout)

filters.name: Quadtone (4-Ink Monotone Print)
filters.note: Photoshop-style quadtone: four inks laid down by their own curves (black in the shadows only, then two mid inks, the lightest ink reaching into the highlights), printed with a density-additive ink model on warm paper; total density rescaled so the print keeps the image tone (approx. preset inks, not Pantone spot data)

filters.name: AM Screening: Euclidean / Elliptical / Hybrid XM / Rosette
filters.note: Amplitude-modulated halftone with PostScript spot functions (Round 1-x2-y2, Euclidean = round below 50% / inverted round above, Adobe Elliptical dot with its 3x+4y-3 split); the threshold for each cell position is its exact rank among 144 sampled spot values, so coverage equals ink area; Hybrid XM keeps a minimum dot (14%) and in highlights / shadows switches to frequency modulation (random dot or hole dropout per cell, approx. of Agfa Sublima / Kodak Staccato hybrids); CMYK uses the classic 15/75/0/45 deg angles (C, M, Y, K) on a GCR separation, Angle error rotates C and M off-angle to show rosette moire

filters.name: Nuke PLogLin / SoftClip / RolloffContrast / CrossTalk
filters.note: Nuke colour nodes on the linearised image x 2^Exposure: PLogLin (Josh Pines log, linRef .18, logRef 445, density/code .002, negative gamma = A; lin to log shows the log code values, log to lin reads the image as log codes); SoftClip (logarithmic compress maps softclip min..max (min = A, max = 1+7B) onto min..1; preserve hue and brightness desaturates toward luma until the max channel is 1; preserve hue and saturation scales the colour down until max = 1); RolloffContrast on display values (contrast = 2.5A about centre .5, soft clip B = quadratic shoulders at both ends, approx. of its bezier shoulders); CrossTalk with linear crossover curves (each channel bleeds into the other two by A-.5 x2, neutral-preserving; Nuke uses user-drawn curves)

filters.name: Filmic Tone Curves (ACES Hill / Romain Guy / Aldridge / Day)

filters.name: Nuke GodRays / VolumeRays

filters.name: Nuke Keyers: HueKeyer / Primatte / Ultimatte / IBK + EdgeExtend
filters.note: Single-frame keyers on a screen colour picked automatically (most green/blue-dominant pixels of a 12x12 grid): HueKeyer = amount curve as a raised-cosine bump around the screen hue (width from Tolerance) with a saturation threshold; Primatte (approx.) = inner/outer shells around the backing colour in a chroma-weighted YUV distance (clear inside, opaque outside, soft between); Ultimatte (approx.) = Vlahos colour difference S - max(other two) normalised by the backing; IBKGizmo pick mode = 1 - (S - (R*rw + other*(1-rw))) / same for the screen colour, rw = weight; despill limits the screen channel; EdgeExtend pushes solid-foreground colour outward under semi-transparent edges (alpha-weighted spiral gather) so fringes lose the screen colour

filters.name: Sixties (Picasa)
filters.note: Picasa 3.9 Sixties approx.: faded, yellowed 1960s print colour (lifted blacks, lower saturation, warm cast) inside a white rounded-corner print border; optional tilt

filters.name: Warmify (Picasa)
filters.note: Picasa Warmify approx.: one-click warming (white balance shifted to roughly +500-1000 K, brightness preserved) with extra saturation on skin-tone hues

filters.name: G'MIC Community Stylize (Turbulent Halftone / Charred Plastic / Whirling Lines / Color Stamp / Metallic Stencils)
filters.note: G'MIC community filters. Turbulent Halftone (iain_turbulent_halftone): per channel (RGB / CMYK / luminance by Variant) the value is averaged 50/50 with an equalised turbulence screen and thresholded at 0.5; screen approx. = line-integral of white noise along a smooth random orientation field (stands in for fx_seamless_turbulence), equalised via a logistic CDF. Charred Plastic (fx_charred_plastic): image + Strength x DoG (sigmas 10% and 40% of the image size x Scale; wide blur on luma, approx.), Gaussian noise sigma 10/255, then normalize_local on luminance with amplitude 2 (= avg + 3 (Y - avg), avg = Gaussian sigma 20 px). Whirling Lines (fx_whirling_lines): blur sigma 30 px, round to steps of 6 (x Strength), gradient norm (Variant 2: Laplacian; Variant 3: negative), ^0.45, cut 40-60% of the range and normalise, light antialias. Color Stamp (fx_colorstamp): Otsu threshold (x Strength) of the RGB norm from a 16x16 sample grid, darken-composited with the colour-quantised (posterised, approx. of k-means quantize 20) blurred image; Variant 2 = B/W only. Metallic Stencils (fx_metallicstencils): Couleurs_Metalliques = noise sigma 22 then luminance replaced by the local gradient orientation angle, composited Darken / Lighten / Overlay (Variant) with a stencil; the lylejk stencil source is no longer published, so the stencil is approx. as luminance above its local mean (sigma 8 px)

filters.name: G'MIC Community Mosaic (Psychedelic Glasswork Tiler / Little Boxy Things / Smoothelate)
filters.note: G'MIC community. Psychedelic Glasswork Tiler (fx_psyglass): stained_glass = gradient-norm edges (threshold Size x 4 / 255) whose colours flood the regions (nearest-edge colour via jump flooding, approx. of the watershed) with dark leading on the influence-zone borders, equalised (min/max stretch, approx.) and grain-merged with itself (opacity Amount B), then array_mirror (Amount A iterations of a 2x2 mirrored array). Little Boxy Things (pr_lilboxy): grid decimation (one sample every Size px), rectangular dilation 40 x A by 60 x B px, sharpen 100000 (inverse diffusion: every non-flat pixel saturates to the channel min or max), erode 2x2. Smoothelate (pr_smoothelate): pixelation (block 8 x Size px), then 3 x [inverse-diffusion sharpen (amount A), Gaussian 0.7, anisotropic smoothing along isophotes (length 12 x B px, approx. of smooth)]. Jump flooding needs float render targets

filters.name: G'MIC Community Line Drawing (Sketchy Ellipses / Line Spam)
filters.note: G'MIC community, per-pixel replay of the drawing loops. Sketchy Ellipses (pr_sketchy_ellipses): 2000 x Amount iterations; each draws 4 + 4 one-pixel ellipse outlines (centres (x,y),(x,x),(y,x),(y,y) in % starting at 35 and drifting by 0.007/0.004 % per step; radius S % of the width, S x 2 % of the height, S grows by uniform(0, 0.04 x Size); angle = i degrees, set B reversed) in black (set A) and white (set B) at random opacity up to 0.3 x Opacity. Line Spam (pr_linespam, style A): 30 x Amount thick lines per quarter turn (4 rotations of the canvas) from (2%, 10i%) to ((N-1-i+101)%, (100-i(N-1-i))%), thickness 3 x Size px growing x1.02, orange (255,85,0) at opacity 0.8 x Opacity on a transparent layer, then alpha-blended over the image

filters.name: G'MIC Community Textures (Reptorian / Martin Souphead generators)
filters.note: G'MIC community generators (input image ignored). Three-Coupled Oscillators (fx_rep_tco): 50 iterations of x += kA - (0.7/2pi) sin(2pi y), y += kB - (0.7/2pi) sin(2pi x_old) from the axis-scaled centred plane (kA = 2pi(0.5 + Variation/2), kB = -pi), |(x,y)| normalised over a 6x6 sample grid, grayscale. Construction Material (_cons_turb, approx.): 8-octave fractal noise (radius 88 x Scale px, damping 2.5) warped by its own intensity (0.19, 0.52), grain noise, range 0-188, emboss relief grain-merged. Color Modulo (rep_color_modulo_texture): channels = y, x and ||x|-|y|| of the centred, rotated (Variation x 180 deg) plane / Scale through modulo 255 (Seed selects regular / continuous / divisive / continuous divisive; default continuous divisive). Binary Alternating Quaddro (rep_binaltquad, 8-bit): bitwise (X op v)+(Y op v) mod 256 with v = 8 x Scale; Seed picks operand (XOR, AND, OR) and style (cracking / glasses / simple); Variation sign = sign of variable 3 (the expression's own int(frac) reduces the comparison to 0 < V). Random Rectangle Division (rep_rrd, own RNG): up to 5 levels of 2-10 uneven splits with 95% continuation, 2 px black borders, gray (or colour when Variation > 0.33) cells; Seed = seed. Spiral RGB (spiral_RGB): channel = sin(2pi r n + angle) with n = (1,3,5) x Scale, Variation < 0 = counter-clockwise. Prime Surface (rep_prime_surface): spiralbw rectangular spiral index (from the top-left corner inward, cells of Scale px) set to 1 where prime; Variation > 0.5 negates the numbering, < -0.5 mirrors x

filters.name: G'MIC Community Warps (Strange Bulger / Logarithmic Distortion / Tiled Zoom / Grouped Pixel Shift)
filters.note: Reptorian (G'MIC community), exact formulas. Strange Bulger (rep_strange_bulger, from Asmageddon's PDN pack): vx = (cX - x)^2 / cX, vy = y^2 / cY (axis X; Y axis swaps roles), source = (x + (x - vx) cos a + (y - vy) sin a, y + (x - vx) sin a + (y - vy) cos a), periodic; Amount scales the displacement. Logarithmic Distortion (rep_logarithmic_pinching_distortion, GUI defaults): centred rotated coords |.| x 512, both axes shifted by Amount x log(ix iy), periodic. Tiled Zoom (rep_tiled_zoom): square tiles of Size % of the half diagonal, each showing its neighbourhood minified by 1 + Amount, outside = black (boundary None). Grouped Pixel Axis-Based Shift (rep_shift_pixel_to_boundary_with_group_pixels, MadJik Gravity): per row / column the pixels with luminance >= threshold (stands in for alpha) are packed toward the position (angle -180..180 = start..end) with influence Amount (0..1); others become black; rows longer than 700 px are sampled

filters.name: Gaussian Blur by Color Space (Reptorian)
filters.note: fx_rep_blur_cs: convert to the colour space (values normalised to 0-1: Lab a,b +128 / 255, LCh C / 134, hues as 0-1 and blurred as plain numbers like G'MIC, so hue wrap-around artefacts are part of the look), Gaussian blur sigma XY then extra X / Y sigma (combined in quadrature), convert back. sRGB = the image re-encoded with the sRGB curve before blurring (G'MIC rgb2srgb); CMYK keeps K in alpha

filters.name: Color Curves: Hue vs Hue / Hue vs Sat / Sat vs Sat / Lum vs Sat (Unity)
filters.note: Unity URP / HDRP Color Curves (ColorGradingLut): Hue vs Hue adds curve(hue) - 0.5 to the hue; Hue vs Sat, Sat vs Sat and Lum vs Sat multiply saturation by 2 x curve(key) (Saturation() = lerp(Rec.709 luminance, colour, s)), all on linear colour. The hand-drawn curve is stood in for by a flat 0.5 curve plus one Gaussian bump (key position, width, amount; circular for hue)

filters.name: Blue Correction / Expand Gamut (Unreal tonemapper)
filters.note: Unreal Engine film tonemapper colour stage (PostProcessCombineLUTs): in ACEScg (AP1, sRGB D65 -> D60 Bradford) bright saturated colours are pushed outward, ExpandAmount = (1 - 2^(-4 |chroma - 1|^2)) (1 - 2^(-4 ExpandGamut Y^2)), with the Wide_2_XYZ -> AP1 x AP1_2_sRGB matrix; then BlueCorrection lerps toward the ACES Academy blue-light-artifact LMT matrix (AP0, here pre-converted to AP1). UE re-applies the inverse blue matrix after its film curve; with no film curve here only the forward correction is shown. Scene exposure scales the linear input before and undoes it after (expansion depends on brightness); defaults are UE's 0.6 / 1.0

filters.name: Screen-Space AO II (SAO / MSVO / SSIL)
filters.note: from the depth map (D: 1 = near; view position = (screen xy, 0.5 D)). SAO: McGuire, Mara & Luebke 2012 reference estimator, 24 spiral taps (7 turns, per-pixel rotation), A = max(0, 1 - intensity / r^6 x 5 / N x sum (r^2 - v.v)^3 max((v.n - bias) / (v.v + eps), 0)). MSVO: Unity PPv2 multi-scale volumetric obscurance, approx.: Loos & Sloan 2010 volumetric obscurance (occupied fraction of a sphere column) at radii r, r/2, r/4, r/8, combined with min. SSIL: Godot 4 screen-space indirect lighting, approx.: one-bounce gather of nearby colours weighted by both cosines and distance, image used as albedo. Depth-aware 5x5 bilateral blur

filters.name: ImageMagick Hit-and-Miss Kernels (Peaks / Ridges / Diagonals)
filters.note: ImageMagick -morphology HitAndMiss on grey levels, per channel: min of the foreground neighbours minus max of the background neighbours, clipped at 0, union (Lighten) over the kernel set. Peaks (default 0,0 = 7x7 ring 7 < r^2 <= 11; or inner,outer radii): centre foreground, ring background. Ridges (Ridges:1): "3x1: 0,1,0" and its 90 degree rotation. Diagonals: "3: 0,0,0 0,-,1 1,1,-" and "3: 0,0,1 0,-,1 0,1,-" with mirror expansion (8 kernels)

filters.name: ImageMagick Morphology: Smooth / ErodeIntensity / DilateIntensity
filters.note: ImageMagick -morphology: Smooth = Open then Close (erode, dilate, dilate, erode; per channel, flat kernel); ErodeIntensity / DilateIntensity copy the whole pixel whose intensity (Rec.709 luma) is lowest / highest inside the kernel, so no new colours appear. Kernels Diamond (|x|+|y| <= r), Square, Disk (x^2+y^2 <= (r+0.5)^2), Plus

filters.name: Pratt Edge Operators (Pixel Difference / Separated / Boxcar / Truncated Pyramid)
filters.note: Pratt, Digital Image Processing (ch. 15, first-order derivative edge detection): pixel difference row [0 1 -1] / column [-1 1]^T; separated pixel difference row [1 0 -1] / column [-1 0 1]^T; boxcar N x N (each row 1..1 0 -1..-1, scale 1/(N (N-1)/2), 1/21 for 7x7); truncated pyramid N x N with weight min(h+1-|col|, h+1-|row|) (the 7x7 mask normalised by 1/34); column gradient = transposed mask; magnitude = sqrt(G_R^2 + G_C^2) on luminance

filters.name: Ignite Distortions (Energy / Fluid / Pond Ripple / Smoke / Block / Vortex)
filters.note: HitFilm / Ignite Pro distortions (approx. of the look; Variation = noise phase): Energy = ridged domain-warped fbm displacement with slight RGB split and blue filament glow; Fluid = 5-step advection along a curl-noise (divergence-free) field; Pond Ripple = damped concentric radial ripples from the centre with slope shading; Smoke = vertically stretched warped fbm wisps; Block = rows of random-width blocks, about half shifted; Vortex = jittered grid of vortices (random spin, quadratic falloff)

filters.name: Ignite Light (Light Streaks / Gleam / Hyperdrive / Dimension Rift)
filters.note: HitFilm / Ignite Pro light effects (look approx.): Light Streaks = two-sided streak gathered from the bright-pass along Angle (exponential falloff over Length); Gleam = 6-ray star (3 lines 60 deg apart) + small halo from the bright-pass; Hyperdrive = warp-speed star streaks radiating from the centre (3 angular layers, density from Threshold) over a darkened zoom-blurred plate; Dimension Rift = glowing jagged tear of half-length Length through the centre (Threshold = opening), swirling fbm energy inside, light pushes the plate away from it

filters.name: Ignite Derez / Dot Matrix
filters.note: HitFilm / Ignite Pro (look approx.): Derez (Video Game High School) = left-to-right noisy dissolve front - blocks grow in powers of two, scatter, pick up a cyan rim and drop out to black as Amount (progress) rises; Dot Matrix = round LED dots on a dark panel, each dot coloured by its cell average, Amount = dot size, Variation = dot glow

filters.name: Crush Blacks & Whites
filters.note: Ignite Pro / HitFilm Crush Blacks & Whites: values below the black point go to black and above the white point to white, linear stretch between; Softness rounds both knees (softplus clamp)

filters.note: Ignite Pro / HitFilm Custom Gray: monochrome from user channel weights (Normalize divides by their sum so overall brightness is kept)

filters.name: Trapezoid Transform (Substance)

filters.name: digiKam Distortion FX (Caricature / Multiple Corners / Waves)

filters.name: Universe Retro (MisFire / RetroGrade / Analog / AV Club / Holomatrix II)
filters.note: single-frame approximations of Maxon Red Giant Universe stylizers (help.maxon.net parameter docs; time-based flicker / weave / frame-rate effects frozen to one seeded state): MisFire = gate weave, warp, fading, funk, splotches, dust, micro / deep / basic scratches, colour + luma grain, desaturation, vignette, flicker, post contrast; RetroGrade = 4:3 rounded faded frame, slight blur, colour process tint, film fading, grain, dust, hair, vignette; Analog = barrel curvature, chroma split, glow, scan lines + RGB triad mask, static, interference bar; AV Club = block pixelate + colour quantize, separated source, hue-noisy dilated edge band, 45 degree shadow, post noise; Holomatrix II = line-band displacement, RGB split, low-res mix, three-tone blue colorize, interference ghost, glow, scan lines, static

filters.name: Universe Finish (Finisher / ShrinkRay / ChromaTown / Spectralicious)
filters.note: single-frame approximations of Maxon Red Giant Universe: Finisher = unsharp detail, enhanced contrast (S-curve on the extremes only), contrast, saturation (the 16 named look LUTs are undocumented and not included); ShrinkRay = rotated focus band, Gaussian blur outside it with highlight gain, saturation and contrast; ChromaTown = 30 samples along a start-to-end zoom (+ rotation) transform tinted by a spectrum and colour-normalised (smooth in/out falloff); Spectralicious = 6 coloured points blended by inverse-distance weights (Spread = Radius), shown over the image at 50% (approx.)

filters.name: Copernicus Grunge Generators (Bark Strips / Birch Bark / Galvanized Steel / Leaking Streaks / Mold Spots / Wipe Trails)
filters.note: Houdini Copernicus grunge generators (look approx. of the layered-noise nodes from the SideFX docs): Bark Strips = inflated vertical strips with edge breakup + horizontal cuts (secondary) + elongated vertical cells (tertiary swirls); Birch Bark = cellular base patches + horizontal lenticel dashes + vertical cracks; Galvanized Steel = distorted Worley spangle crystals, each with its own grey level and an oriented in-cell gradient; Leaking Streaks = vertically distorted streaks fading downwards + background horizontal folds + tertiary highlights; Mold Spots = three spot layers (primary Worley blobs, secondary / tertiary noise spots) with fuzzy spread; Wipe Trails = broken circular wipe rings (foreground) over fainter background rings. Mask contrast as in the node (around 0.5); seeded

filters.name: Copernicus Patterns (Bubble Noise / Chladni / Cell Pattern / Tile Pattern)
filters.note: Houdini Copernicus generators: Bubble Noise = fractal octaves of folded noise, each octave domain-warped (Shape = Distortion) which compresses / expands it into bubbles; Chladni Cymatic Patterns = interference of two waves with swapped frequencies, z = cos(n pi x)cos(m pi y) - cos(m pi x)cos(n pi y) with non-integer m = n*2^anisotropy (Shape), output Nodal Lines or Absolute Value; Cell Pattern = Worley cells on a grid or hexagonal lattice with gap, bevel (Shape) and random height; Tile Pattern = stretcher (running) bond, herringbone 2:1 and basketweave layouts with Inset (Shape) and per-tile value variation. approx. of the node parameter sets; seeded

filters.name: Hyperbolic Tile (Copernicus)
filters.note: Houdini Copernicus Hyperbolic Tile: regular hyperbolic {p,q} tiling of the Poincare disk; points are folded into the central polygon by repeated inversion in the polygon edge circles (circle centre c = cos(pi/q)/D, radius r = sin(pi/p)/D, D = sqrt(cos^2(pi/q) - sin^2(pi/p)), orthogonal to the unit circle), so copies are reflected and inverted toward the boundary; outside the disk the pattern is mirrored by inversion. Rectanglize maps the square image onto the disk (elliptic grid or FG-squircle). The polygon-per-vertex count replaces the node Size / Flattening controls (it fixes the polygon size); uv = image fitted in the polygon (mirror-repeated near the corners)

filters.name: Planar Inflate (Copernicus)
filters.note: Houdini Copernicus Planar Inflate: the region (pixels on the minority side of Threshold, i.e. light shapes on dark or dark shapes on light; the node uses an SDF) is inflated by solving the Poisson equation lap(h) = -f inside, h = 0 outside, with Jacobi iterations on a coarse-to-fine stride ladder (32 > 16 > 8 > 4 > 2 > 1 px, 19 sweeps), a round pillow profile; output height = sqrt-shaped solution x Height scale (approx. of the node Pre Scale / Height Scale), optional fractal Mounds noise, shaded (Lambert + specular) or tangent normal map

filters.name: Height to Caustics (Copernicus)
filters.note: Houdini Copernicus Height to Caustics, approx.: luma = refractive height; per pixel the light ray (directional, azimuth 45 deg, altitude as set) is refracted through the surface normal (Snell, IOR, default 1.33 water) and travels Ground depth to a flat ground plane; photons are gathered back with a small Gaussian splat (25x25 window, displacement capped at 11 px) and normalised so a flat surface = 1 (shown as mid-grey); dispersion = per-channel IOR +/- 0.03 (Perturbation method)

filters.name: Edge Detect by Normal (Copernicus)
filters.note: Houdini Copernicus Edge Detect by Normal: crease lines of variable width; each neighbour within the Thickness radius whose normal has dot(n, n_neighbour) below Normal tolerance votes for an edge, Gaussian-weighted (Edge spread scales the sigma); normals read from a tangent normal map or derived from luma as height (approx.: plain neighbour comparison instead of the node ray differentials)

filters.name: Illegal Pixel (Copernicus)
filters.note: Houdini Copernicus Illegal Pixel: finds NaN / Inf (float images; never present in 8-bit input) or values matching a Custom rule against Compare value, per component or on luma; fixes by blending the legal neighbours (nearest square ring with a legal value, up to 6 px, only the bad components replaced), zeroes the whole pixel, highlights in magenta, or isolates (bad = magenta, good = black)

filters.name: Surface Dither (Copernicus)
filters.note: Houdini Copernicus Surface Dither (2-D image case, UV = image coordinates, dotscale = darkness): round halftone dots on a rotated grid built as a signed distance field (min over the 3x3 neighbouring dots, radius sqrt(darkness) x 0.707 cell) and output raw (SDF, 0.5 = edge, in cell units) or converted to a black / white mask at Iso offset with a 1 px smooth; single texture level (no level transitions)

filters.name: NewBlue Imagine / Excite Paint (Mural / Paper Collage / Pencil Rubbing / Hand Drawn / Color Melt)
filters.note: NewBlue Stylizers looks (approx., from the product descriptions): Mural = smoothed, hue / value-posterised colour with directional shading and soft edge darkening on a wall texture; Paper Collage = luma split into coloured paper strata (Color levels) with drop shadows cast by the higher layers; Pencil Rubbing = pencil hatching whose density follows darkness, revealed through paper grain, plus edge strokes; Hand Drawn = dark DoG lines over vibrant, partly posterised colours; Color Melt = colours expanded and softened by a saturation-weighted wide gather, then brightened (lava-lamp look)

filters.name: NewBlue Illuminate (Halovision Plus / Light Bender / Spinning Light / Starlight)
filters.note: NewBlue Stylizers Illuminate light effects (approx., from the product descriptions): Halovision Plus = bokeh-like halo rings gathered from highlights above Threshold (disc of radius Size, rim-weighted); Light Bender = curved flares, highlights smeared along circular arcs in four bent directions; Spinning Light = swirling radial rays of light from the image centre plus a swirl-zoom gather of nearby highlights; Starlight = sparse highlight specks turned into 8-point stars whose arm angle drifts across the frame (rotating specks); seeded

filters.name: Shear Energy (NewBlue)
filters.note: NewBlue Shear Energy (approx., from "a shear, blended motion effect by blurring the image on two axes"): two off-centre motion blurs along two axes averaged, blended with the image and with their lighter-than-image energy added on top

filters.name: NewBlue Detail by Chroma / Detail by Luma / Dual Booster
filters.note: NewBlue Video Essentials detail tools (approx., from the product descriptions): Detail by Chroma = unsharp detail and contrast boosted only inside a hue region (Gaussian hue window ~25 deg around Target hue, saturation-gated); Detail by Luma = separate detail gain for the high and the low regions, shadow detail cored to compensate for the noise increase; Dual Booster = lightest and darkest regions adjusted separately (shadows deepened, highlights lifted, vibrance + detail boosted in both)
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Enhance Dark Holes (CellProfiler)
filters.note: CellProfiler EnhanceOrSuppressFeatures > Enhance > Dark holes (centrosome enhance_dark_holes): image inverted so holes are peaks; holes with radius in [min, max] = difference between the openings of the inverted image at radius min and at radius max + 1 (CellProfiler sums the successive differences of openings by reconstruction with a cross element, keeping the per-step maximum; approx.: plain openings with a square element)

filters.name: Enhance DIC (CellProfiler)
filters.note: CellProfiler EnhanceOrSuppressFeatures > Enhance > DIC (centrosome line_integration, Kam 1998 style): Gaussian smoothing (sigma = Smoothing) perpendicular to the shear direction, then integration along the shear axis with exponential decay, (forward sum - reverse sum) / 2 = sum_k decay^k (s[i-k] - s[i+k]) / 2 (truncated at weight 0.003, max 160 px); output as 0.5 + gain x result
passes: float a=radians(u_p0);vec2 dP=vec2(cos(a),-sin(a));return blur1d(u_tex,uv,dP,R(u_p2)*2.);

filters.name: Morph Operations (CellProfiler: branchpoints / clean / diag / spur / vbreak)
filters.note: CellProfiler Morph binary operations on the thresholded image (1 working pixel grid): branchpoints = keep only skeleton pixels with 3 or more branches (0-to-1 transitions around the 8-neighbour ring; run after Skeletonize); clean = remove isolated pixels; diag = fill a background pixel whose two 4-neighbours meet diagonally across a background corner (removes 8-connectivity of the background); spur = remove pixels with exactly one 8-neighbour (line end points); vbreak = remove the centre of a horizontal bridge between vertical lines (1 0 1 / 1 1 1 / 1 0 1); clean, diag and spur repeat up to Repeat count (CellProfiler Once / Custom), the others run once as in CellProfiler

filters.name: OpenLines (CellProfiler Morph)
filters.note: CellProfiler Morph openlines: union of openings (erosion then dilation) with linear structuring elements of the given length, keeping structures that contain a line of that many pixels in some direction and suppressing dots of the same size; 4 orientations (0 / 45 / 90 / 135 deg; CellProfiler rotates the line in finer steps) - approx.

filters.name: gThumb Special Effects (Arctic / Cherry / Mango / Desert)
filters.note: gThumb (src/Ext/Editor/SpecialEffects/*.vala) curve presets, exact control points: per-channel R / G / B curves then the Value curve (Desert) through the value map; gth_bezier curves = cubic Bezier per interval with control-point x at 1/3 and 2/3 and y from the neighbour slopes (GIMP 2.8 style), rounded to 8 bits; outside the first / last point the end value is held

filters.name: Blurred Edges (gThumb)
filters.note: gThumb gth_image_progressive_blur: separable Gaussian (horizontal then vertical) whose radius grows with the distance d from the image centre: radius = round(20 x Amount x clamp(d - m, 0, m + 100) / (m + 100)) with m = min(w, h) / 2 / 4, sigma = (2 radius + 1) / 6, no blur where radius <= 1 (weights renormalised)

filters.name: Multi Direction Lee Filter (SAGA)
filters.note: SAGA grid_filter Multi Direction Lee Filter (Lee 1980; Selige, Bohner & Ringeler 2006): 16 directional 9x9 line masks (weight 1 on the line, 0.5 on the adjacent cells when Weighted); the direction with minimum (weighted) standard deviation of luma gives mean m and sigma; Lee gain b = (sigma^2 - n^2) / sigma^2, out = x b + (1 - b) m (mean when sigma <= n); noise n absolute or relative to the image mean of the minimum std dev (single pass; the Ringeler variant with its correction table is not included); colour: per-channel means along the chosen direction with the luma gain

params.label: Method
opts: Noise relative to mean std dev

filters.name: Majority / Minority Filter (SAGA)
filters.note: SAGA grid_filter Majority/Minority Filter (Conrad 2010), circle kernel: the most (Majority) or least (Minority) frequent value in the window replaces the cell when its count is > threshold x kernel size (Majority) or < (1 - threshold) x kernel size (Minority), threshold in percent (default 0); for colour images the classes are colours quantised to Levels per channel and the replacement is the first window pixel of that class; ties = first in scan order

filters.name: Olympus / OM System Art Filters (Pale and Light Color, Light Tone, Gentle Sepia, Dramatic Tone, Grainy Film, Key Line, Punk, Fragmented, White Edge)
filters.note: Olympus / OM System art filters, look approximations from the camera manuals (OM-5 II etc.): Pale and Light Color = slight overexposure + light scatter, warm airy pastel; Light Tone = shadows and highlights softened; Gentle Sepia = shadows opened, soft sepia; Dramatic Tone = strong local contrast (image minus Gaussian, radius 8x size) + vignette, colour or B and W; Grainy Film = rough high-contrast B and W with grain; Key Line = black Sobel outlines over matte colours; Punk (Magic Filter, mju-7050) = pink and black block print (adaptive threshold); Fragmented (Magic Filter, TG) = mosaic of shifted / scaled tiles; White Edge art effect = white fade towards the frame edge. approx., not Olympus code
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p3*8.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p3*8.));

filters.name: Olympus Picture Modes (i-Enhance / Color Creator)
filters.note: Olympus picture modes, approx.: i-Enhance = saturation boost weighted toward the dominant scene hue (saturation-weighted hue mean on a 12x12 grid) + mild contrast; Color Creator = whole-image colour cast toward the chosen hue (30 hue steps on the camera) and saturation in 8 levels (-4..+3)

filters.name: Sony Picture Effects (Pop Color / Retro Photo / Soft High-key / High Contrast Mono)
filters.note: Sony Picture Effect, look approximations from the Sony help guide: Pop Color = vivid emphasised colour; Retro Photo = faded colour with sepia tones; Soft High-key = bright, airy, soft (glow from a 12 px Gaussian, slight cool); High Contrast Mono = high-contrast B and W. approx.
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(12.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(12.));

filters.name: Sony Creative Style / Creative Look (Autumn Leaves, Clear, Deep, Light, Sunset, VV2, FL, IN, SH)
filters.note: Sony Creative Style / Creative Look, look approximations from the Sony help guide descriptions: Autumn Leaves = reds and yellows emphasised, greens nudged yellow, warm; Clear = clean bright highlights; Deep = darker, dense colour; Light = bright, low contrast; Sunset = warm, reds emphasised; VV2 = brighter higher-saturation vivid; FL = calm muted colour with crisp contrast and cool shadows; IN = matte, low contrast and saturation; SH = bright, soft, airy. Contrast / Saturation in camera steps -3..+3. approx.

filters.name: iMovie Filters (Blast, Blockbuster, Dreamy, Western, Camo, Comic Vintage, Silent Era)
filters.note: Apple iMovie clip filters, look approximations (Apple publishes no formulas): Blast = blown-out warm high-key; Blockbuster = teal shadows / orange highlights, contrast; Dreamy = soft screen glow (10 px Gaussian); Western = warm amber desaturated with vignette; Camo = olive-green duotone; Comic Vintage = posterised colour, ink edges, halftone dots on yellowed paper; Silent Era = B and W, flicker, grain, vertical scratches, heavy vignette (seeded). approx.
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(10.));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(10.));

filters.name: Film Stock Emulation V (Kodak Pro Image 100, LomoChrome Color 92, Ferrania P30, ADOX Silvermax 100)
filters.note: G'MIC Simulate Film stocks, data-driven look approximations from published film character, NOT the G'MIC CLUT data: Kodak Pro Image 100 = warm consumer neg, rich reds, gentle contrast, fine grain; LomoChrome Color 92 = warm nostalgic 90s colour, faded green-black base, heavy grain; Ferrania P30 = high-contrast cine B and W, deep blacks, red-leaning pan; ADOX Silvermax 100 = long tonal scale, bright highlights, fine grain. approx.

filters.name: Color Slice (DaVinci Resolve)
filters.note: DaVinci Resolve 19 Color Slice palette, approx.: six vector slices (R Y G C B M centres every 60 deg, smooth +-45 deg window) plus a Skin slice (25 deg, mid-saturation, not in shadows); per slice hue rotate, saturation and subtractive density (darkens in proportion to saturation, like the Resolve density control). Weighting is our own, not Blackmagic code

filters.name: Fibonacci Bokeh (lygia)
filters.note: lygia filter/fibonacciBokeh (after Xor): 100 taps on a golden-angle spiral (rotation matrix -0.737/0.676, radius step s += 1/s), gathered in linear (gamma 2.2). Uniform mode scales the spiral so its outer tap is at Radius; lygia mode keeps the original position-dependent radius gradient. Gain = lygia amount (1/(1.001-amount) pre-gain)

filters.name: RYB Hue Shift (lygia artist colour wheel)
filters.note: lygia color/hueShiftRYB: rgb2ryb -> HSL hue rotate -> ryb2rgb. Trilinear = lygia default (cubic-smoothed trilinear interpolation of the 8 cube corners, Gossett and Chen 2004 / Sugita 2015); Fast = lygia RYB_FAST homogeneous conversion. lygia's function passes PI instead of its angle argument; here the angle is used

filters.name: lygia Palettes (Zorn / Wada Sanzo / Ridgway / Flexoki)
filters.note: lygia color/palette data: Zorn = lygia pigments (titanium white, yellow ochre, cadmium red, ivory black) plus 1:3 / 1:1 / 3:1 and tint mixes in linear RGB (approx. of paint mixing, 34 colours); Wada Sanzo (157 in lygia), Ridgway 1912 (1107) reduced to 48-colour farthest-point OKLab subsets; Flexoki = its 23 distinct lygia values. Nearest colour in OKLab with Bayer dither on L, or luma ramp through the L-sorted palette

filters.name: Reinhard-Jodie Tone Map (lygia)
filters.note: lygia color/tonemap/reinhardJodie: mix(x/(L+1), x/(x+1), x/(x+1)) with L = Rec.709 luminance, so saturated highlights desaturate smoothly toward the per-channel curve; applied in linear light after an exposure gain. Per-channel and luminance Reinhard for comparison

filters.name: Untile (Quilez texture-repetition breakup, lygia)
filters.note: lygia sample/untile = Inigo Quilez "texture repetition" technique 1: the image is tiled N times and each Voronoi cell samples it with a random offset, Gaussian-weighted (exp(-falloff d^2)) over 3x3 cells with contrast-preserving variance normalisation (mean taken from the image; lygia uses a constant 0.3). Fast = suslik variant of IQ technique 3 (index from a low-frequency noise lookup, here value noise instead of a noise texture)

filters.name: psrdnoise (periodic rotating simplex noise, lygia)
filters.note: lygia generative/psrdnoise 2D (Gustavson and McEwan 2022): tiling simplex noise with optional integer period and rotating gradients (alpha) plus analytic gradient; Flow fBm = 5 octaves, each rotating faster and domain-warped by the accumulated gradient (the authors' flow-noise demo); Gradient output = analytic derivative as a normal map

filters.name: Gerstner Waves Heightmap (lygia)
filters.note: lygia generative/gerstnerWave (after Catlike Coding): sum of 4 Gerstner waves (wavelength ratios 1 / .61 / .37 / .23, spread directions, steepness split so the sum never loops); the horizontal displacement is inverted with 3 fixed-point iterations so the output is a true heightfield over the image grid; normal from the analytic tangent / binormal (tangent starts at (1,0,0), binormal at (0,0,1) as in the tutorial). Time = 0

filters.name: Bead, Stitch & Hook Patterns (Perler / Loom / Needlepoint / Latch-hook / Crochet)
filters.note: craft-pattern looks (approx.): the image is averaged per cell and posterised (levels per channel); Perler = ironed fuse beads (ring tube shading, centre hole, pegboard between beads); loom beadwork = aligned cylinder beads, horizontal holes, warp threads in the gaps; needlepoint = slanted tent stitches (half cross) as plied yarn on a canvas mesh; latch-hook = jittered shaggy yarn tufts with radial fibre texture; tapestry crochet = single-crochet stitches (top loop bar + leaning post)

filters.name: Woven Textiles (Jacquard / Tapestry / Ikat)
filters.note: woven-textile looks (approx.): Jacquard = black warp, image-coloured weft; each thread crossing shows the weft when the luminance beats an 8-shaft satin rank (step 3), so tone becomes satin / twill-like floats with dips where threads change sides; tapestry = weft-faced picks over warp pairs in brick rows, posterised colour with alternating hatching at colour borders; ikat = posterised weft dyed before weaving: each weft thread shifted by a random amount and smeared along its length (feather), on a plain-weave texture

filters.name: Resist Dyeing (Batik / Tie-dye / Shibori)
filters.note: resist-dye looks (approx.): batik = image posterised into dye baths on cotton, wax crackle veins (warped Voronoi cell borders) dyed dark in the waxed (lighter) areas; tie-dye = the image swirled into a spiral and saturated, with white fold-resist arms bleeding into the dye; shibori = indigo vat dye whose depth follows the image darkness, with itajime (mirrored fold grid + clamped squares), arashi (pole-wrapped diagonal pleats) or kumo (bound spider-web circles) resist patterns and capillary bleed

filters.name: Print Processes (Gravure / Letterpress / Flexo / Inkjet / Laser / Gocco / Dye-sub)
filters.note: print-process looks (approx.): CMYK (GCR) separations at 15/75/0/45 deg; gravure = rotated screens of square engraved cells, ink density = tone (variable depth) with walls that thin in the shadows and missing dots in highlights; letterpress = single-ink halftone with ink squeeze (dark rims, starved mottled interior) and a debossed paper impression; flexo = dot gain plus the doughnut halo (heavy rim, light centre, faint outer ring); inkjet = stochastic drops with per-pass density banding and dead-nozzle lines; laser = AM halftone with toner specks scattered near printed dots; Gocco = a few flat spot inks (hue / saturation / value quantised) with mesh texture, uneven thickness, misregistration and skips; dye-sub = continuous tone, slight dye diffusion, panel misregistration and faint head lines

filters.name: Map Projections II (conic / azimuthal / Eckert / G'MIC)
filters.note: forward map projections with the image taken as an equirectangular (plate carree) world map, fitted uniformly into the frame (outside the map = black), Snyder 1987 formulas inverted per pixel: Albers equal-area conic, equidistant conic and Lambert conformal conic on the two standard parallels (LCC cut at 80 deg toward the far pole); azimuthal equidistant and Lambert azimuthal equal-area centred on (central meridian, centre latitude); cylindrical equal-area with the given standard parallel (30 = Behrmann, 45 = Gall-Peters); Eckert IV and VI; G'MIC Triangular Projection (Jarventaus): naive linear row squeeze to the pole width (Parallel 2 / 90; 0.5 = Eckert I-like). Orthographic and sinusoidal: see Map Projections (mapproj)

filters.name: Rotate Equirectangular Map (G'MIC)
filters.note: G'MIC rotate_equirectangular_map (Kristian Jarventaus) ported exactly: each output pixel -> unit-sphere point (theta = pi + 2 pi x/w, phi = pi y/h) -> roll / pitch / yaw rotation matrix (or its reverse) -> back to equirectangular coordinates

filters.name: Halo Removal II (YAHR / BlindDeHalo3 / EdgeCleaner)
filters.note: single-frame ports (approx.) of the AviSynth / VapourSynth dehalo scripts, per RGB channel: YAHR (Didee) = clp - (b1D - repair(b1D, w1b1D)) with b1 = MinBlur(r=2) + [1 2 1] (3x3 median stands in for the 5x5 CTMF) and w1 = an aWarpSharp2-style warp (Sobel mask, 5x5 blur, depth 32 x Strength) - repair approximated by the 3x3 min/max clamp; BlindDeHalo3 (Didee 2005) = blurred copy (Gaussian ~ the rx down/up-size), TWK_HLIGHT curve h = TWK + (128 - TWK) TWK / 128 with TWK = |x - blur| strength rx / 12 (lodamp = hidamp = 0) subtracted from luma, masked by 4 x the local range of the blur; EdgeCleaner = AWarpSharp2(depth = strength / 2) repaired to the source 3x3 range, merged through the inverted, levelled (4..32) Prewitt mask box-blurred 3x3
passes: int md=int(u_p0+.5);if(md==1)return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(1.2*u_p1));vec2 g=sobel(uv);return vec4(vec3(clamp(length(g)*1.5,0.,1.)),1.);

filters.name: Vinverse / SangNom2 (comb and aliasing repair)
filters.note: Vinverse (tritical / Didee, VS port by HolyWu / Asd-g) exactly per RGB channel: pb3 = vertical [1 2 1], pb6 = [1 4 6 4 1] of pb3; d1 = src - pb3, d2 = (pb3 - pb6) x sstr; out = pb3 + (the smaller-magnitude of d1, d2; x scl when they disagree in sign); Vinverse2 uses the vertical sbr (blur-difference highpass) instead of pb3. SangNom2 (approx.): the other field is dropped and re-interpolated by edge-directed averaging (best of 7 directions by 3-pixel SAD); AA mode repeats it on columns

filters.name: MSmooth (masked smoother, tritical)
filters.note: MSmooth (AviSynth, tritical) single-frame: edge mask = 3x3-box-blurred luma differs across the pixel (4 directions) by more than Threshold (8-bit); non-edge pixels are replaced Strength times by the mean of their non-edge 3x3 neighbours, so smoothing never crosses detected edges (approx. of the original mask / blur iteration)

filters.name: FFT3DFilter (2D Wiener, single frame)
filters.note: FFT3DFilter (Fizick) bt=1 mode, one frame, luma only: 16x16 blocks with 50% overlap (4 shifted grids), per-block 2D DFT computed as a Hartley transform (|F|^2 = C^2 + S^2), Wiener factor max((|F|^2 - sigma^2) / |F|^2, (beta - 1) / beta) with sigma in 8-bit units, optional high-frequency sharpen gain, inverse transform and sin^2 window overlap-add; chroma untouched; pixels within 8 px of the right / top border may stay unfiltered

filters.name: VariBlur (Fusion)
filters.note: Fusion VariBlur (approx.): per-pixel blur radius = Blur size x the chosen blur channel (0 = sharp, 1 = full size), separable Gaussian (soften) or box with the radius of the pixel being written in each pass

filters.name: Dent (Fusion)
filters.note: Fusion Dent (approx.: the exact Fusion warp curves are undocumented): a circular warp of the given size around the frame centre; Dent 1 = power-law bulge / pinch, Kaleidoscope = 6-way mirrored angle with an inverted dent, Dent 2 = sinusoidal radial displacement, Dent 3 = swirl-like deform growing toward the centre, Cosine dent = angular fracture creases toward the centre, Sine dent = smooth rounded sine-squared dent

filters.name: Day Sky (Fusion, Preetham)
filters.note: Fusion Day Sky (approx.; generator, input ignored): Preetham, Shirley & Smits 1999 analytic daylight with the Perez distribution in Yxy for the given turbidity, sun position from latitude, day of year and solar time (declination 0.4093 sin(2 pi (J - 81) / 368)), rendered as a lat-long of the upper hemisphere (azimuth across, horizon at the bottom, zenith at the top) with a sun disk, exposure-tone-mapped 1 - exp(-k Y / Yzenith); the sky fades out with the sun below the horizon

filters.name: Ultra Keyer (Fusion)
filters.note: Fusion Ultra Keyer core (approx.): colour-difference matte (screen channel minus the larger other channel), normalised by the strongest screen difference found on a 12x12 grid of the frame, with clip black / clip white matte levels; screen-colour despill limits the screen channel to the larger other channel; composite over grey, matte or premultiplied despilled foreground

filters.name: Z to World Position (Fusion)
filters.note: Fusion Z to World Pos (approx.): the depth map (1 = near) is taken as linear camera distance between Near and Far, each pixel is unprojected through a pinhole camera of the given vertical FOV at the origin looking down -Z: position shown as RGB (X, Y scaled to the far frustum, -Z / Far), Euclidean distance, or the normal from the cross product of the position derivatives

filters.name: Membrane Projections (Weka)
filters.note: Trainable Weka Segmentation membrane projections: a patch-size line kernel (thickness 1, normalised by its length) rotated in 30 steps of 6 deg is correlated with the luminance, and the 30 responses are projected per pixel as sum, mean, standard deviation, median, max or min (Weka default patch 19)

filters.name: Lipschitz Filter (Weka)
filters.note: Trainable Weka Segmentation Lipschitz filter (Stencel): Lipschitz cover with the given slope (8-bit levels per pixel, diagonal slope x sqrt 2): downhill = upper cover max over y of f(y) - slope d(x, y), uphill = lower cover; top-hat = cover minus image (shown x gain); approx.: the two raster sweeps of the original are replaced by jump propagation (steps 32..1, 2, 1), per RGB channel

filters.name: Pentax Custom Image (Muted / Reversal Film / Radiant / Flat)
filters.note: Pentax Custom Image looks (approx. from the K-series manuals): Muted = low saturation and contrast; Reversal Film = slide-film contrast, deep blacks, slightly cool; Radiant = vivid saturated high-contrast warm; Flat = very low contrast and saturation for grading; Saturation / Contrast / Key = the in-camera fine-tune sliders

filters.name: Pentax Digital Filter (Tone Expansion / Unicolor Bold / Bold Monochrome)
filters.note: Pentax Digital Filters (approx. from the manual descriptions): Tone Expansion = HDR-like compressed global tone with expanded local detail (24 px base); Unicolor Bold = one hue kept and boosted, everything else high-contrast B&W; Bold Monochrome = hard high-contrast B&W with local contrast and a strong vignette

filters.name: Slim (Pentax Digital Filter)
filters.note: Pentax Slim digital filter (16 steps): changes the horizontal / vertical ratio at the same output size; + stretches vertically (subjects look slimmer, top and bottom cropped), - stretches horizontally; up to 20% (approx. range)

filters.name: Ricoh Image Control (HDR Tone / Positive / Negative Film / Monotones / Hi-contrast B&W)
filters.note: Ricoh GR Image Control looks (approx. from the GR manuals): HDR Tone = local tone compression with boosted detail (20 px base); Positive Film = vivid high-contrast slide; Negative Film = soft, desaturated, lifted cyan-black / warm-white print; Soft / Hard Monotone = low / high contrast B&W; Hi-contrast B&W = extreme push-processed contrast, grain and vignette; Toning = sepia (+) / cool (-) for the monochromes

filters.name: Lumix Creative Control
filters.note: Panasonic Lumix Creative Control (approx. from the Lumix manuals): Expressive = pop saturated colour; Retro = faded yellowed print; Old Days = bright, desaturated, warm, vignetted; Toy Pop = bright vivid with darkened corners; Fantasy = pale airy blue with a soft glow; High Dynamic = shadows-to-highlights tone compression; Impressive Art = dramatic surreal local contrast; Dynamic / Silky / Rough Monochrome = punchy / soft-focus / grainy B&W; Adjust = effect strength (colour) or yellow (+) / blue (-) toning (mono)

filters.name: Clarity & Structure (Capture One methods)

filters.name: HDR Smart Structure (Aurora HDR)

filters.name: Image Radiance (Aurora HDR)

filters.name: D90 Stair-Stepping Fix (frei0r)

filters.name: Elastic Scale (frei0r)

filters.name: Color Distance (frei0r)

filters.name: Pr0file (frei0r line-profile scope)

filters.name: Robust Vector Filters (VMF / BVDF / Olympic / Peer Group)
filters.note: Astola, Haavisto & Neuvo 1990 vector median (window sample with least summed L2 distance); Trahanias & Venetsanopoulos 1993 basic vector directional filter (least summed vector angle); Olympic filter = per-channel mean with the minimum and maximum removed; Deng & Kenney peer group filtering: neighbours sorted by colour distance to the centre, peer group size by the Fisher discriminant split of the sorted distances, output = Gaussian-weighted peer-group mean; a centre whose peer group is no larger than Peer impulse size is treated as an impulse and replaced by the vector median (simplified impulse test)

filters.name: Adaptive Smoothing (Saint-Marc, Chen & Medioni 1991)
filters.note: Saint-Marc, Chen & Medioni 1991 adaptive smoothing: iterated 3x3 average weighted by w = exp(-|grad I|^2 / (2 k^2)) at each neighbour (central-difference luma gradient), so smoothing stops at edges

filters.name: Side Window Box Filter (Yin, Gong & Qiu 2019)

filters.name: Curvature Filters (Gong & Sbalzarini 2017: GC / MC / TV)

filters.name: Linear Kuwahara (Fiji)

filters.name: Crisp (ERDAS IMAGINE)

filters.name: Replace Bad Lines (ERDAS IMAGINE)

filters.name: VTK Boolean / Triangular Texture

filters.name: RevTV (EffecTV, Rutt-Etra scan lines)

filters.name: ShagadelicTV (EffecTV)

filters.name: SimuraTV (EffecTV colour mirror)

filters.name: WarpTV (EffecTV)

filters.name: DisplayWallTV (EffecTV video wall)

filters.name: Penrose Tiling (GMIC P3 rhombs / P2 kites and darts)
filters.note: G'MIC fx_penrose_tiling (Tschumperle): Robinson-triangle deflation from a sun of 10 golden triangles; per pixel the containing sub-triangle is followed through n deflations (n set so the tile edge is Tile edge px); P3 rules (thin / thick halves) as in Preshing; P2: half-kite (36 deg, legs phi) -> 2 half-kites + 1 half-dart, half-dart (108 deg) -> half-kite + half-dart (Robinson A-triangle deflation), each tile outlined without its axis; outline = the two drawn sides CA, AB; tile A (110,170,240) thick rhomb / kite, tile B (240,150,60), outline (20,20,20), random brightness variation per tile; mosaic modes fill each tile with the image colour at its centre

filters.name: Hitomezashi Stitches / Ellsworth Kelly Board (GMIC Reptorian)
filters.note: Hitomezashi (sashiko) stitching: each grid row / column has a random bit (Density = probability of 1); a row with bit a has horizontal stitches on the segments x with (x + a) even, columns likewise; two-colour mode fills the regions by parity of the stitches crossed from the corner (the pattern is always 2-colourable; G'MIC duotone A (241,255,85) / B (159,26,157)); mirrored strings = bits symmetric about the centre. Ellsworth Kelly Board (rep_ekb): square grid, each square painted with probability Density in a random colour of a 12-colour Kelly-like spectrum palette, inset by the border width (border value 25 % grey), unfilled squares (110,105,130)

filters.name: Dynamical-System Maps (Markus-Lyapunov / Henon / Chirikov / Thorn)
filters.note: Markus-Lyapunov (rep_mlfrac): logistic map x -> r x (1-x) with r taken from (a, b) by the A/B string, a horizontal and b vertical over [2,4]^2, exponent = mean log|r (1 - 2x)| after 20 warm-up steps (Parameter = x0); negative = yellow, chaotic = blue -> black. Henon area-preserving quadratic map x' = x cos a - (y - x^2) sin a, y' = x sin a + (y - x^2) cos a (a = 2.569 at Parameter .5) and Chirikov-Taylor standard map p' = p + K sin th, th' = th + p' (K = 0.9716 critical at .5): G'MIC plots many orbits as points; here each pixel is an initial condition coloured by its weighted Birkhoff-average rotation number (hue: constant along each invariant curve, so the KAM curves and island chains of the phase diagram appear as bands) and darkened where the two half-orbit averages disagree (chaotic sea), escaping orbits black (approx. visualisation of the same phase portrait). Thorn fractal / Secant Sea (rep_thorn_fractal, Bourke): a' = a / cos b + dx, b' = b / sin a + dy (inverted: a / sin b, b / cos a; arctangent: a / atan b, b / atan a) from the pixel, PI-based scaling, grey = escape iteration (|z|^2 > 10000)

filters.name: Harmonograph / Pintograph / Chryzodes / Tangential Circles (GMIC)
filters.note: G'MIC samj Harmonograph: x = A1 sin(f1 t + p1) e^(-d1 t) + A2 sin(f2 t + p2) e^(-d2 t), y likewise with A3, A4 (defaults 150/200/200/100 px, f 4/6/2/2, phases 15/270/75/60 used as radians as in the source, damping .04/.04/.05/.06, dt .04, pen (192,128,64) drawn over the image; Variant > 0 = other frequency sets); Pintograph (samj): the same undamped with near-equal frequencies 4 / 4.05 / 4.16 / 4.32 (beat patterns); Chryzodes (chryzode.org, samj examples): N points on a circle, chord from k to k*m mod N (79/3, 431/7, 353/3, 619/4, 691/12, 613/20, 358/13, 118/20, 699/6), orange on black; Tangential Circles (Claude Lion): ring of n circles tangent to the big circle and each other (r = R/(1 + 1/sin(pi/n)) at distance R/(1 + sin(pi/n))), recursed 3 levels (n = 5 + Variant), black stroke on white; lines drawn as exact distance-to-segment (1200 segments)

filters.name: Pythagoras Tree (GMIC samj / Rosetta Code)
filters.note: Pythagoras tree (G'MIC samj_Arbre_Pythagore after Rosetta Code): on the top side of each square a right triangle with angle Angle at its left end carries two child squares (sides cos a and sin a); evaluated per pixel by depth-first descent through the inverse child transforms with a self-similar bounding-disc cull (deepest square containing the pixel wins), drawn over the image, trunk at 50 % / 95 % (from top), side = Trunk width % of the image width

filters.name: Cosmic Nebula (GMIC) / Nebulous (MadJik)
filters.note: Cosmic Nebula (G'MIC fx_cosmic_nebula, Tschumperle, approx.): plasma-like fbm dust map (pow 1.5) masking two gas layers (25,128,204) / (204,51,128) and a core (255,230,178) x exp(-8 r^2), global fade exp(-2.5 r^2), background stars 350 u^(300/density) under the dust, small foreground stars 1000 u^(2000/density) blurred 1.5, giant stars with 2-orientation diffraction spikes exp(-d^2/.5) max(0, 1 - |t|/size) at Angle, highlight bloom; fbm replaces the plasma fractal, star cells replace the per-pixel random draw. Nebulous (rep_nebulous, after MadJik's Paint.NET plugin): exact formula, rotated scaled polar coordinates t, r, ti = sin t cos r k + r + angle, RGB = sin(pi + ti), sin(pi/2 + ti), sin(ti) (x/y factor 10 at Scale 1.5, disturbance 500 x Stars, distortion angle 15)

filters.name: Neon Carpet (GMIC Claude Lion)
filters.note: Claude Lion cl_neonCarpet: per channel c the integer field ((x^2 + y^2 + 128c) mod 512 mod (f2 + Sequence) mod f2), f2 = 11 + 2 x Item; normalised to 0..256, Euclidean distance to the pixels equal to 128 (the middle value), mod 32, normalised and cut at 100/255; distance searched within 12 px (approx.: the bilateral smoothing and despeckle steps are omitted)

filters.name: Tupper Self-Referential Formula (GMIC Reptorian)
filters.note: Tupper 2001: 1/2 < floor(mod(floor(y/17) 2^(-17 floor(x) - mod(floor(y), 17)), 2)) plotted for 0 <= x < 106, k <= y < k + 17: the bits of k/17 (exact, from the 543-digit k via BigInt) drawn as the 106 x 17 bitmap; k values from the G'MIC filter (Tupper, Euler identity, Pac-Man, Daves)

filters.name: Thinning (Stentiford)
filters.note: Stentiford & Mortimer 1983 (as in Parker, Algorithms for Image Processing): four 3x3 templates (N white / S black, W black / E white, N black / S white, W white / E black) applied in turn; a matching pixel is deleted when its Yokoi 8-connectivity number is 1 and it is not an end point (exactly one neighbour); 20 iterations of the 4 sub-passes

filters.name: Ed Harvey Distorts (Drop Ripple / InsideOut / Multiview Warp / Wobble) + Vibrato (MadJik)
filters.note: Paint.NET plug-in packs, approx. from the forum descriptions (no published source): Ed Harvey Drop Ripple = water-drop rings from the centre, radial displacement sin(2 pi r / Size) with exponential decay, Highlight brightens the crests; InsideOut = radial inversion, the centre is pulled from the rim and the rim from the centre (r' = R (1 - r/R)^(0.5 + Amount)), optional twist; Multiview Warp = the whole image repeated in an n x n grid of bulging lens views (n = 2..6 by Amount); Wobble = two-frequency sinusoidal x/y wobble (phase = Highlight); MadJik Vibrato = per-channel vibrato: each RGB channel resampled with a sinusoidal row delay whose phase is modulated by that channel's own value (sound-effect vibrato formula applied to the image)

filters.name: True Blur / Simplify (Ed Harvey)
filters.note: Ed Harvey pack, approx. (no published source): True Blur = Gaussian blur done in linear light (sRGB decoded, separable, sigma = Radius/2) so bright details keep their energy instead of greying, Tileable wraps the image edges (the tiling option of the plug-in); Simplify = colour-tolerance smoothing: two passes of a 96-sample disc average over only those neighbours within Tolerance of the centre colour (sigma filter), with slight level flattening, giving flat simplified regions with kept edges

filters.name: Gravity (MadJik)
filters.note: MadJik Gravity (Paint.NET, approx. from its description "objects pulled down by gravity"): pixels that differ from the background colour (Tolerance) fall down their column and pile up from the bottom in their original order; Fall < 100 % moves each pixel only part of the way (s' = s - Fall (s - rank)); the plug-in uses transparency, here the background is keyed by colour (corner average, white or black)

filters.name: Seismograph (Ed Harvey) / Cobweb (Red ochre)
filters.note: approx. from the forum descriptions: Ed Harvey Seismograph = rows of seismograph traces every Spacing px whose jittery oscillation amplitude follows the darkness of the image under the line (curves drawn by distance to the trace); Red ochre Cobweb = "works out the direction of the tone gradient then randomly draws tangents and radiuses": random seed points each emit a segment along the luminance gradient (radius) and one across it (tangent), drawn as light threads over the darkened image

filters.name: Psychocolour (Red ochre) / Change Extreme Colors (MadJik)
filters.note: approx. from the forum descriptions: Red ochre Psychocolour = single-slider psychedelic recolouring, each channel replaced by a sinusoid of a rotated channel and the luminance (cycle count grows with Amount); MadJik Change Extreme Colors = only the extreme channel values (darkest, brightest or both, within Range of 0 / 1 per channel, soft edge) are changed, pushed toward inverted / shifted colours by Amount

filters.name: Object Edge (Red ochre)
filters.note: Red ochre Object Edge (approx.: the plug-in works on the layer alpha): the object = pixels farther than Tolerance from the background colour; the distance to the nearest background pixel (16 directions x 12 steps up to Width) colours the edge band (Outline: black band), shades it like a bevel lit from the upper left, or grades from a dark edge colour to a light middle colour

filters.name: HSV Hold / HSV Key (FFmpeg hsvhold / hsvkey)
filters.note: FFmpeg vf_hsvkey.c: pixel hue = atan2(U, V) + pi, sat = |UV| / (half sqrt 2), key hue = sign(h) pi mod(526 - |h|, 360) / 180 (a non-positive Hue disables the hue test), diff = sqrt(s^2 v^2 + sk^2 vk^2 - 2 s v sk vk cos(hk - h) + (v - vk)^2), keyed when diff < similarity (blend 0); hsvhold keeps colour only for matching pixels (chroma of the rest set to 0), hsvkey makes matching pixels transparent (shown over a checkerboard or as the alpha matte); val fixed at -0.5 (brightness ignored), BT.601 YUV

filters.name: Luma Key (FFmpeg lumakey)
filters.note: FFmpeg vf_lumakey.c: black = threshold - tolerance, white = threshold + tolerance; luma inside [black, white] -> alpha 0, within softness outside -> linear ramp, else opaque (BT.601 luma); shown over a checkerboard or as the matte

filters.name: Chroma Shift (FFmpeg chromashift)
filters.note: FFmpeg vf_chromashift.c (edge = smear): out Cb(x, y) = in Cb(clip(x - cbh), clip(y - cbv)), Cr likewise with crh / crv, luma untouched (positive = right / down); BT.601 YCbCr

filters.name: Data Scope / Pixel Scope (FFmpeg datascope / pixscope)
filters.note: FFmpeg vf_datascope.c datascope: a grid of cells, one per source pixel starting at X/Y (top-left), each showing the R, G, B values as hex (or decimal) digits (color2: cell filled with the pixel colour, contrasting text; mono: white on black); pixscope: a 7 x 7 window around X/Y shown magnified in a box on the opposite side (centre pixel outlined) with average / min / max per channel below and the sampled window outlined on the image; 3x5 digit font
