filters.name: RGB Spectral Indices III (soil & vegetation)
filters.note: published RGB formulas (uavRst rgb_indices / rgbIndices tables; Escadafal soil colour indices): GLAI = 25 (G-R)/(G+R-B) + 1.25; SAT = (max-min)/max; HUE = atan(2(R-G-B) / (30.5 (G-B))); BI = sqrt((R^2+G^2+B^2)/3); HI = (2R-G-B)/(G-B) (shown as atan); CI = (R-B)/R; TCVI = 1.4 (2R-2B)/(2R-G-2B+255*0.4) (0..255 scale); GRRI = G/R, RBRI = R/B (shown as log); NRBDI = (R-B)/(R+G+B). Display = index minus its value for neutral grey of the same brightness (SAT, BI, HUE, HI shown raw), times Gain

filters.name: Ultrasound Log Compression / Optical Density
filters.note: B-mode ultrasound log compression: pixel value read as envelope amplitude A (max 1), shown as 20 log10(A) dB over the chosen dynamic range (0 dB white, -DR black). Optical density (Beer-Lambert / Ruifrok colour deconvolution convention): OD = -log10(I / I0) per RGB channel, displayed OD / OD-at-white

filters.name: FIB-SEM Curtaining / Stripe Removal
filters.note: approx. spatial analogue of wavelet-FFT destriping (Muench et al. 2009) used for FIB-SEM curtaining: stripe estimate = image smoothed along the stripe direction (Gaussian, Stripe length) minus that result smoothed across it (Stripe width), subtracted from the image; long straight structures parallel to the stripes are attenuated too
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,u_p0<.5?vec2(0.,1.):vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p1));
vec2 d=u_p0<.5?vec2(1.,0.):vec2(0.,1.);vec3 a=T(uv).rgb,b=blur1d(u_tex,uv,d,R(u_p2)).rgb;return vec4(O(uv).rgb-(a-b)*u_p3,1.);

filters.name: CT Ring Artifact Removal
filters.note: approx. polar-domain ring removal (after Sijbers & Postnov 2004): ring profile = mean over 48 angles on the circle through the pixel around the rotation centre, sampled at 13 radii (step Ring width / 2); ring artifact = profile minus its radial median (keeps concentric object edges), subtracted

filters.name: Gibbs Ringing Removal (Kellner local sub-pixel shifts)
filters.note: Kellner, Dhital, Kiselev & Reisert 2016 (MRtrix mrdegibbs): per pixel, 17 sub-pixel shifts (+-0.5 px), choose the shift with the least total variation over offsets 1..3 on the left or right side, then interpolate back linearly to the original grid; approx.: shifts by Lanczos-6 windowed sinc instead of FFT phase ramps, and the k-space x/y weighting is replaced by an x pass followed by a y pass

filters.name: Specular Reflection Removal (endoscopy)
filters.note: after Arnold, Ghosh, Ameling & Lacey 2010 (approx.): highlights = bright, low-saturation pixels by an absolute threshold plus a relative one against the local mean brightness, dilated 3x3; filled by normalised Gaussian convolution of the non-specular pixels and blended with a softened mask
passes:
float a=1.;for(int j=-1;j<=1;j++)for(int i=-1;i<=1;i++){vec2 q=uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*R(1.5)*u_px;vec3 s=O(q).rgb;float mx=max(s.r,max(s.g,s.b)),mn=min(s.r,min(s.g,s.b));float st_=mx>0.?(mx-mn)/mx:0.;float l=luma(s);float lb=0.;for(int b=-2;b<=2;b++)for(int e=-2;e<=2;e++)lb+=luma(O(q+vec2(float(e),float(b))*R(4.)*u_px).rgb);lb/=25.;
  if(st_<u_p1&&(l>u_p0||(l>u_p0*.7&&l>lb*(1.+2.*(1.-u_p0)))))a=0.;}return vec4(O(uv).rgb*a,a);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Fundus Luminosity & Contrast Normalisation
filters.note: after Foracchia, Grisan & Ruggeri 2005 (approx.): local mean and std in a window; background pixels = within t std of their local mean (Mahalanobis distance); luminosity drift L and contrast drift C = mean and std of the background pixels around each pixel; output (I - L)/C. Windows sampled on an 11x11 grid
passes: float w=R(u_p0)/5.;int ch=int(u_p2+.5);float s1=0.,s2=0.;for(int j=-5;j<=5;j++)for(int i=-5;i<=5;i++){vec3 s=O(uv+vec2(float(i),float(j))*w*u_px).rgb;float v=ch==1?luma(s):s.g;s1+=v;s2+=v*v;}s1/=121.;return vec4(s1,sqrt(max(s2/121.-s1*s1,1e-6)),0.,1.);

filters.name: Inverse Tone Mapping (Akyuz / Masia / Huo / Rempel / Kovaleski-Oliveira)
filters.note: expansion operators as in Banterle HDR Toolbox (input linearised with gamma 2.2, luminance scaled, colour ratios kept): Akyuz: L = ((L-Lmin)/(Lmax-Lmin))^gamma (parameter -> gamma 0.35..2.8, 0.5 = 1); Masia: gamma = 10.44 k - 6.282, k = image key (log-average) (clamped >= 0.2); Huo: L/Lmax * (Ls^n + sigma^n)^(1/n), Ls = bilateral local adaptation (single pass approx. of the two-pass filter), sigma = log-average, n = 0.86 at 0.5; Rempel: brightness enhancement = Gaussian blur (sigma = width/40) of the >0.9 mask scaled to 1..alpha (parameter -> alpha 1..16, 0.5 = 4; edge-stopping flood fill omitted, approx.); Kovaleski-Oliveira: cross-bilateral of that mask guided by luminance, e = (3b+1)/4. Output normalised to peak 1, viewed through extended Reinhard (white = exposure), exposure clip, or log2 expansion ratio
passes: float m=step(.9,max(c.r,max(c.g,c.b)));return vec4(m,m,m,1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_res.x/u_k*.05));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_res.x/u_k*.05));

filters.name: LCIS Tone Mapping (Tumblin-Turk low-curvature image simplifier)
filters.note: Tumblin & Turk 1999 LCIS on log luminance, discretised as in the authors' example code: link curvature magnitude^2 from second differences, conductance 1/(1+|curv|^2/K^2), flux = conductance x change of curvature across the link (third differences), conservative update, timestep 0.03; approx.: 34 iterations on a coarse-to-fine lattice (spacing 4, 2, 1 px) instead of hundreds, leak-fix gains omitted. Tone mapping: log L = compression x (base - max) + detail x (log L - base), colour ratios ^ saturation

filters.name: Spacek Optimal Edge Detector (1986)
filters.note: Spacek 1986: Canny-type optimal antisymmetric filter, integrated (as Spacek proposed) into a symmetric smoothing operator applied separably, edges = maxima of a central difference; approx.: Spacek's cubic-spline first approximation of the filter, g(x) = x^3+2x^2+x on [-w,0], whose integral h(u) = 1-6u^2+8u^3-3u^4 (u = |x|/w) is the smoothing kernel (performance 0.1823 vs 0.1824 for the full filter, Petrou & Kittler 1988)
passes: float w=max(R(u_p0),1.);float st=max(1.,w/24.);vec4 a=vec4(0.);float ws=0.;for(int i=-24;i<=24+int(u_p0*0.);i++){float x=float(i)*st;float u=abs(x)/w;if(u>=1.)continue;float h=1.-6.*u*u+8.*u*u*u-3.*u*u*u*u;a+=T(uv+vec2(1.,0.)*x*u_px)*h;ws+=h;}return a/ws;

float w=max(R(u_p0),1.);float st=max(1.,w/24.);vec4 a=vec4(0.);float ws=0.;for(int i=-24;i<=24+int(u_p0*0.);i++){float x=float(i)*st;float u=abs(x)/w;if(u>=1.)continue;float h=1.-6.*u*u+8.*u*u*u-3.*u*u*u*u;a+=T(uv+vec2(0.,1.)*x*u_px)*h;ws+=h;}return a/ws;

filters.name: Pb Probability of Boundary (brightness + colour gradients)
filters.note: after Martin, Fowlkes & Malik 2004 (approx.): oriented half-disc histogram gradients, chi^2 distance between the two halves (8 soft bins) of CIELAB L* (brightness gradient) and a*, b* (colour gradient), 4 orientations, max over orientations, non-maximum suppression across the boundary; texture gradient (textons) and the trained logistic weights are omitted
passes:
vec4 a=T(uv);float th=a.g*3.14159;vec2 n=vec2(-sin(th),cos(th))*u_px*max(u_k,1.);float v=a.r,p1=T(uv+n).r,p2=T(uv-n).r;int om=int(u_p2+.5);
  float ov=om==1?v:((v>=p1&&v>=p2)?v:0.);ov=1.-exp(-ov*u_p3);if(om==2)return vec4(mix(O(uv).rgb*.6,vec3(1.,.2,.1),ov),1.);return vec4(vec3(ov),1.);

filters.name: Tektronix Scopes (Lightning / Diamond / Arrowhead / Spearhead / Stop)
filters.note: Tektronix gamut displays from a 36x36 sample grid of the image (read as R'G'B' 0-100%): Lightning = luma up vs Pb in the upper half, inverted luma vs Pr in the lower half (BT.709), with 75% bar targets; Diamond (US 5307087) = B-G across vs B+G up (upper diamond) and R-G vs -(R+G) (lower), legal-gamut diamonds as graticule; Arrowhead = NTSC luma IRE (7.5 setup, BT.601 Y) up vs composite chroma amplitude 92.5 x |U,V| across, with 110 / 120 IRE luma+chroma limit lines and a -20 IRE lower line (approx. limits); Spearhead (US 7071965) = lightness (max+min)/2 up vs max-min across in the black-white-saturation triangle with iso-saturation / iso-value lines; Stop display = waveform of log2(scene luminance / 0.18) after inverting the chosen transfer curve (sRGB, BT.709, gamma 2.4, S-Log3, LogC3 EI 800), -10..+9 stops, 0 stop line bright

filters.name: Monitor Checks (Blue Only / Superwhite / Illegal Levels)
filters.note: monitor line-up checks. Blue only: only the blue gun shown (as grey), used with SMPTE / RP 219 bars to set chroma and hue until the blue-containing bars match the reverse-blue row below. The level checks read the pixel values as 8-bit video-range codes (16 = 0 %, 235 = 100 %): superwhite / sub-black flags luma above the upper or below the lower limit (striped red / blue); RGB gamut flags any R'G'B' component outside the EBU R 103 tolerance band (limits widened by 5 %, i.e. -5 % / 105 % at the defaults)

filters.name: Retinex: Random Sprays / Light Sprays / Termites / QBRIX / Land Paths
filters.note: RSR (Provenzi et al. 2007): per channel L = mean over N sprays of I / max(spray), spray points at radius R*rand, angle 2pi*rand (identity radial density, so denser near the pixel), R = image diagonal by default; N x n capped at 1200 samples. LRSR (Banic & Loncaric 2013): RSR result R smoothed against the input with an averaging kernel, out = I * (R*k)/(I*k) (kernel 5-45 px, default 25), meant for 1 small spray (no downsampling step here). Termite Retinex (Simone et al. 2014), approx.: per pixel N agents walk Ns steps, each step choosing among 4 forward neighbours with probability ~ bilateral closeness 1/(1+20|dL|) (backtracking tabu, agents start on spread headings; no shared poison map), out = mean I / max(path). QBRIX (Gianini et al. 2014) local version: white reference = quantile (0.8-1, default 0.9) of an 80-sample spray population, out = I / quantile. Land & McCann 1971: N random-walk paths ending at the pixel, log ratios below the threshold set to 0, product reset at 0, out = exp(mean product)

filters.name: Retinex: Frankle-McCann / McCann99
filters.note: Ciurea, Funt & McCann "Retinex in Matlab" (2000) per channel on the log image log(255 I + 1)/log 256: Frankle-McCann = shifts from 2^(floor(log2 min side)-1) halving with alternating sign, each iteration a horizontal then a vertical ratio-product (OP(x-s) + r(x) - r(x-s)), reset at the image maximum, average with the old product (both steps exact in one pass); McCann99 = pyramid of block means (coarsest block 2^(floor(log2 min side)-2)), per level 8 neighbour comparisons N, NE ... NW with reset and averaging, product replicated to the next level; neighbours read from the previous pass (approx. of the sequential sweep); image maximum from a 16x16 sample grid; max 10 levels, 1-3 iterations
passes: vec3 r=c.rgb;return vec4(u_p2>.5?r:clamp((pow(vec3(256.),r)-1.)/255.,0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Retinex PDE (Poisson, Morel-Petro-Sbert)
filters.note: PDE Retinex (Morel, Petro & Sbert 2010; Limare et al. IPOL 2011): per channel solve -Lap u = F with F(x) = sum over the 4 neighbours of f(I(x)-I(n)), f(d) = 0 if |d| < t else d (t = 4 of 255 by default), Neumann boundary, then give u the mean and variance of the input (16x16 sample grid). Solved here as u = I + e with -Lap e = -(sum of the small differences) by cascaded damped (w = 2/3) strided Jacobi sweeps (strides 64..1, 24 passes) instead of the reference DFT solve - approx.

filters.name: Morphological Amoebas (Lerallut)
filters.note: Lerallut, Decenciere & Meyer 2005 morphological amoebas: adaptive structuring element = pixels whose amoeba distance (path length, each step 1 + lambda x |pilot difference| with the difference in units of 16/255) from the centre is <= r; pilot = lightly smoothed luminance of the input (used for both passes of opening / closing). Approx.: star-shaped amoeba, the cost accumulated along 12 straight rays instead of the geodesic minimum over all paths; median = the pixel of median luma

filters.name: Fuzzy Morphology (Bloch-Maitre)
filters.note: Bloch & Maitre 1995 (Pattern Recognition 28:9) t-norm morphology, each channel taken as a membership function mu: dilation D(x) = sup_y t[mu(y), nu(y-x)], erosion E(x) = inf_y T[mu(y), c(nu(y-x))] with c = 1 - v; pairs min/max (their definition 2), product / probabilistic sum (def. 3), Lukasiewicz max(0,a+b-1) / min(1,a+b) (def. 4); fuzzy structuring element nu = cone, Gaussian or crisp disc of the radius (sampled on a <= 21x21 grid)

filters.name: Soft Morphological Filters (Koskinen)
filters.note: Koskinen, Astola & Neuvo 1991 soft grey-scale morphology with a flat structuring system [B, A, k]: B = disc of the radius, hard centre A = centre pixel or 3x3; soft erosion = k-th smallest and soft dilation = k-th largest of the multiset where core values are repeated k times and soft-boundary values once (k = 1 gives plain erosion / dilation); soft opening / closing chain the two per channel

filters.name: Sine Scroller / DYCP (demoscene)
filters.note: classic 8-bit / Amiga demo text effects over the dimmed image: sine scroller = a scrolling bitmap-font banner whose every pixel column is displaced vertically by a sine of its screen x; DYCP (different Y character position, C64) = each whole character moved up / down by the sine of its own screen position (character shape kept); 5x7 font, rainbow raster colours, drop shadow; single frame at the Scroll position

filters.name: Broadcast Test Signals (Bars / PLUGE / Multiburst / Staircase / Checkfield / Bowtie)
filters.note: generators (optionally over the image): SMPTE EG 1 bars (75% bars, reverse-blue row, -I / 100% white / +Q, PLUGE -4 / 0 / +4 IRE; geometry as FFmpeg smptebars); RP 219 / ARIB STD-B28 (40% grey side panels, 75% bars, 100% cyan / blue with 75% white row, 100% yellow / red with Y ramp, 15% grey, white and PLUGE -2 / 0 / +2 / 0 / +4%; row-4 widths approx.); EBU 100/0/75/0; BT.814 PLUGE (-2 / 0 / +2% stripes and 100 / 63 / 35 / 15% patches, layout approx.); NTSC multiburst (white flag, packets 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 3.58, 4.2 MHz, 100 IRE p-p on 50 IRE, over a 52.6 us line - the highest packets alias at small sizes as on a real line sampled this coarsely); 5 / 10-step staircases; SDI checkfield per SMPTE RP 198 (top: Y 198h, Cb Cr 300h purple; bottom: Y 110h, Cb Cr 200h grey; BT.709 decode); Tektronix bowtie (Y 500 kHz 350 mV p-p, Pb / Pr 502 kHz +-175 mV, decoded to RGB; timing markers omitted). Full range draws black at 0 (sub-black clips); video range writes 8-bit studio codes (black 16) so PLUGE stays visible

filters.name: Test Cards & Resolution Targets (PM5544 / FuBK / Card F / Indian Head / Siemens / USAF / ISO 12233)
filters.note: generators, approx. layouts: PM5544 (19 x 14 white grid on grey, castellated border, circle with 75% square wave, 75% Y C G M R B bars, white / black step, centre cross, 0.8-4.8 MHz gratings, 6-step grey scale, yellow / red step); FuBK (grid on 25% grey, circle with 75% EBU bars, black band with 2T cross and reflection block, 1 / 2 / 3 / 4.43 MHz gratings, 5 grey steps); Test Card F layout (95%-saturation bars, 1.5-5.25 MHz gratings, grey scale, castellations, overscan triangles) with the input image as the centre picture; Indian-head layout (converging resolution wedges, grey bands, circles, corner stars) with the input as the portrait; Siemens star (spokes = black / white cycles); USAF 1951 (3-bar elements 5:1, width 2^-(group + (element-1)/6), groups 0-3 in columns rather than the spiral layout); ISO 12233-style chart (zone plate, hyperbolic wedges, 5-degree slanted squares)

params.label: Card
opts: BBC Test Card F (layout, image as centre picture)

filters.name: Safe Areas & Camera Frame Lines
filters.note: monitoring overlays: SMPTE ST 2046-1 safe areas for 16:9 HD (action safe 93%, title safe 90% of width and height, centred) or the legacy SMPTE RP 13 / RP 8 values (action 90%, title 80%); camera frame lines = the largest centred frame of the chosen aspect inside the image with inner corner brackets; outside area darkened; centre cross

filters.name: Demosaic III (Kimmel / ACPI / GBTF / RI / MLRI / Cok / Laroche-Prescott / Freeman)
filters.note: RGGB mosaic of the input, then: Kimmel 1999 (edge weights e = (1 + D(p)^2 + D(n)^2)^-1/2 from the raw mosaic, weighted green, ratio R/B, 3 green / colour-ratio correction iterations over 8 neighbours; central differences everywhere, ratios offset by 0.02, no step-2 inverse diffusion); ACPI / Hamilton-Adams (US 5,629,734: Laplacian-corrected green with gradient + Laplacian classifiers, chroma with /2 green Laplacian and diagonal classifiers); GBTF (Pekkucuksen & Altunbasak 2010: Hamilton-Adams directional colour differences, N / S / E / W weights 1/(sum of 5x9 gradient window)^2, 1-D filter [.26 .24 .21 .17 .12], R/B with the 7x7 / 32 kernel then axial colour differences); RI and MLRI (Kiku et al. 2013 / 2014: directional guided-filter tentative G / R / B with linear-interpolation guides, 11-tap (RI) or 9-tap Laplacian-energy (MLRI) windows, residuals interpolated linearly, GBTF weighting; R/B guided by G with 5x5 windows (paper 11x11) and bilinear residuals, eps 1e-4 - approx.); Cok 1987 smooth hue (bilinear G, R/G and B/G ratios interpolated); Laroche-Prescott (US 5,373,322: green direction from chroma samples 2 px away, R/B by bilinear colour difference); Freeman 1988 (bilinear, then R = G + median3x3(R-G), B = G + median3x3(B-G) at unmeasured sites, Bayer form). Output demosaiced, error, mosaic or signed error
passes:
#define RSM(q) ((u_res-1.)-abs((u_res-1.)-abs(q)))
#define RSW(q) (mod((q).x,2.)<.5?(mod(u_res.y-1.-(q).y,2.)<.5?vec3(1.,0.,0.):vec3(0.,1.,0.)):(mod(u_res.y-1.-(q).y,2.)<.5?vec3(0.,1.,0.):vec3(0.,0.,1.)))
#define RAW(q) dot(O((RSM(q)+.5)/u_res).rgb,RSW(q))
#define TP(q) T((RSM(q)+.5)/u_res)
#define RSX vec2(1.,0.)
#define RSY vec2(0.,1.)
vec2 p=floor(uv*u_res);vec3 r=clamp(c.rgb,0.,1.);vec3 o=O(uv).rgb;int md=int(u_p1+.5);
 if(md==1)return vec4(clamp(abs(r-o)*u_p2,0.,1.),1.);if(md==2)return vec4(RSW(p)*RAW(p),1.);if(md==3)return vec4(clamp(.5+(r-o)*u_p2,0.,1.),1.);return vec4(r,1.);

filters.name: Wavelet Shrinkage (NeighShrink / Bivariate / SURE-LET, a trous)
filters.note: approx. (the papers use decimated orthogonal / Haar UWT subbands): 4-level undecimated B3 a trous transform of luma, noise sigma from the MAD of level 1 (49 samples, /0.6745/0.889) unless set, per-level sigma_j = sigma x (.889 .200 .086 .041 .020) x Strength. NeighShrink (Chen, Bui & Qian 2004): beta = (1 - lambda^2/S^2)+ with S^2 = sum of squares in the 3x3 coefficient neighbourhood, lambda = sqrt(2 sigma_j^2 ln N). Bivariate (Sendur & Selesnick 2002, local variance): w = y (sqrt(y^2+p^2) - sqrt3 sigma_n^2/sigma)+ / sqrt(y^2+p^2), p = parent (next level, same position), sigma = sqrt((mean y^2 over 7x7 - sigma_n^2)+). SURE-LET (Luisier & Blu 2007): theta(y) = a1 y + a2 y exp(-y^2/(12 sigma^2)), a = M^-1 c from SURE sums over a 16x16 coefficient sample, solved per level (in-band, not the paper's joint image-domain solve). Chroma: B3 low-pass (not wavelet-shrunk)

filters.name: Progressive Switching Median (Wang-Zhang)
filters.note: Wang & Zhang 1999 (IEEE TCAS-II 46(1)), per RGB channel: noise ratio R from Sun-Neuvo switch-I counts (|med3x3 - x| >= 40) on a 12x12 sample, W_D = 3 if R <= 25% else 5, T_D = 65 - 50 R; N_D = 3 progressive detection iterations (newly flagged pixels replaced by the W_D median); then 6 filtering iterations from the noisy image with W_F = 3: flagged pixels take the median (left/right median mean for even M) of the good pixels only and become good

filters.name: Center-Weighted / Rank-Conditioned / Decision-Based Median
filters.note: per RGB channel. CWM (Ko & Lee 1991): weighted median with the centre sample repeated 2K+1 times. Rank-conditioned median: the centre is replaced by the window median only when fewer than k window samples are below it or fewer than k above it (centre rank among the k lowest / highest, ties counted in its favour) (order-1 RCRS selection conditioned on the centre rank, Hardie & Barner 1994 / Alparone et al.; trained selection tables are not reproduced). Decision-based (Srinivasan & Ebenezer 2007): only 0 / 255 pixels (within the tolerance) are processed; they take the 3x3 median unless it is itself 0 / 255, then the left neighbour (approx.: parallel, the nearest unflagged pixel to the left instead of the raster-processed value)

filters.name: Directional Distance Filter (Karakos-Trahanias)
filters.note: Karakos & Trahanias 1997 DDF: output = the window colour vector minimising (sum of angles to the others)^(1-p) x (sum of Euclidean distances)^p; p = 0 gives the BVDF, p = 1 the vector median; p = 0.5 as in Celebi et al. 2007

filters.name: DPAD Detail-Preserving Anisotropic Diffusion (Aja-Fernandez)
filters.note: Aja-Fernandez & Alberola-Lopez 2006 (IEEE TIP 15(9)) per RGB channel: SRAD-style explicit diffusion I += dt div(c grad I) with the Kuan-based coefficient c = (1 + 1/Ci^2) / (1 + 1/Cu^2) (clipped to [0,1]), Ci^2 = local variance / mean^2 over a 5x5 (or 3x3) window (unbiased variance); Cu^2 per iteration = median of Ci^2 over a 6x6 sample of windows (or set). Up to 16 iterations (the paper runs hundreds)

params.label: Noise coeff. of variation Cu (0 = auto)

filters.name: No-Neighbours Deblurring
filters.note: single-plane no-neighbours deblurring (optical-sectioning microscopy, after Agard 1984): f = c2 [g - 2 c1 (g * h)], the out-of-focus planes above and below approximated by the plane itself blurred with a Gaussian PSF h; default c2 keeps the mean
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p0));
vec3 bl=blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p0)).rgb;vec3 gi=O(uv).rgb;float c2=u_p2>0.?u_p2:1./(1.-2.*u_p1);return vec4(clamp(c2*(gi-2.*u_p1*bl),0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Local Space Average Colour (Ebner)
filters.note: Ebner 2003/2007: each pixel divided by f x its local space average colour (out = c / (2 a), linear light). The iterative 4-neighbour averaging a = p c + (1 - p) avg(a) converges to the screened-Poisson Green function K0(r/L), L^2 = (1-p)/(4p); here it is applied directly by importance sampling (32 radius quantiles of 1 - x K1(x) x 12 angles, approx.: edge-clamped borders instead of the grid boundary)

filters.name: Resampling Kernels III (Lagrange / Schaum / Akima / O-MOMS / Magic Kernel Sharp)
filters.note: input = image enlarged N x (block pixels), resampled separably from the block grid. Lagrange 4-point = Schaum cubic and Schaum quadratic (Schaum 1993) kernels as in IPOL "Linear methods for image interpolation" (Getreuer 2011); Lagrange 6-point basis polynomials; Hamming window 0.54 + 0.46 cos(pi x/3) x sinc; Magic Kernel Sharp (Costella): quadratic-B-spline Magic Kernel after the input-space sharpening {-1/4, 3/2, -1/4} (2013) or {-1, 6, -35, 204, -35, 6, -1}/144 (2021); O-MOMS cubic (Blu, Thevenaz & Unser 2001) after the causal/anticausal prefilter with pole (sqrt(105) - 13)/8, applied as its truncated symmetric impulse response (|k| <= 5); Akima 1970 slopes (weights |m_i+1 - m_i|) with cubic Hermite segments, x then y

filters.name: Iterative Back-Projection SR (Irani-Peleg, from N x grid)
filters.note: Irani & Peleg 1991 with a single low-resolution frame: start from a Keys (Catmull-Rom) upscale of the N x N blocks, then x <- x + lambda BP(y - D x) per iteration, D = box average over each block (pixel-integration PSF, up to 6 x 6 sub-samples), BP = bilinear (or nearest) spreading of the per-block error

filters.name: LBP Variants III (CS-LBP / Median Binary / LDN / Elongated)
filters.note: codes shown as grey = code / max code. CS-LBP: sum over 4 centre-symmetric pairs of s(n_i - n_i+4 > T) 2^i on a radius-R circle (bilinear); MBP: 3x3 block (spacing R) incl. centre thresholded at its median, 9 bits; LDN: Kirsch compass responses on the 3x3 ring, code = 8 x argmax + argmin (6 bits); ELBP: 8 neighbours on an ellipse with axes A and B = A/2 at the chosen orientation, s(n_p - g_c >= 0)

filters.name: Extended LBP & Local Tetra Patterns (NI / RD / AD / CI-LBP, LTrP)
filters.note: Liu et al. 2012 extended LBP (8 samples): NI-LBP s(x_r,p - mean of the ring), RD-LBP s(x_r,p - x_r-delta,p), AD-LBP s(x_r,p - x_r,p+delta), CI-LBP s(x_c - image mean); Murala, Maheshwari & Balasubramanian 2012 LTrP: direction of each pixel from the signs of its horizontal / vertical first differences (1..4), tetra code 0 where a neighbour (radius R ring) shares the centre direction else its direction, split into 3 binary patterns (one per other direction, shown as RGB), plus the magnitude pattern s(M_p - M_c); direction map = hue by direction, value by magnitude

params.label: Pattern
opts: LTrP tetra patterns (3 codes as RGB)

filters.name: Surround-Inhibition Contours (Grigorescu-Petkov)
filters.note: Grigorescu, Petkov & Westenberg 2003 isotropic surround inhibition: Gabor energy (8 orientations, lambda = sigma/0.56, aspect 0.5, DC-free even part) maximised over orientation, inhibition term = Gabor energy weighted by the normalised positive part of DoG(4 sigma) - G(sigma) (sampled 17x17), b = (E - alpha t)+, then non-maximum suppression across the winning orientation (no hysteresis)
passes:
vec4 t0=T(uv);int om=int(u_p3+.5);if(om==2)return vec4(vec3(clamp(t0.b*u_p2,0.,1.)),1.);if(om==1)return vec4(vec3(clamp(t0.r*u_p2,0.,1.)),1.);

filters.name: LBP Defocus Sharpness Map (Yi-Eramian)
filters.note: Yi & Eramian 2016 sharpness metric: rotation-invariant uniform LBP (P = 8, R = 1, bilinear diagonals, bit = n_p - n_c > T_LBP, T = 0.016 on [0,1]), fraction of pixels with riu2 code 6, 7, 8 or 9 (non-uniform) in an s x s window (box filter, s = 21); min-max normalised over an 8x8 sample of the map (approx. of the global normalisation in the paper); single scale, no matting

filters.name: Focus Measures: Gradient / Laplacian / Misc (Pertuz 2013)
filters.note: Pertuz, Puig & Garcia 2013 operators (code names of fmeasure.m) evaluated in a WxW neighbourhood (7x7 samples at stride W/7, mean instead of sum): GDER = (I*Gx)^2+(I*Gy)^2 with sigma = W/5, kernels normalised by sum|G'|; GRAT = max(|Ix|,|Iy|) (T = 0); GRAS = Ix^2; SFRQ = sqrt(sum Ix^2 + sum Iy^2); TENV = variance of the Sobel magnitude; CURV = |c0|+|c1|+|c2|+|c3| of the quadratic-surface fit (M1/6, M2/5 masks, c2 = 3/2 M2*I - M2t*I, c3 = 3/2 M2t*I - M2*I); CONT = sum over 3x3 of |I(x,y)-I(i,j)|; LAPE = squared fspecial Laplacian (alpha .2); LAPD = |Lx|+|Ly|+|Ld1|+|Ld2| (diagonals /sqrt2); HELM = mean ratio max(m/I, I/m) - 1 with m the WxW box mean. Display 1-exp(-gain x value)

filters.name: Focus Measures: Statistics / DCT / Moments (Pertuz 2013)
filters.note: Pertuz 2013 statistics / DCT / moment operators over a WxW neighbourhood (7x7 samples at stride W/7): ACMO = sum_k |k-mu| P_k (= mean absolute deviation); GLVN = variance / mean; HISE = -sum P_k log2 P_k of the 256-level histogram of the window samples; HISR = max - min; DCTE = AC/DC energy (sum F^2 - F00^2)/F00^2 and DCTR = (F01^2+F10^2+F20^2+F11^2+F02^2)/F00^2 of the 8x8 orthonormal DCT of the sliding block at every pixel, averaged over the window; CHEB = ||high||/||low|| moment energy of the window normalised by sqrt(sum I^2) with orthonormal Tchebichef polynomials on 7 points, low = total order <= p = 2 (approx. of the order split); EIGV = sum of the k = 5 largest eigenvalues of S = J J^T/(MN-1), J = normalised mean-removed 7x7 window (cyclic Jacobi). Display 1-exp(-gain x value)

filters.name: Focus Measures: Wavelet WAVS / WAVV / WAVR (Pertuz 2013)
filters.note: Pertuz 2013 wavelet operators on the over-complete (undecimated) Daubechies-6 transform as in the paper: WAVS = sum |W_LH1|+|W_HL1|+|W_HH1|, WAVV = sum of the three level-1 sub-band variances, WAVR = sum(W_LH1^2+W_HL1^2+W_HH1^2) / sum W_LL3^2 (level-3 approximation via a trous filters at dilations 1, 2, 4), all over a WxW neighbourhood (7x7 samples at stride W/7). Display 1-exp(-gain x value)

filters.name: Fusion-Based Low-Light Enhancement (Fu 2016)
filters.note: Fu, Zeng, Huang, Liao, Ding & Paisley 2016 (Signal Processing 129): illumination L = max(R,G,B), morphological closing with a 7x7 disk, refined by a guided filter guided by the HSV V channel; reflectance = S/I; inputs I1 = I, I2 = (2/pi) arctan(lambda I) with lambda = 10 + (1 - mean I)/mean I, I3 = CLAHE(I); weights W_B = exp(-(I_k - .5)^2 / (2 x .25^2)) and chromatic W_C = I_k (1 + cos(alpha H + phi) S) with alpha 2, phi 250 deg; output = R x sum normalised W_k I_k. Approx.: CLAHE replaced by a clipped local rank equalisation (strength = mix), guided-filter eps .001, and single-scale (naive) fusion instead of the 6-level Laplacian / Gaussian pyramids

filters.name: Camera Response Low-Light Enhancement (Ying 2017 / LECARM)
filters.note: Ying, Li, Ren, Wang & Wang 2017 (ICCVW, "A new low-light image enhancement algorithm using camera response model"; journal version LECARM, Ren et al.) after the authors' code: T = max(R,G,B) refined by the RTV-weighted least squares (weights 1/(|sum5 dT| |dT| + .001), lambda) on the half-resolution grid, exposure ratio K = min(1/T, 7), each pixel moved to its exposure by the camera brightness-transform g(P,K): Beta-Gamma e^(b(1-K^a)) P^(K^a) (a -.3293, b 1.1258), Preferred (a 4.3536, c .1447), Affine (alpha -.1797, gamma .3988), Beta (c .48); no fusion. Approx.: 12 weighted Jacobi sweeps at strides 32..1 instead of the PCG solve
passes: return vec4(max(c.r,max(c.g,c.b)),0.,0.,1.);

filters.name: Alpha Rooting (block DCT, Aghagolzadeh-Ersoy 1992)
filters.note: Alpha rooting X' = X |X|^(alpha-1), normalised so the DC term is unchanged, in an 8x8 orthonormal DCT (one of the block transforms of Aghagolzadeh & Ersoy 1992, Opt. Eng. 31(3)); evaluated per pixel on the sliding block (maximal overlap-save, no block edges), keeping the reconstructed sample at the block position of the pixel. alpha < 1 boosts the high-frequency (low-magnitude) coefficients relative to DC. The classic whole-image DFT version needs an FFT and is not built

filters.name: Logarithmic Image Processing LIP (Jourlin-Pinoli)
filters.note: Jourlin & Pinoli LIP model on grey tones f = M - I (M = 1): f + g = f+g-fg/M, f - g = (f-g)/(1-g/M), lambda x f = M - M(1-f/M)^lambda. Scalar multiplication (on intensities = I^lambda); dynamic expansion with the lambda that maximises lambda x fmax - lambda x fmin, lambda0 = ln(ln a / ln b) / ln(b/a) with a = 1-fmax/M, b = 1-fmin/M (min / max from a 16x16 sample grid); LIP unsharp f (+) k (x) (f (-) Gaussian mean of f) built from the same LIP operations
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p2));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p2));

filters.name: Parameterized LIP PLIP (Panetta 2008)
filters.note: Panetta, Wharton & Agaian PLIP model (IEEE TSMC-B, 2008/2011) on grey tones g = mu(M) - f with mu = M = 1: a (+) b = a+b-ab/gamma(M), a (-) b = k(M)(a-b)/(k(M)-b), c (x) a = gamma(M) - gamma(M)(1 - a/gamma(M))^c, gamma = k (default 1026/256 x M as recommended; gamma = k = M gives classic LIP). Scalar multiplication, and PLIP unsharp g (+) c (x) (g (-) Gaussian mean of g)
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p3));
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p3));

filters.name: Ratio of Low-Pass Pyramid Contrast (Toet 1989)
filters.note: Toet 1989 ratio-of-low-pass (contrast) pyramid R_k = G_k / G_(k+1), image = G_N x prod R_k; contrast enhancement by raising every ratio to a gain (R_k^g) and the base level about the image mean (base gain), applied to luma and transferred to RGB as a ratio. Approx.: undecimated Gaussian levels (sigma 1, 2, 4, 8 px) instead of REDUCE / EXPAND subsampling
passes: vec4 sg=vec4(1.,2.,4.,8.)*u_k;vec4 a=vec4(0.),w=vec4(0.);for(int i=-12;i<=12+int(u_p0*0.);i++){float t=float(i)/4.;float g=exp(-.5*t*t);for(int k=0;k<4;k++){a[k]+=g*luma(O(uv+vec2(t*sg[k],0.)*u_px).rgb);w[k]+=g;}}return a/w;

filters.name: Rational Unsharp Masking (Ramponi 1996)
filters.note: Ramponi & Polesel rational unsharp masking: y = x + lambda (z_x c(d_x) + z_y c(d_y)), z = 2x(n) - x(n-1) - x(n+1), edge sensor d = x(n-1) - x(n+1), rational control c(d) = d^2 / (k d^4 + h) with k = 1/(d1^2+d2^2), h = d1^2 d2^2/(d1^2+d2^2) (c is largest for medium edges between d1 and d2: low on noise, no overshoot on strong edges); per RGB channel

filters.name: PDE Inpainting (Harmonic / Oliveira / TV / CDD / Bertalmio)
filters.note: Iterative PDE inpainting inside the mask (boundary values fixed, lambda = 0 in the hole): Harmonic = Jacobi relaxation of the Laplace equation; Oliveira, Bowen, McKenna & Chang 2001 = repeated convolution with their diffusion kernel (diagonal a = .073235, axial b = .176765, centre 0); TV (Chan & Shen 2001) = lagged-diffusivity solve of div(grad u/|grad u|) = 0 (eps .01); CDD (Chan & Shen 2001) = div(g(|kappa|) grad u/|grad u|) with g(s) = s (+ .05 floor so flat starts diffuse), kappa = div(grad u/|grad u|); Bertalmio, Sapiro, Caselles & Ballester 2000 = transport u_t = grad(Lap u) . N with the slope-limited |grad u| of the paper, interleaved with diffusion. All start from an inverse-distance radial fill and run 24 sweeps on a coarse-to-fine stride schedule (16..1 px) instead of thousands of single-pixel iterations (approx.)
passes: vec4 t=T(uv);return int(u_p3+.5)==1?vec4(vec3(t.a),1.):vec4(t.rgb,1.);

filters.name: Kannala-Brandt Fisheye Model (2006)
filters.note: Kannala & Brandt 2006 generic fisheye model (as in Usenko et al. 2018): theta = atan2(r, z), d(theta) = theta + k1 theta^3 + k2 theta^5 (k3 = k4 = 0), pi(x) = f d(theta) x/r; unprojection by Newton on d(theta) = r_u. Pinhole to fisheye renders the image (taken as a pinhole view with the given horizontal FOV) through the model with the same focal length; fisheye to pinhole undistorts an image taken with the model (k1 = k2 = 0 is the equidistant lens)

filters.name: Unified Camera Model (Mei 2007)
filters.note: Unified camera model (Geyer-Daniilidis / Mei & Rives 2007) in the form of Usenko et al. 2018: pi(x) = f (x, y)/(xi d + z), d = |x|; unprojection ((xi + sqrt(1 + (1 - xi^2) r^2))/(1 + r^2)) (mx, my, 1) - (0, 0, xi), valid for r^2 <= 1/(xi^2 - 1) when xi > 1 and z > -w d; focal = pinhole focal x (1 + xi) x zoom so the image centre keeps its scale; xi = 0 is the pinhole, xi = 1 the parabolic catadioptric

filters.name: Double Sphere Camera Model (Usenko 2018)
filters.note: Double sphere model of Usenko, Demmel & Cremers 2018: d1 = |x|, d2 = |(x, y, xi d1 + z)|, pi(x) = f (x, y)/(alpha d2 + (1 - alpha)(xi d1 + z)); closed-form unprojection m_z = (1 - alpha^2 r^2)/(alpha sqrt(1 - (2 alpha - 1) r^2) + 1 - alpha), x = ((m_z xi + sqrt(m_z^2 + (1 - xi^2) r^2))/(m_z^2 + r^2)) (mx, my, m_z) - (0, 0, xi), with the paper's validity regions; model focal = pinhole focal x (1 + xi) so the image centre keeps its scale

filters.name: Field-of-View Lens Model (Devernay-Faugeras 2001)
filters.note: Devernay & Faugeras 2001 FOV distortion model (as in Usenko et al. 2018): r_d = atan2(2 r_u tan(omega/2), z)/omega, unprojection (m sin(r_d omega)/(2 r_d tan(omega/2)), cos(r_d omega)); omega is the field of view of the ideal fisheye lens; focal scaled by 2 tan(omega/2)/omega x zoom so the image centre keeps its scale

filters.name: Division Model Lens Distortion (Fitzgibbon 2001)
filters.note: Fitzgibbon 2001 one-parameter division model x_u = x_d/(1 + lambda r_d^2) (coordinates normalised to the half-diagonal): Undistort samples the distorted input at r_d = (1 - sqrt(1 - 4 lambda r_u^2))/(2 lambda r_u) (closed-form inverse); Distort renders x_d from the undistorted input. Negative lambda = barrel

filters.name: Underwater & Haze Priors (Median DCP, UDCP, Red Channel, MIP, ULAP)
filters.note: single-image restoration I = J t + A (1 - t), J = (I - A)/max(t, 0.1) + A; transmission smoothed by a joint bilateral pass instead of guided filter / soft matting; airlight from a 16x16 sample grid. Median DCP (Gibson, Vo & Nguyen 2012): dark channel = median (not minimum) of min_c I over the patch, gray A = max dark value, t = 1 - w dark / A. UDCP (Drews et al. 2013): dark channel of G and B only, A = pixel at the brightest G-B dark channel, t = 1 - w min_patch min(I_G/A_G, I_B/A_B). Red channel prior (Galdran et al. 2015): t = 1 - w min(min_patch (1-I_R)/(1-A_R), min_patch I_G/A_G, min_patch I_B/A_B), A = the sample with the lowest red among the 10% highest red-channel values (saturation term omitted). MIP (Carlevaris-Bianco, Mohan & Eustice 2010): D = max_patch R - max_patch max(G,B), t = D + 1 - max D, A = pixel of minimum t. ULAP (Song et al. 2018): relative depth d = 0.53214829 + 0.51309827 max(G,B) - 0.91066194 R stretched to 0..1, B = brightest of the farthest samples, d0 = 1 - max |B - I| / max(B, 1 - B), t_c = Nrer_c^(8 (d + d0)) with Nrer = 0.83 / 0.95 / 0.97 (reference implementation); Strength scales the haze term

filters.name: Night & Low-Light Priors (Maximum Reflectance, Bright Channel)

filters.name: Fusion Enhancement (Ancuti Underwater 2018, Ancuti Dehaze 2013, AMEF)
filters.note: image fusion with two-scale blending (Gaussian-smoothed normalised weights for the base layer, per-pixel weights for the detail layer) instead of the Laplacian pyramid, approx. Ancuti, Ancuti, De Vleeschouwer & Bekaert 2018: red compensation I_rc = I_r + (mean G - mean R)(1 - I_r) I_g, gray-world white balance; inputs = gamma-corrected (gamma 2) and sharpened (I + N(I - Gaussian(I)))/2 with N = min-max stretch; weights = Laplacian contrast + saliency (|Gaussian-blurred opponent colour - image mean|, Achanta-style) + saturation (std of R,G,B about luminance), (W + 0.1)/(sum W + 0.2). Ancuti & Ancuti 2013 dehazing: inputs = gray-world white-balanced image and gamma (I - mean luminance) with gamma = 2(0.5 + mean); weights = luminance (channel std), chromatic exp(-(S - 1)^2 / (2 0.3^2)), saliency (constants from memory, approx.). Galdran 2018 AMEF: exposures I^gamma for gamma = 1..5 (the per-channel CLAHE member is omitted), weight = |Laplacian of gray| x saturation (reference amef.m)

return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(u_p1));

filters.name: ICM / UCM Underwater Colour Correction (Iqbal)
filters.note: Iqbal et al. (as in the Wang et al. 2019 review reference code): ICM = per-channel min-max contrast stretch of R, G, B, then min-max stretch of HSV saturation and value. UCM = von Kries colour equalisation (R and G scaled to the blue mean), selective histogram stretching (R stretched toward the top, G both ways, B toward the bottom between its 0.2 % percentiles), then HSV saturation / value stretch; global extremes from a 16x16 sample grid instead of exact percentiles

filters.name: Skin Colour Models (Jones-Rehg GMM, Chai-Ngan YCbCr)
filters.note: Jones & Rehg 2002 (CRL 98/11 Table 5): 16-kernel diagonal-covariance Gaussian mixtures for skin and non-skin RGB (8-bit), pixel is skin when log P(rgb|skin) - log P(rgb|non-skin) > threshold (score = logistic of the margin). Chai & Ngan 1999 skin map: BT.601 Cb in [77,127] and Cr in [133,173]

filters.name: Local Thresholds (Eikvil, Kamel-Zhao, Parker)
filters.note: local document thresholds (b = dark print). Eikvil, Taxt & Moen 1991 (as described by Trier-Taxt / Blayvas 2006): Otsu on the large window L (sampled 15x15, 32 bins); if the class means differ by at least Threshold (paper 15/255) the pixel is thresholded by T, otherwise it joins the class whose mean is closest to its 3x3 mean (local class means stand in for the running updated means). Kamel & Zhao 1993 logical level technique: L(P) = ave(P) - g > T with ave the (2SW+1)^2 box mean (5x5 samples) at the 8 points P_i at distance SW; print iff L(P_i) and L(P_i+4) and L(P_i+1) and L(P_i+5) for some i = 0..3. Parker 1991 local intensity gradient (as in Yang & Yan 2000): d = min over 8 neighbours (f - f_i), local mean M and std S of d over the window, print where not (M >= -1 or S < 1) and d < M - S (8-bit units); the region-growing fill of object interiors is omitted, so mostly stroke borders are marked (approx.)

filters.name: Saliency Models (LC, Maximum Symmetric Surround, SUN, Self-Resemblance)
filters.note: saliency maps. LC (Zhai & Shah 2006): S(I_k) = sum over all pixels |I_k - I_i|, from a 64-bin luminance histogram of a 16x16 sample grid, min-max normalised. Maximum symmetric surround (Achanta & Susstrunk 2010): S = || mean CIELAB over the largest symmetric window centred at the pixel (half sizes min(x, w-x), min(y, h-y); 12x12 samples) - 3x3 binomial-blurred CIELAB ||. SUN (Zhang, Tong, Marks, Shan & Cottrell 2008) DoG version, approx.: DoG responses of intensity, R-G, B-Y at 3 scales, generalized-Gaussian fits per feature (shape from the moment ratio, scale from E|f|^theta) on a 6x6 sample grid of the image itself instead of a natural-image training set, log s = sum |f_i / sigma_i|^theta_i (minus its mean). Self-resemblance (Seo & Milanfar 2009), approx.: LARK kernels sqrt(det C) exp(-dx^T C dx) from the normalised local gradient covariance C over a 3x3 neighbourhood (one 9-D LARK vector per pixel instead of a 3x3 patch of them, no 64x64 downsampling), matrix cosine similarity rho to the 7x7 surround, S = 1 / sum exp((rho - 1) / 0.07^2)

filters.name: Recursive Bilateral Filter (Yang 2012)
filters.note: Yang 2012 recursive bilateral filter (as in the RecursiveBF reference code): first-order causal + anticausal recursions y_i = (1 - a) x_i + a R(i, i-1) y_(i-1), a = exp(-sqrt(2) / sigma_s), range weight exp(-(2|dR| + |dG| + |dB|)/4 / sigma_r) between successive pixels, the same recursion on a constant image gives the normalisation; horizontal then vertical, divided once at the end. Each recursion is evaluated in parallel as its truncated weighted sum (64 steps, step widened for large sigma), so it matches the sequential filter up to the truncation

filters.name: High-Dimensional Gaussian Filter (Permutohedral / Gaussian KD-tree target)
filters.note: the Gaussian filter in a high-dimensional feature space that the permutohedral lattice (Adams, Baek & Davis 2010) and the Gaussian KD-tree (Adams et al. 2009) accelerate, evaluated directly on sparse samples instead of through the lattice / tree: 5-D (x, y, r, g, b) Gaussian = colour bilateral filter (15x15 samples over 2 sigma), or the patch-space Gaussian = non-local means (3x3 patches, 7x7 search positions, Gaussian position term)

filters.name: Beltrami Flow (Sochen-Kimmel-Malladi)

filters.name: Alvarez-Mazorra Shock Filter

filters.name: Dual Rank Filter (HALCON dual_rank)

filters.name: LazPaint Textures (Plastik / Metal Floor / Snow Print / Round Stone)
filters.note: LazPaint ugraph.pas CreatePlastikTexture / CreateMetalFloorTexture / CreateSnowPrintTexture / CreateRoundStoneTexture: 6-octave cyclic Perlin map (32..1 px cells, exponent 1 or 1.2), the per-texture height remap (Plastik 3-segment curve + vertical motion blur of 1/6 image height + blur 2; Metal Floor = 100x50 tile of four ellipses + 14% noise; Snow Print = levels squeezed outside 50..80; Round Stone = blur 2) and BGRABitmap TPhongShading with each texture's light settings and colour; the value noise and normalisation are approx. (generates, ignores the image)

filters.name: Hypocycloid (LazPaint)
filters.note: LazPaint uhypocycloid.pas MakeHypocycloid: big circle R = 0.4 x min(width, height) centred, small circle r = R/cusps, point = (R-r)(cos t, sin t) + r(cos((R-r)t/r), -sin((R-r)t/r)), drawn as a closed red (CSS red) curve, pen width 3

filters.name: Angular Waves / Radial Waves (Pixelitor)
filters.note: Pixelitor AngularWavesFilter / RadialWavesFilter (CenteredTransformFilter, centre, zoom 100%, circle metric): Angular = angle += wave(dist / wavelength) x amount/100 rad; Radial = r += wave(angle x divisions) x amount/100 x r; wave types sine, sin-like sawtooth 2 mod(x/2pi,1)-1, sin-like triangle

filters.name: Radial Mosaic (Pixelitor)
filters.note: Pixelitor RadialMosaic: Voronoi of concentric seeds (centre + ring k at radius (k+1) x tile size with 6(k+1) points, odd rings rotated by pi/n when Offset, jitter up to 0.4 x spacing x randomness), each cell filled with the source colour at its seed, black cell edges of the given width (pinch/twist left at 0)

filters.name: Circle Weave (Pixelitor)
filters.note: Pixelitor CircleWeave (CurveFilter, white 2 px stroke on black, outer radius 0.45 x min side): Circle grid = circles centred between the N vertices and the centre (t = inner/2, radius x (1 + tuning sin)), Maurer rose r = R or inner R x sin(n k) at k = t (1+|tuning|) deg, Modular times table i -> (1+|tuning|) i mod N, Mystic rose = all chords (max 18 points; tuning curvature not drawn - straight chords)

filters.name: Flower of Life (Pixelitor)
filters.note: Pixelitor FlowerOfLife: overlapping circles of the given radius grown from the centre for N iterations on a triangular lattice (6 neighbours at distance r), square (4 neighbours at r sqrt2) or square-2 (diagonal neighbours); white strokes on black

filters.name: Brushed Metal (JH Labs / Pixelitor)
filters.note: JH Labs BrushedMetalFilter as used by Pixelitor: per-row uniform noise of +-amount around grey 128 plus shine x sin(pi x / width), clamped, then a horizontal box blur of radius Length along the rotated brush direction (more than 160 taps are strided)

filters.name: Spectral Colour Mixing (lygia mixSpectral / spectral.js)
filters.note: lygia color/mixSpectral (Ronald van Wijnen spectral.js, MIT): linear RGB -> 38-band reflectance from white/cyan/magenta/yellow/red/green/blue basis curves, concentrations (sqrt(Y) t)^2, Kubelka-Munk K/S mixing R = 1 + KS - sqrt(KS^2 + 2KS), back to XYZ (CIE 1931 weights) and linear sRGB; the image is mixed with a pigment colour (blue + yellow give green)

filters.name: Windmill Tile (lygia)
filters.note: lygia space/windmillTile: square tiles (sqTile = fract/floor), each rotated about its centre by (|x mod 2 - y mod 2| + 2 (y mod 2)) / 4 of a full turn (0, 90, 180, 270 deg pattern), lygia rotate2d; content = the tile's own piece of the image or the whole image per tile

filters.name: Colour Checker Chart (lygia)
filters.note: lygia draw/colorChecker: 6x4 patches at 80% of each cell (scale 1 x 1.5 about the centre), centre cross and corner brackets, colours from lygia color/palette/macbeth (24 sRGB patches) and palette/spyder (SpyderCheckr 48, sides A and B); drawn in a centred square

filters.name: Bracketing Flow-Aligned Texture (lygia / Bowles)
filters.note: lygia space/bracketing (Huw Bowles 2022): the flow direction (here the smoothed structure-tensor tangent of the image) is snapped to multiples of the bracket angle, the texture is sampled in the two bracketing UV frames and blended by the fractional angle, avoiding the swirl artefacts of per-pixel rotation; the hatch / brush textures are procedural

filters.name: Eye Spatial-Frequency Test Pattern (libvips eye)
filters.note: libvips vips_eye: v = y^2 cos(factor pi x^2 / (2 (width-1))) / (height-1)^2 - spatial frequency rising along x up to factor x Nyquist, amplitude rising down y; shown as 0.5 + 0.5 v (working-resolution pixels)

filters.name: Push-Pull Hole Filling (OpenImageIO fillholes_pushpull)
filters.note: OpenImageIO fillholes_pushpull: pull = successively halved, alpha-weighted (premultiplied) levels un-premultiplied wherever they have any coverage; push = each finer level composited over the upsampled coarser one, so holes take the colour of the nearest covered region at the finest scale that reaches them; here the 2^k levels are 8x8-tap windows evaluated per pixel (approx. of the decimated pyramid) and holes are taken from alpha, dark, bright or green-key pixels of an opaque image

filters.name: Image Encryption with Key (Plugin Galaxy Cryptology)
filters.note: approx. of the vendor description only (encrypt / decrypt an image with a 64-bit key): a self-inverse keyed cipher - pixels are swapped inside 64x64 blocks by XOR-ing their coordinates with a key-and-block hash, and each 8-bit channel is XOR-ed with a hash of the swapped pixel pair and the 63-bit key (3 x 21 bits); applying the same key again decrypts exactly at full resolution with 8-bit output

filters.name: Video-Synthesizer Patterns (Plugin Galaxy Synthesizer)
filters.note: approx. of the vendor description only (synthetic patterns like old video synthesizers): Sandin/Paik-style horizontal and vertical sine/square oscillators with cross- and luma-modulation (bars, moire rings, Lissajous plasma, luma-keyed colouriser), quantised to 7 levels and colourised by hue cycling

filters.name: SSIQ Spatial Derainbow (VapourSynth)
filters.note: dubhater vapoursynth-ssiq (port of the SSIQ AviSynth / VirtualDub plugin, after Graft's Smart Smoother): luma untouched, each chroma plane (BT.601 U, V) replaced by the rounded mean of the Diameter x Diameter neighbours within tolerance sqrt(floor(T^2/3)) of the centre, T = floor((Strength + 2) / 3) (8-bit units); computed at full resolution here instead of the plugin's 4:2:0 2x2 replication; interlaced option omitted

filters.name: EdgeFixer Border Line Repair (VapourSynth ContinuityFixer)
filters.note: sekrit-twc EdgeFixer ContinuityFixer: each of the outer N columns / rows (working-resolution pixels) is replaced by a*x + b, the least-squares fit (a = (n Sxy - Sx Sy) / (n Sxx - Sx^2 + eps), b = (Sy - a Sx) / n) of the line x against its inner neighbour y, per channel, over a window of +-Radius along the line (Radius 0 = whole line, 129 samples); lines repaired innermost first so each uses the already fixed neighbour (assumed order), left/right then top/bottom; one count per pair of opposite edges

filters.name: LGhost Ghost / Ringing Reduction (VapourSynth)
filters.note: HomeOfVapourSynthEvolution LGhost (one ghost term on luma, as the plugin processes only luma by default): Y += term x Intensity / 128 (arithmetic shift), term = Y[x-shift+1] - Y[x-shift] (edge), Y[x-shift] (luminance), or only the positive (rising) / negative (falling) part of that difference; horizontal shift in pixels; the luma change is added to R, G and B

filters.name: DCTFilter 8x8 DCT Frequency Suppressor (VapourSynth)
filters.note: HomeOfVapourSynthEvolution DCTFilter: per 8x8 block (working-resolution grid) orthonormal DCT, coefficient (u, v) multiplied by factor[u] x factor[v], inverse DCT; the 8 factors are grouped as 1 (DC, fixed), f1 f1, f2 f2, f3 f3, f4 to fit 4 controls; separable 4-pass DCT, coefficients carried in float textures (8-bit fallback GPUs lose precision)

filters.name: Binoculars View (VapourSynth vfx)
filters.note: V.C. Mohan vfx Binoculars (single frame of the start state): the disc of radius Radius x min(w, h) around the centre is magnified (offsets / mag) and drawn twice, as two touching discs centred at centre +- radius on the same row; everything else unchanged, no rim; bilinear instead of the plugin's 4-tap cubic

filters.name: Line Magnifier (VapourSynth vfx)
filters.note: V.C. Mohan vfx LineMagnifier (single frame): a strip Strip width x frame size wide starting at Position (from the left / top) shows the image magnified about its leading edge (offset / mag); drop mode uses a parabolic factor, mag / 2 at the strip centre and mag at its edges (profile reconstructed, approx.); bilinear instead of 4-tap cubic

filters.name: ColorTones Effect (Wolfram ImageEffect)
filters.note: Wolfram ImageEffect {"ColorTones", {col1, col2, ...}}: chromaticities of the colours mapped to increasing intensity - here each pixel keeps its CIE L* and takes the a*b* of the colour list interpolated at L* (colour space not stated in the docs, approx.); the first list is the documentation example, the others are sample lists; Chroma scales a*b*

filters.name: Hilbert / Differentiator Filter (Wolfram HilbertFilter, DifferentiatorFilter)
filters.note: Wolfram HilbertFilter / DifferentiatorFilter: FIR least-squares kernels with cutoff wc, h[k] = (1 - cos(wc k)) / (pi k) (Hilbert, 90 degree phase shift) and h[k] = (wc k cos(wc k) - sin(wc k)) / (pi k^2) (differentiator), h[0] = 0, odd length n, times a Hamming window (the docs only say a "suitable" default window, approx.), convolved with Fixed (clamped) padding; on an image Wolfram filters each dimension in turn (both axes), or one axis here; signed result shown as 0.5 + Gain x value, per channel

filters.name: FCC Lattice Palette Quantisation (FFmpeg latticepal)
filters.note: FFmpeg vf_latticepal (Niedermayer 2026): each RGB pixel scaled to Density lattice steps per axis and snapped to the nearest point of the FCC (D3 checkerboard: integer coordinates with even sum) lattice by the Conway-Sloane rule (round, and if the sum is odd re-round the coordinate with the largest error the other way, kept inside 0..N), output idx * 255 / N; ordered dither = 8x8 Bayer offsets of amplitude 2 / N with green shifted one column and blue rows flipped (approx. of the swscale 73-level matrix); the palette reduction to max_colors (whole-frame heap merging) and Floyd-Steinberg / blue-noise dithers are not included, so the output is exact only while the used lattice colours fit 256 (Density <= 7)

filters.name: Edge Slope Tracing Deinterlacer (FFmpeg estdif)
filters.note: FFmpeg vf_estdif (Paul B Mahol), one field of a still frame: every other row is rebuilt; for each candidate slope i in +-rslope the cost ecost x sum over +-redge of |prev[x+i+j] - next[x-i+j]| + |prev2[..] - prev[..]| + |next[..] - next2[..]| + mcost x (|p - m| + |n - m|) + dcost x |i| (ecost 2, mcost 1, dcost 1 defaults) picks the edge slope k, then 2-point (prev[x+k] + next[x-k]) / 2, 4-point (9, -1)/16 or 6-point (20, -5, 1)/32 interpolation along it; slope chosen on luma for all channels and searched around zero for every pixel (FFmpeg carries k along the row - sequential, approx.)

filters.name: Tetrahedral Colour Mixer (OBS shaderfilter tetra)
filters.note: obs-shaderfilter examples/tetra.shader: tetrahedral interpolation of the RGB cube - the input is located in one of the six tetrahedra by sorting r, g, b and output as the weighted sum of its corners (black fixed at 0, white fixed at 1, the six primary / secondary corners user colours); the shader has 18 sliders (3 per corner), here one corner is edited at a time and the others stay at their identity colours

filters.name: Bizarro-Negation (Paint.NET)
filters.note: Xhin Bizarro-Negation (Plugin Index description): the layer is duplicated, flipped horizontally and vertically, and composited with the Paint.NET Negation blend mode, result = 1 - |1 - A - B|; Flip offers one axis only, Mix = layer opacity

filters.name: Overliner (Paint.NET)
filters.note: MadJik Overliner, approx. from the Plugin Index description: each pixel is compared with its neighbour (right and / or below, at Distance); where the step exceeds Threshold the pixel is a colour break and is painted with the light colour (white) if the break goes from dark to light, otherwise with the dark colour (black); other pixels keep the image (or grey)

filters.name: Lattice (Paint.NET Ed Harvey)

filters.name: Cuboids (Paint.NET)
filters.note: Red Ochre Cuboids, approx. from the Plugin Index description: the image is cut into square cells, each extruded as a block toward a one-point-perspective viewer above the centre (top face scaled by 1 + Perspective x height about the vanishing point, analytic ray / frustum test over the neighbouring cells, nearest top wins); Perspective 0 = plain pixelation, larger values = tower blocks; sides darkened toward their base

filters.name: Gradient Blocks (Paint.NET)
filters.note: pyrochild Gradient Blocks, approx. from the Plugin Index description ("pixelated version with gradient filled blocks"): each block is filled with a gradient between the means of its four quarters (bilinear between the quarter centres, or horizontal / vertical / diagonal two-colour gradients)

filters.name: Tattersall (Paint.NET toe_head2001)

filters.name: Koch Snowflake (Paint.NET)

filters.name: Fibonacci Fill (Paint.NET)

filters.name: Varicose / Turbulent Circles (Paint.NET)

filters.note: Filter Forge library texture, approx. procedural re-creation from the library preview and name (Filter Forge publishes no source): Barbed Wire Fence = rows of twisted two-strand wire with four-point barbs and coils, galvanised with rust (Variation = rust) against a grey sky; Chain Mail (Maille Maker) = European 4-in-1 rings on offset rows, alternate rows tilted so rings interlock (Variation = wire gauge); Chicken Wire = hexagonal netting with twisted vertical pairs over grass (Variation = gauge); Expanded Metal Floor = diamond openings in a diagonal lattice with inclined strands (Variation = opening size); Pegboard = hardboard with round holes (Variation = hole size); Speaker Grill = hex-perforated black plate over cloth (Variation = hole size); Knurling = diamond-knurl pyramids on brushed steel (Variation = sharpness); Diamond tread plate = raised lozenges alternating +/-45 deg on brushed aluminium (Variation = lozenge width); height field lit from the upper left (normal from the pixel and its +x/+y neighbours), Variation = style-specific shape / wear amount, Output = material colours, its luminance tinted by the input image, or the relief and part of the material laid over the image; seeded; wire styles use their wire mask as coverage

filters.name: Filter Forge Techno Textures (Carbon Fiber / Greebles / Spaceship Hull Plates)
filters.note: Filter Forge library texture, approx. procedural re-creation from the library preview and name (Filter Forge publishes no source): Carbon Fiber = 2/2 twill (Variation < 0.5) or plain weave of tows with fibre streaks, anisotropic sheen (warp/weft tows lit differently) and clear-coat gloss; Greebles = quadtree-split panels (up to 3 levels, Variation = split rate) at random heights with bevels and vents / knobs / studs / recesses, rare accent panels; Spaceship Hull Plates = staggered 2:1 plates with seams, rivet rows, slight bulge, paint variation and streaky grime (Variation = grime); height field lit from the upper left (normal from the pixel and its +x/+y neighbours), Variation = style-specific shape / wear amount, Output = material colours, its luminance tinted by the input image, or the relief and part of the material laid over the image; seeded

filters.name: Filter Forge Fibre Textures (Berber Carpet / Cardboard / Tatami Mat / Woven Wicker)
filters.note: Filter Forge library texture, approx. procedural re-creation from the library preview and name (Filter Forge publishes no source): Berber Carpet = offset rows of looped-pile tufts with ply twist, oatmeal yarn with dark berber flecks (Variation = fleck amount); Cardboard = kraft brown fibres, mottling, soft creases and corrugation ridges showing through (Variation = corrugation); Tatami Mat = staggered 2:1 mats of igusa rush straws with warp grooves and dark heri borders (Variation = straw green-ness); Woven Wicker = round weavers passing over / under upright stakes in alternate rows (Variation = weaver fullness); height field lit from the upper left (normal from the pixel and its +x/+y neighbours), Variation = style-specific shape / wear amount, Output = material colours, its luminance tinted by the input image, or the relief and part of the material laid over the image; seeded

filters.name: Filter Forge Building Textures (Asphalt / Roof Shingles / Cinder Blocks / Flagstones / Terrazzo / Wattle and Daub)
filters.note: Filter Forge library texture, approx. procedural re-creation from the library preview and name (Filter Forge publishes no source): Asphalt road = Voronoi aggregate stones in dark binder, fine grit, wear exposing lighter stones and cracks (Variation = wear); Asphalt Roof Shingles = 3-tab shingle rows offset by half a tab, cut-out slots, butt-edge shadow and granule speckle (Variation = tab colour mix); Cinder Blocks = 2:1 running-bond concrete masonry units with mortar joints and porous pits (Variation = pit density); Flagstones = warped irregular Voronoi stones in slate / sandstone / red tones with soil-and-moss joints (Variation = joint width); Terrazzo Tiles = two sizes of angular chips (shrunk Voronoi cells) in white / black / grey / terracotta / green over cement, polished (Variation = chip density); Wattle and Daub = clay daub with straw and cracks over woven wattle that shows through where it has fallen away (Variation = loss); height field lit from the upper left (normal from the pixel and its +x/+y neighbours), Variation = style-specific shape / wear amount, Output = material colours, its luminance tinted by the input image, or the relief and part of the material laid over the image; seeded

filters.name: Filter Forge Stone Textures (Dry Lakebed / Malachite / Geode / Lichen Stone / Stalactite Cave / Travertine / Widmanstatten)
filters.note: Filter Forge library texture, approx. procedural re-creation from the library preview and name (Filter Forge publishes no source): Dry Lakebed = warped Voronoi mud plates curling up at the crack edges plus fine secondary cracks (Variation = crack width); Malachite = concentric light / dark green bands around warped botryoidal centres, polished (Variation = band density); Geode = one cut geode per cell: host rock, white rind, blue-violet agate banding and a faceted crystal cavity (Variation = amethyst to clear quartz); Lichen Covered Stone = grey granite with yellow-green / orange / grey-green rosette lichen patches (Variation = coverage); Stalactite Cave = three depth layers of tapering stalactites and stalagmites with flowstone ripples between rock ceiling and floor bands (Variation = stalactite length); Travertine = cream / tan banded stone with horizontally elongated voids (Variation = void amount); Widmanstatten = etched meteoritic iron: interrupted kamacite lamellae in three directions 60 deg apart with orientation-dependent sheen, bright taenite rims and dark plessite fill (Variation = lamella length); height field lit from the upper left (normal from the pixel and its +x/+y neighbours), Variation = style-specific shape / wear amount, Output = material colours, its luminance tinted by the input image, or the relief and part of the material laid over the image; seeded

filters.name: Filter Forge Generated Textures

filters.name: Border Dispersion (Fred bordereffects)
filters.note: Fred Weinhaus bordereffects: white rectangle with a black border of size+pad (pad 2) displaced by a random map v: sample at (x + size sin(2 pi density v), y + size cos(2 pi density v)), image shown where the displaced mask is white, background colour elsewhere; v = per-pixel random noise (curviness 0) or blurred, contrast-stretched noise (approx. value noise of matching scale)

filters.name: Film Perforations Border (Fred perforations)
filters.note: Fred Weinhaus perforations (black border): hole height = size% of the smaller dimension, width = ratio x height, rounded rectangle centred in cells of floor(W/number) x 2 height, tiled along the two long sides (or chosen pair), black band with white holes; approx.: ratio (Hole aspect) and corner factor 0.15 are not stated on the page, aged/faded borders omitted

filters.name: Random Colour Cells (Fred colorcells)
filters.note: Fred Weinhaus colorcells: image split into numx x numy cells; per cell rr = random, factor = rr if rr > (100-percent)/100 else 0, -modulate 100,100,(100 + factor x random x 200) (HSL hue shift up to 360 deg); cells touching the elliptical mask (diameters % of image) only; optional white grid lines

filters.name: Hexagons of Rotated Input (Fred hexagons)
filters.note: Fred Weinhaus hexagons: centre-cropped square of the input scaled to ~sqrt(2) x cell size, rotated by a random angle per cell and masked into a hexagonal tiling, optional coloured hexagon edges; approx.: flat-top hexagon orientation assumed

filters.name: Polygon Ring (Fred polyring)
filters.note: Fred Weinhaus polyring (polygon format): N copies, angle step 360/N, ring radius = h/2 + w/(2 tan(angle/2)), copy i placed at radius x (cos, sin)(i x angle) and rotated by i x angle + 90 deg (-distort SRT) so the bottoms meet, merged over the background and fitted to the frame; ring format omitted

filters.name: Primary RGB Dots (Fred rgbdots)

filters.note: Fred Weinhaus warplog: -fx v.p{exp(ln(v.w) i/(w-1))-1, j} - output column i samples source x = W_in^(i/(W_out-1)) - 1 (and likewise rows), virtual pixels black; output size = factor x input, letterboxed into the frame

filters.note: Fred Weinhaus 3Dcover: the left (or right, negative angle) side-size strip becomes the spine and the rest the front face of a box rotated about the vertical axis and viewed in perspective (exaggeration factor), fitted to the frame over the background; approx.: ray-cast box replaces the 3Drotate script, vignette/join line/shadow options omitted

filters.name: Wood Brand Burn (Fred woodbrand)
filters.note: Fred Weinhaus woodbrand: brand mask blurred, -auto-level, -level 50x100%, -motion-blur 0xM-135, multiplied by the mask, darkens the HSB-brightness-modulated wood inside the brand (darker toward the edges); approx.: single-image version - the brand is the thresholded input and the wood grain is procedural (the script takes a second wood image)
passes: float m=step(.5,luma(O(uv).rgb));m=u_p3<.5?1.-m:m;return vec4(vec3(m),1.);

filters.name: Filter Forge Textures (Iris / Swiss Cheese / Ceiling Tile / Tactile Paving / Solar Panels / Manhole / Petri Dish)
filters.note: approx. procedural re-creations of Filter Forge library textures (Organic / Techno / Building categories): iris (radial fibres, collarette, crypts, limbal ring, veined sclera), Swiss cheese (random spherical holes), acoustic ceiling tile (T-bar grid, fissures, pinholes, stains), tactile warning paving (truncated domes), solar panels (6x10 cells, busbars, frame), manhole cover (frame, diamond lugs, rust), agar plate petri dish (amber or blood agar, domed colonies); height-field lit; Wear = dirt, rust, hole/colony density; seeded

filters.name: Telecine Net Silk (Magic Bullet Looks)
filters.note: Magic Bullet Looks Telecine Net: silk net in the telecine softens the blacks - light from the surroundings (Gaussian, net Size) bleeds into the shadows plus a slight veil and overall softening, scaled by Strength, Exposure Compensation in stops; approx. (Maxon help gives only the parameter meanings)
passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p0));

filters.name: Shutter Streak (Magic Bullet Looks)
filters.note: Magic Bullet Looks Shutter Streak: misaligned film gate lets light leak into the top and bottom of the frame - each column's highlight energy is smeared from the top and bottom edges toward the middle (Size = reach toward the midpoint, Boost = exposure of the streak in stops, Falloff = softness toward the centre); approx.
passes: vec3 acc=vec3(0.);for(int i=0;i<48+int(u_p0*0.);i++){vec3 s=O(vec2(uv.x,(float(i)+.5)/48.)).rgb;acc+=max(s-.55,0.)*2.2;}return vec4(acc/48.,1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(3.));

vec3 x=O(uv).rgb;float e=abs(2.*uv.y-1.);float sz=max(u_p0/100.,.01);float w=clamp((e-(1.-sz))/sz,0.,1.);w=pow(w,exp2(u_p2*1.5)*1.2);vec3 st=T(uv).rgb*w*exp2(u_p1)*1.6;return vec4(clamp(x+st*(1.-x*.5),0.,1.),1.);

filters.name: Haze / Flare Uncoated Lens (Magic Bullet Looks)
filters.note: Magic Bullet Looks Haze/Flare: light from the image (Spillage: frame edges only at low values, nearly the whole image at high values) spreads horizontally (Reach) with Softness blur, added at Exposure (stops) plus a tinted reflection mirrored through the centre at higher exposure; approx.: matte box options omitted
passes: vec3 x=O(uv).rgb;vec2 q=abs(uv*2.-1.);float ed=max(q.x,q.y);float sp=u_p0/100.;float m=smoothstep(1.-sp-.1,1.-sp+.25,ed)+sp*sp*.5;return vec4(x*x*clamp(m,0.,1.),1.);
float r=R(4.+u_p2/100.*u_res.x/u_k*.5);vec4 a=blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),r);vec4 b=blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),r*.25);return vec4(a.rgb*.6+b.rgb*.4,1.);
return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(0.,1.),R(1.+u_p1*.4));

filters.name: Huenity Hue Unification (Magic Bullet Looks)

filters.name: Advect along Guide (Matchbox Ls_Advect)
filters.note: Lewis Saunders Ls_Advect (lcrs/matchboxes): pass 1 turns a guide into vectors (3x3 Sobel of the guide, rotated 90 deg unless radial), pass 2 walks each pixel along the field and takes the colour at the end of the walk. Here the guide is the image itself (blurred luma) and the vectors are unit directions with soft magnitude (approx.; the Matchbox scales raw gradients by 32/ksize and averages an oversample grid)

filters.name: Spline Blur along Contours (Matchbox Ls_Splineblur)
filters.note: Lewis Saunders Ls_Splineblur (lcrs/matchboxes): pass 1 = Sobel vector field of the guide (rotated 90 deg so it runs along contours, or radial), pass 2 averages Samples points spaced Length/(Samples-1) either traced forward and backward along the streamline (re-reading the field at each step) or on a straight segment along the centre vector. Guide = the image (pre-blurred luma); field directions normalised with soft magnitude so flat areas stay sharp (approx. magnitude scaling)

filters.name: Exponential Blur (Matchbox crok_expon_blur)
filters.note: crok_expon_blur (Ivar Beer, code by Miles and Lewis): blur with an exponential falloff exp(-|d|/Amount), independent X and Y amounts, applied separably (so the 2-D kernel is exp(-(|dx|/ax+|dy|/ay))), Blend mixes with the original; kernel out to 6 x Amount (approx.: erode for negative amounts, gamma and half-res options omitted)

filters.name: Airglow (Matchbox Ls_Airglow)
filters.note: Lewis Saunders Ls_Airglow (lcrs/matchboxes): air-scatter glow = weighted sum of 8 Gaussian blurs whose size doubles per level (largest sigma = Size), computed in linear light and added back onto the image; level weights follow Falloff^k from the smallest blur (the Matchbox draws them from a UI curve; >1 favours the wide blurs). filters.name: Random Grade (Matchbox Ls_RndmGrade)
filters.note: Lewis Saunders Ls_RndmGrade (lcrs/matchboxes): seeded random grade = random cross-channel bleed matrix weighted by saturation (greys untouched), then a random spline curve per channel with ends locked to 0 and 1; Colourfulness blends between the per-channel curves and their common average shift (less colour cast). passes: return blur1d(u_tex,uv,vec2(1.,0.),R(u_p3));

filters.note: nob_trigrade (nobbl211, MIT) with one active Colour-mode vector: the linear colour matrix M = I + (t - s) s^T / (s.s) maps the source colour s exactly to the target t and leaves the colour space orthogonal to s unchanged; target luminance normalised to the source (on by default, Rec.709 luma here instead of ACEScg). filters.name: Reverse Grade (Matchbox AFX_ReverseGrade)
filters.note: AFX_ReverseGrade (John Ashby) = the reverse mode of the Nuke Grade node: forward grade y = A x + B with A = (gain - lift)/(whitepoint - blackpoint), B = lift - A blackpoint (multiply 1, offset 0, gamma 1); reverse x = (y - B)/A maps lift back to blackpoint and gain back to whitepoint, used to match one plate to another. filters.note: AA_Multiband_ColorCorrect (Anthony Augusta): Master plus five fixed luminance bands (Low, Low Mid, Mid, High Mid, High), each with its own colour wheel (hue + gain) and exposure; one band at a time here. filters.name: Rift Side-by-Side Barrel Warp (Matchbox crok_rift)
filters.note: crok_rift (Lewis Saunders and Ivar Beer, after Lubosz 2013 GStreamer Oculus viewer): each half of a side-by-side frame is warped about its lens centre with the Oculus SDK distortion r * (k0 + k1 r^2 + k2 r^4), k = (1, .22, .24) at Distortion .5, ScaleIn (2, 2/aspect), output scale 1/Scale; Mono duplicates one image into both eyes. filters.name: Hex-Tiling Repetition-Free Texture (Matchbox crok_tile)
filters.note: crok_tile (Ivar Beer, after Suslik shadertoy tsVGRd, hex tiling by Shane): the image is used as a texture and re-tiled without visible repetition: every vertex of a triangular lattice (= hex-cell centre) gets a random offset and rotation, each pixel blends the three surrounding cells with barycentric weights sharpened by 1/Blend. filters.name: Social Safe Zones (Matchbox BB_SocialSafeZones)
filters.note: BB_SocialSafeZones (BayleyBY, CC BY-SA 4.0): unsafe margins (top/bottom/left/right % of frame) from its README table - Reels 14/35/6/6, Meta Feed 1:1 12.5/12.5/2.5/2.5, 4:5 10/10/2.5/2.5, Stories 14/20/6/6, TikTok 13/21/5.6/5.6, YouTube DemandGen 3.5/35.8/2/8.4, Shorts 15/35/4.4/17.8 - filled red outside a 20 px rounded safe box, with border; cutouts: Reels right 21% x lower 60%, TikTok right 14.8% x lower 44.8%, DemandGen top corners 496x183 / 475x133 of 1920x1080. filters.name: Vanishing-Point Line Fan (Matchbox BB_PerspectiveLines)

filters.name: Camera Flashes (Matchbox crok_cameraflash)

filters.name: Ancient Symbols (Matchbox crok_ancient_symbols)
